issues.title: Add option to limit st.cache size by memory footprint rather than total number of entries
issues.body:
### Problem

The ability to limit the size of the cache was added by https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/1152 which is extremely useful when deploying a streamlit app to a remote server to prevent a memory leak, however it leaves the question as to what value `max_entries` should be set to.  For example, if my remote server has 1GB of memory and I'd like to allocate 500MB of it for the purposes of caching responses, what values of `max_entries` should I set for each of the functions I am caching to ensure I don't exceed that memory limit?  As of right now the only way to determine it is through trial and error.

### Solution

**MVP:** One solution would be to add another parameter to the `st.cache` function like `max_memory_footprint` to limit the size of the cache by memory rather than number of entries.

**Possible additions:** An addition to this would be a global parameter like `maxCacheSize` in the `config.toml` file, this would be more convenient than limiting memory footprint by function as it may be difficult to determine what the optimal allocation per function would be in the case that you are caching multiple functions. 

**Preferred solution:** The preferred solution would probably be both options, a global memory limit that can be set to prevent the application from running out of memory, and a per-function memory limit for finer control when necessary. 

Thank you!

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

**If you'd like the Streamlit team to prioritize this feature request, please use the 👍 (thumbs up emoji) reaction in response to the initial post.**

issues.title: Using st.data_editor with session state, input data "disappears": Requires double input to register changes.
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

This issue is practically the same as this closed issue: #7354
But since it is closed (due to the user not really needing the particular use case) I have opened this new one with another simple minimum reproducible example.

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-7749)

```Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# using session state, works ever other input:
if "df" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.df = pd.DataFrame({"In":[0,1,2],"Out":[0,0,0]})
st.session_state.df = st.data_editor(st.session_state.df)
st.session_state.df["Out"] = st.session_state.df["In"]**2
st.write(st.session_state.df)

# # works every input but the df is not updated in data_editor:
# df = pd.DataFrame({"In":[0,1,2],"Out":[0,0,0]})
# df = st.data_editor(df)
# df["Out"] = df["In"]**2
# st.write(df)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click on a field in the in column.
2. Input a number, enter.
3. Watch for changes in the dataframes.

### Expected Behavior

I expect that each input in the data_editor to result in the rest of the code to run, before it loops back to the top and into the data_editor with new data which is displayed.
In this example I expect the "state" version to behave just like the "non-state" example, with the added functionality of the state of course.

### Current Behavior

1. I input a number(say 5) in a input field press enter.
2. This new input is replaced with the previous value instantly.
3. I input 5 in the same box again.
4. The edit_data frame now has the correct input, but not the updated input. The st.write frame is updated to reflect the correct values.

Another variant:
1. I input 5 in row 1. -> instantly replaced, nothing in st.write
2. I input 4 in row 2. -> editor: input is updated, output is not. st.write: row two is updated.
3. I input 3 in row 3. -> editor: row 2 is updated, row 3 ignored. Both editor and write now agrees.
OR: in another box I input a changed number (not the same as exists already, that doesnt do anything)

Pretty hard to explain, please try for yourself to get an idea how it really behaves.
Basically the state of data_editor is always one loop behind in updating, and the input seems to dissapear until another change is made.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.28.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Win 10
- Browser: Edge or Firefox


### Additional Information

[See my earlier comment on the other issue: ](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7354#issuecomment-1823470192)
Similar problem from the docs, with an incompatible solution: [Widget updating session_state problem](https://docs.streamlit.io/knowledge-base/using-streamlit/widget-updating-session-state)

Please help me with workarounds if possible.
Thank you for considering this issue, and for Streamlit itself!

issues.title: Add form validation to make form fields required
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit currently has no built-in form validation to prevent a form from being submitted when one or more of he required fields is not populated or has invalid data. Adding a manual check that gets executed on form submit button click is not ideal from a user experience point of view, because this means either the entire form will be cleared even when a required field is not correctly populated when the form's clear_on_submit property is set as True, or the form fields will still carry the entered values even when the form is successfully submitted if the form's clear_on_submit property is set as False.

### Why?

If a form is submitted with all necessary fields populated, ideally I would want the form to be cleared upon submission and hence would want clear_on_submit set to True. When, however, a necessary field is left empty I would indeed want the already populated fields to retain the provided input rather than being cleared.

I could not make things work with a form but wrote a workaround that does not use a form as follows: I created input fields (not inside a form), created state vars assigned to keys of input fields, added a standard button, created a function to reset the state variables to be called from within the on_click function of the button only when all compulsory fields are populated.

However, I do think this is way too much work for a simple form validation, which is pretty fundamental feature built into any web framework that I’ve ever worked with (I do recognise that Streamlit probably does not aim to become an all-purpose web framework but still), and in my humble opinion, make it difficult for Streamlit to be adopted by a wider user base.

### How?

Adding a `required` property to form input fields might be a possible solution. 

### Additional Context

This issue was discussed at [https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/make-input-fields-required-using-st-form/30822](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/make-input-fields-required-using-st-form/30822)

issues.title: Add `dataframeHeaderTextColor` theme option for dataframe header text
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `dataframeHeaderTextColor` theme option to control the foreground (text) color of `st.dataframe` / `st.data_editor` column headers. Today `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor` exists, but the header text color can't be customized — it's always derived from the body `textColor` (as `fadedText60`), so a custom/tinted/dark header background often results in weak or unreadable header text.

### Why?

Users can already set a custom header background via `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`, but there's no matching control for the header text. With a dark or strongly tinted header background, the faded, body-derived header text has poor contrast and can be hard to read. A dedicated `dataframeHeaderTextColor` lets the header background and foreground be styled together for a readable, on-brand look.

### How?

Add a theme config option, e.g.:

```toml
[theme]
dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor = "#1f2937"
dataframeHeaderTextColor = "#ffffff"
```

Implementation notes:
- Wire it through the dataframe's custom theme so it overrides the header text color instead of the hardcoded default.
- In the frontend this currently maps to the glide-data-grid `textHeader` (and likely `textGroupHeader`), which today is set to `theme.colors.fadedText60`:

```117:119:frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/DataFrame/hooks/useCustomTheme.ts
      textHeader: theme.colors.fadedText60,
      textHeaderSelected: theme.colors.white,
      textGroupHeader: theme.colors.fadedText60,
```

- If unset, fall back to today's derived default (so nothing changes for existing apps).

### Additional Context

- Complements the existing `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor` theme option.
- Related: #6958 (keep header style), #6340 (style tables)

issues.title: New component: `st.drawer` as a dismissable container
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit has expanded its layout options, which compound on each others to create complex application user flows beyond the single page, top to bottom interaction. 

As `st.dialog` is coming along, and `st.popover` merged, most types of surfaces are being covered by streamlit, except the drawer concept, which is a dismissable container sliding from the right of the screen on demand, which blocks the screen from the side without masking the context, can be used as an information surface, for continuous interactions (like LLM Chat), or for form input. 

### Why?

`st.sidebar`, which is the current closest equivalent has been very useful to have a permanent set of widget independent of the main window context but fall short when

- The interface has to be conditional, it requires more `session_state `trickery to redraw the sidebar
- The navigation gets rich, and the sidebar should have only a few other static elements but not a full form entry / sub interface

Thus, the sidebar and drawer concepts may overlap for simple usage, but are very different in practice and we would beneficiate from a better separation of duty 

Gitlab makes a good example of using a rich navigation sidebar to the left hand side, and drawers for Gitlab Duo AI Chat, or to input CI Variables

![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/97103608/3c830664-12c6-4b8a-8e91-8192c326a05d)

![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/97103608/5bd212a0-f31a-4f73-b4f4-3fca85374585)


### How?

The [Base Web](https://baseweb.design/components/drawer/) component is a starting point.

The main behaviours between the background and drawer I can refine in a first round are : 

- _Focused_ : The background is frozen, the user must exit using a default exit button. Clicking on the background does not exit the drawer (as it leads to different input errors). A drawer is always exitable. The background gets slightly greyed out, to ensure the drawer is in focus but remains readable
- _Scrollable_ : The background can be scrolled. This ensures that the user can retain a mental image of where they are in the UX Flow of the app.
- _Form Like (Optional)_ : The developer should be able to set a condition which closes the drawer, similar to how `st.form_submit_button` allows to exit the form. Perhaps we could reuse behaviours, and a form could be nested within a drawer, upon submission it closes the drawer.

With only those basic behaviour we can address most use cases:

1. A one-shot configuration (i.e. use a drawer to make a request, drawer closes and request shows up in main app area)
2. A continuous data entry, where the drawer remains open whilst the user makes several input (i.e. add multiple records)
3. An information/documentation panel with little interactions, but potentially rich display elements
4. A chat like interface on demand, a la copilot or gitlab duo chat.

On the python end, `st.drawer` should be similar syntaxically to st.dialog and st.popover to ease on the cognitive load, meaning

```python
with st.drawer("Open Drawer"):
   ...

```

Should call the drawer to expand, clicking away or on a well visible close/exit button should close the drawer.

### Additional Context

_No response_

issues.title: AppTest drops page-persistent widget state on a same-page rerun
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

AppTest loses a conditional text input's value when it is hidden and shown again with `persist_state="page"`, although the test never switches pages. The same sequence retains the value in a browser, and `persist_state="session"` works in AppTest.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

at = AppTest.from_string("""
import streamlit as st

if st.toggle("Show", key="show"):
    st.text_input("SKU", key="sku", persist_state="page")
""").run()

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
at.text_input[0].set_value("SKU-42").run()
at.toggle[0].set_value(False).run()
print("While hidden:", repr(at.session_state["sku"]))
assert at.session_state["sku"] == "SKU-42"

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
print("After showing again:", repr(at.text_input[0].value))
assert not at.exception
assert at.text_input[0].value == "SKU-42"  # Fails: actual value is "".
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install Streamlit 1.65.0 in a normal Python environment: `pip install streamlit==1.65.0`.
2. Save the example as `repro_page_persistence.py` and run `python repro_page_persistence.py`. Pytest is not required.
3. Observe that the hidden value is still `SKU-42`, but the final input value is empty and the final assertion fails.
4. Change `persist_state="page"` to `persist_state="session"` and run again. The value remains `SKU-42` and the assertion passes.
5. For a browser comparison, save only the app string as `app.py`, run `streamlit run app.py`, enable Show, enter `SKU-42` and press Enter, then disable and re-enable Show. The browser retains the input value.

### Expected Behavior

Page-scoped persistence should keep the value through the hide/show sequence in AppTest because the test remains on the same page. It should return `SKU-42` after the input is shown again, matching the browser.

### Current Behavior

Reproduced on both Streamlit 1.64.0 and 1.65.0:

```text
While hidden: 'SKU-42'
After showing again: ''
AssertionError
```

There are no application exceptions in `at.exception`; the failure is the final test assertion. A browser comparison on both versions retains `SKU-42`. AppTest's `persist_state="session"` control also retains it; the default `persist_state=None` control resets it as expected.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

A previously working version has not been established. The versions tested are 1.64.0 and 1.65.0.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0; also reproduced on 1.64.0.
- Python version: 3.14.8.
- Operating System: macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- Browser: Not required for the AppTest reproduction. Browser comparisons used the Codex in-app browser on macOS.
- Package integrity: The tested Streamlit Python files match their wheel RECORD hashes. No installed Streamlit source was modified.

### Additional Information

#### Related issues checked

- [#17119](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17119) concerns the remount of a `persist_state=None` widget and a backend/frontend mismatch. This reproduction uses explicit page persistence and works in a browser.
- [#17093](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17093) concerns a delayed first mount after a session-state value was set. Here, the widget was mounted, edited, hidden, and remounted.
- [#16611](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16611) concerns `AppTest.switch_page()` with a custom `url_path`. This example has no page switch or custom URL path.
- [#9128](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9128) and [#12566](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12566) report KeyErrors with changing widget trees. This example has no script exception and loses a page-persistent value.

I did not find an existing issue with this same reproduction.

#### Possible cause

AppTest creates a fresh PagesManager for each run. Its current page hash initially equals `""`. ScriptRunner interprets the mismatch with the target page hash as a page change and performs cleanup before resetting the context, so page-scoped persistence can be evaluated against the empty current hash.

Source links are pinned to the inspected develop commit `ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e`:

- [AppTest creates PagesManager](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py#L506).
- [PagesManager initializes an empty current page hash](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/pages_manager.py#L50).
- [ScriptRunner performs page-change cleanup before context reset](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py#L660).

In a separate single-page diagnostic on both released versions, seeding the reconstructed runner's current page hash with the main page hash before cleanup makes this reproduction pass. It also prevents a keyed stateful tab from resetting after a child-widget interaction in AppTest. This diagnostic is evidence about the cleanup path; a complete fix must still handle real page switches correctly. The develop source was inspected, not executed.

issues.title: Button in horizontal container shows native browser title tooltip even when the label is not truncated
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Starting with Streamlit 1.62.0, a button inside **st.container(horizontal=True)** (or placed directly in a column) gets an HTML **title** attribute on its label when **help** is not set. Hovering the label then shows the browser's native tooltip.

According to the **wrap** docstring, this is meant to "reveal the full label" when it's truncated with an ellipsis. However, the **title** is added even when the label fits and nothing is truncated. The result is an unexpected, unstyled tooltip on every short button in a horizontal layout. It also looks inconsistent next to Streamlit's own **help** tooltip, which has a different style and position.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

LONG_LABEL = "This is a very long button label " * 6

# 1. Unexpected: native tooltip although the label is not truncated
with st.container(horizontal=True):
    st.button("Short label")

# 2. Truncated label: here the native tooltip is useful
with st.container(horizontal=True):
    st.button(LONG_LABEL)

# 3. wrap=True: label wraps, no native tooltip
with st.container(horizontal=True):
    st.button(LONG_LABEL, wrap=True, key="wrapped")

# 4. Vertical container: no native tooltip
with st.container(horizontal=False):
    st.button("Short label", key="vertical")

# 5. help set: Streamlit tooltip only
st.button("With help", help="This is a button with a tooltip")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above with **streamlit run app.py**.
2. Hover the mouse over the text of the first button ("Short label") and wait about one second.

### Expected Behavior

No tooltip should appear, because the label is fully visible and **help** is not set. The native **title** tooltip should appear only when the label is actually truncated, as in case 2.

### Current Behavior

The browser's native tooltip (rectangular, below and to the right of the cursor) shows the label text even though nothing is truncated. The button in the vertical container (case 4) does not show it.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0 (also reproduced on 1.62.0)
- Python version: 3.12.8
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: Chrome 154.0.8037.95 (64-bit)

### Additional Information

**Button** passes **addTitleTooltip = !wrap && !help** to the label component. In the 1.65.0 bundle, the hook that handles this flag (minified, in **StreamlitMarkdown.*.js**) always sets **title** to the label's text content. It does not check whether the text overflows (for example **el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth**).

A possible fix is to set **title** only when the label is truncated, and re-check it with a **ResizeObserver** alongside the existing **MutationObserver**. The same hook appears to be used by **st.checkbox**, **st.popover** and markdown with **wrap=False**, so these may be affected too.

Workaround: pass **wrap=True** to the button.

issues.title: AppTest: synchronize query parameters when interacting with query-bound widgets
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Please make AppTest's widget interaction API synchronize query parameters for widgets using `bind="query-params"`. Currently, `.set_value(...).run()` changes the widget value but leaves both `at.query_params` and the app's `st.query_params` unchanged, so tests observe a different state from the browser.

### Why?

Native query-param binding lets apps replace manual URL callbacks. After that change, AppTest tests that verify shareable filters or inspect `st.query_params` can no longer reproduce the state reached by the same user interaction in the browser. Each test must manually mirror the binding's serialization into `at.query_params`.

The following self-contained example demonstrates the gap on Streamlit 1.65.0; it also occurs on 1.64.0:

```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

at = AppTest.from_string("""
import streamlit as st

st.selectbox("FC", ["A", "B"], key="fc", bind="query-params")
st.session_state["seen_query"] = dict(st.query_params)
""").run()

at.selectbox[0].set_value("B").run()
assert not at.exception
print("Widget:", at.selectbox[0].value)
print("AppTest query params:", at.query_params)
print("App query params:", at.session_state["seen_query"])
```

Save as `repro_query_binding.py` and run `python repro_query_binding.py` with `streamlit==1.65.0` installed. No pytest or app-specific dependencies are required.

Observed:

```text
Widget: B
AppTest query params: {}
App query params: {}
```

In a browser, selecting B in the app string above updates the URL to `?fc=B` and the script sees `{"fc": "B"}`. The same AppTest gap occurs with `st.text_input(..., key="fc", bind="query-params")` and `at.text_input[0].set_value("B").run()`.

### How?

Use the existing interaction API to model the bound query-param update when a widget commits a value. For the example above, the desired result after `.set_value("B").run()` is:

```text
Widget: B
AppTest query params: {'fc': 'B'}
App query params: {'fc': 'B'}
```

The interaction should send a coherent widget-state/query-string pair using the widget's binding semantics, including serialization and clearing of the bound parameter. Unrelated query parameters should remain intact. This can be supported in the existing browserless AppTest API; a new browser runner is not requested.

A current workaround is to set the query params manually in the test before the run:

```python
at.selectbox[0].set_value("B")
at.query_params["fc"] = "B"
at.run()
assert at.session_state["seen_query"]["fc"] == "B"
```

This works, but the test must duplicate application binding logic. Keeping explicit `on_change` callbacks that write `st.query_params` also works, at the cost of retaining the application glue that native binding could replace.

### Additional Context

#### Environment and controls

- Streamlit: 1.65.0, also reproduced on 1.64.0.
- Python: 3.14.8.
- OS: macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- Browser: Not required for the AppTest example. Browser comparisons used the Codex in-app browser on macOS and confirmed correct binding on both versions.
- The tested Streamlit Python files match their wheel RECORD hashes; no installed source was modified.
- Initial URL values correctly seed a bound widget in AppTest.
- Programmatically changing `st.session_state["fc"]` before rendering the bound widget correctly updates query params.
- Manual URL-writing callbacks work in AppTest.

#### Related work checked

- [#16906](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16906) requests a first-party browser-testing API. This request targets bound-widget query serialization during existing AppTest interactions.
- [PR #17191](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17191), included in 1.65.0, fixes single-value/list representation in `at.query_params`. The example still returns an empty dict after that fix.
- [PR #16998](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16998) fixes browser back/forward restoration. This example changes a widget through AppTest and performs no history navigation.

I did not find an existing issue requesting this specific AppTest behavior. I am using the feature-request form because this extends the test simulation; the runtime binding itself works in the tested browser examples.

[LocalScriptRunner.run](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/testing/v1/local_script_runner.py#L170) constructs the query string from the query params passed by AppTest. The current widget interaction path does not generate the corresponding query-param update that a browser would send.

issues.title: Proposal: Make Streamlit Truly Event-Driven — Client-Side State, Events & Selective Reruns
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Feature Proposal: From Rerun-Driven to Event-Driven Streamlit
The Core Idea

Streamlit's greatest strength is also one of its defining architectural characteristics: Python execution is the primary mechanism through which application state and UI are updated.

This works exceptionally well for data applications where an interaction naturally maps to a Python computation.

However, highly interactive applications expose a different requirement:

A browser event is not necessarily a Python execution event.

A mouse move, drag, hover, resize, crosshair movement, animation frame, realtime tick, or temporary UI state change may occur dozens or hundreds of times per second.

Most of these events should not require Python to rerun.

The proposal is therefore not simply to add more widgets or more rerun options.

The deeper proposal is to introduce a lightweight event/state runtime between the browser and Python execution model.

Instead of treating every interaction as:

UI event → Python → rerun → UI

Streamlit could support:

                         UI EVENT
                             │
                 ┌───────────┴───────────┐
                 │                       │
                 ▼                       ▼
          Client-side state        Event routing
                 │                       │
                 │              ┌────────┼────────┐
                 │              │        │        │
                 ▼              ▼        ▼        ▼
             UI update       Client   Fragment   App
                              only      rerun    rerun

Python would remain the primary application and business-logic layer, but it would no longer have to participate in every interaction.

This is the architectural distinction behind the rest of this proposal.

The objective is not to turn Streamlit into React.

The objective is to make Streamlit capable of supporting both:

Traditional Streamlit
interaction → Python rerun

and:

Highly interactive Streamlit
interaction → client/state/event layer → Python only when needed

The existing programming model would remain intact. The new model would simply provide a second level of control for applications that need it.

Streamlit has made significant progress toward more granular execution control, fragments, background execution, and real-time UI updates.

The next step could be to provide a more general event-driven interaction model that allows Streamlit applications to handle high-frequency client-side events and state changes without requiring a Python script rerun for every interaction.

This would make Streamlit much more suitable not only for dashboards and data applications, but also for highly interactive applications such as trading terminals, monitoring systems, visual editors, control panels, and real-time operational interfaces.

The goal is not to replace Streamlit's existing rerun model, but to add a second, more granular interaction layer alongside it.

---

# The Core Problem

Today, Streamlit provides an excellent Python-first programming model:

User interaction
      ↓
Widget event
      ↓
Python execution
      ↓
UI update

This model is extremely productive for traditional data applications.
However, highly interactive applications often have a different event profile:

Mouse movement
Drag
Resize
Hover
Crosshair movement
Keyboard shortcut
Realtime market tick
Chart event
Component state change
      ↓
potentially dozens or hundreds of events per second

Not every one of these events should require a Python rerun.

For example, dragging a trading order line from one price to another may generate many intermediate browser events, while the application may only need to execute Python logic when the user releases the mouse button.

Similarly, a chart crosshair can move continuously without requiring Python execution at every pixel.

A more explicit separation between **client-side interaction**, **application state**, and **Python execution** would make Streamlit considerably more powerful.

# Proposed Model
Introduce an event/state layer that allows developers to explicitly define what happens when a client-side event occurs.

Conceptually:

                    ┌─────────────────────┐
                    │      Browser        │
                    │                     │
                    │ UI / Chart / Input  │
                    └──────────┬──────────┘
                               │
                    Client-side events
                               │
              ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐
              │                │                │
              ▼                ▼                ▼
          Client state     Event stream     Python event
              │                │                │
              ▼                ▼                ▼
       No rerun needed    Optional rerun    Fragment/App

The important idea is that **an event should not automatically imply a Python rerun**.

# 1. True Client-Side State

Allow components to maintain state that can change frequently on the client without immediately triggering Python execution.

For example:

chart_state = st.chart(
    symbol="BTCUSDT",
    client_state=True
)

Client-side state could include:

* cursor position
* selected item
* drag position
* zoom level
* viewport
* temporary form state
* hover state
* drawing state
* component-local UI state

Python could explicitly request the current state when needed.

This would preserve Streamlit's Python-first model while allowing components to behave more like native browser applications.

# 2. Event Channels

Introduce a generic event mechanism for high-frequency or transient browser events.
For example:

[python]
chart.on("mousemove", handler)
chart.on("drag", handler)
chart.on("crosshair", handler)
chart.on("resize", handler)
chart.on("selection", handler)

Events should be distinguishable from persistent state.
A useful distinction could be:

State
→ "What is the current value?"

Event
→ "What just happened?"
```
This distinction is particularly important for transient events such as mouse movement, clicks, keyboard shortcuts, and drag operations.

# 3. Fire-and-Forget Events

Allow events to be processed entirely on the client without invoking Python.
For example:

[python]
chart.on(
    "mousemove",
    client=True
)
or conceptually:

[python]
chart.on("drag", rerun=False)

This would allow extremely frequent UI interactions without overwhelming the Streamlit execution engine.
Python could still receive the final result:

drag start
   ↓
client-side movement
   ↓
client-side movement
   ↓
client-side movement
   ↓
drag end
   ↓
Python event

This is especially useful for:

* chart interactions
* sliders
* drawing tools
* drag-and-drop
* resizing
* visual editors
* canvas applications

# 4. Explicit Rerun Policy

Allow developers to explicitly define the execution scope of an event.
For example, conceptually:

[python]
widget(
    on_change="client"
)

or:

[python]
widget(
    on_event="fragment"
)

or:

[python]
widget(
    on_event="app"
)

or:

[python]
widget(
    on_event="none"
)

The exact API is open for discussion.
The important principle is that the developer should be able to specify:

No Python execution
        OR
Component/client update
        OR
Fragment rerun
        OR
Full application rerun

This would complement Streamlit's existing progress toward selective reruns.

# 5. Shared Reactive State

Provide a lightweight mechanism for multiple components to observe the same application state without requiring a full application rerun for every update.
For example:

[python]
price = st.reactive_state("BTCUSDT.price")

chart.bind(price)
price_panel.bind(price)
order_panel.bind(price)

A state update could then propagate selectively:

             BTC price
                 │
       ┌─────────┼─────────┐
       ▼         ▼         ▼
     Chart     Metric    Order UI

This would be particularly useful for real-time applications where many UI elements depend on the same rapidly changing state.

The mechanism should ideally support:

* selective subscriptions
* batching
* throttling
* debouncing
* immutable snapshots
* explicit synchronization boundaries

# 6. High-Frequency Event Streams

Provide first-class support for event streams that may produce many updates per second.

Examples:

market ticks
sensor data
telemetry
mouse movement
chart crosshair
audio/video state
live logs
simulation output

Instead of:

event → rerun → render → event → rerun → render

the model could support:

event stream
     ↓
buffer / throttle / batch
     ↓
selected subscribers
     ↓
UI update

Developers should ideally be able to control:

[python]
throttle=50      # milliseconds
debounce=100
batch=True
max_rate=20

This would make realtime applications much easier to build while protecting the Python execution engine from excessive event traffic.

# 7. First-Class JavaScript / TypeScript Components

Streamlit's custom component architecture is extremely valuable, but highly interactive applications often require developers to move a significant amount of application logic into JavaScript/TypeScript.

A future component API could make this boundary more seamless.
Ideally, a component should be able to expose:

Python API
     │
     ├── persistent state
     ├── transient events
     ├── client-side actions
     └── server-side callbacks

without forcing developers to effectively build a separate frontend application.

For example:

[python]
chart = st.interactive_component(...)

chart.state
chart.events
chart.call("zoom_to", ...)
chart.emit("selection", ...)

The goal would be to make JavaScript/TypeScript an **extension of Streamlit**, rather than a parallel application architecture.

# 8. A Unified Event → State → Rerun Model

The eight ideas above could ultimately form one coherent programming model:

                 CLIENT
                   │
        ┌──────────┴──────────┐
        │                     │
      Events                State
        │                     │
        ▼                     ▼
   Event routing       State synchronization
        │                     │
        └──────────┬──────────┘
                   ▼
             Execution policy
                   │
        ┌──────────┼──────────┐
        ▼          ▼          ▼
      Client     Fragment     App
       only       rerun      rerun

This would preserve the simplicity that makes Streamlit attractive while giving developers much more control when building complex interactive applications.

# Example Use Case: Real-Time Trading Interface

A real-time trading terminal is a useful stress test for this model.
Consider a chart with draggable Entry, Stop Loss, and Take Profit levels.
During dragging:

Mouse movement
      ↓
Client-side chart update
      ↓
No Python rerun

When the user releases the mouse:

Drag end
      ↓
Event
      ↓
Python
      ↓
Risk calculation
      ↓
Order validation
      ↓
UI update

At the same time, market data could arrive independently:

WebSocket
    ↓
price event
    ↓
shared reactive state
    ↓
chart + position panel + P/L

This type of application currently requires a significant amount of custom frontend logic.

A more granular Streamlit event model could make such applications much more natural to implement while retaining Python as the primary application language.

# Why This Could Be Valuable Beyond Trading

The same architecture would benefit:

* real-time monitoring dashboards
* industrial control panels
* IoT interfaces
* scientific visualization
* financial terminals
* simulation environments
* visual editors
* workflow builders
* interactive maps
* multimedia applications
* operational dashboards
* collaborative applications

In other words, this would not be a trading-specific feature.

It would expand the category of applications that can be built naturally with Streamlit.

# Compatibility With the Existing Streamlit Model

This proposal does not require removing or fundamentally changing Streamlit's current execution model.

The existing model would remain the default:

Widget → Python → rerun

The new model would simply provide additional levels of control:

Client event
     ↓
   ┌───────────────────────────────┐
   │                               │
Client only → Fragment → App rerun


Developers building traditional data applications would not need to use any of this.

Developers building highly interactive applications could opt into it where necessary.

# Design Principle

The key principle could be summarized as:

> **Not every UI event should be a Python execution event.**

And similarly:

> **Not every state change needs to become a full application rerun.**

Streamlit has already been moving toward more granular execution and real-time interaction. A unified event/state model could provide the architectural layer that connects these improvements into a coherent system.

# Suggested Discussion Questions

Some questions that would be useful for the Streamlit team and community:

1. Should transient events and persistent component state be first-class, separate concepts?
2. Should client-only events be able to bypass Python entirely?
3. Should developers be able to explicitly select the rerun scope of an event?
4. Could shared reactive state be implemented without introducing a React-like programming model?
5. How should high-frequency events be throttled, debounced, or batched?
6. Could custom components expose a standardized event/state interface?
7. How far should Streamlit go toward supporting desktop-class interactive applications while retaining its Python-first simplicity?

---

## Conclusion

Streamlit's Python-first development model is one of its strongest advantages.

The goal should not be to turn Streamlit into React.

Instead, Streamlit could provide a **small, explicit event/state layer** that allows developers to build applications where:

* Python remains the application and business-logic layer;
* the browser handles high-frequency interaction locally;
* state can be synchronized selectively;
* events can be routed to client, fragment, or application scope;
* realtime streams can be throttled and batched;
* custom components can participate in the same model.

That would preserve Streamlit's simplicity while significantly expanding the class of interactive applications it can support.


### Why?

_No response_

### How?

_No response_

### Additional Context

_No response_

issues.title: st.multiselect without key drops the user's selection when options come in a different order on rerun
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

If `st.multiselect` has no `key` and its `options` list comes back in a different order on the next run, every selection the user makes is thrown away. The widget briefly shows the new chip, then flickers back to the default. Passing `sorted(options)` makes it work, and so does setting any `key`.

The order of options is often unstable in real apps: `list(set(...))`, `df[col].unique()` after a filter, SQL queries without `ORDER BY`, dict/set unions, and "move selected to top" patterns.

Similar reports were closed as expected behavior (#5995, #8496). #11277 fixed the case where `key` is set. The keyless case still resets, even though multiselect doesn't need it to.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import random
import streamlit as st

opts = ["apple", "banana", "cherry", "date", "elderberry"]
random.shuffle(opts)  # stands in for list(set(...)), an unordered query, etc.

sel = st.multiselect("Fruits", opts)  # works with sorted(opts) or key="fruits"
st.write(sel)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app.
2. Pick any option in the multiselect.

### Expected Behavior

The option stays selected, because the set of options didn't change and only their order did.

### Current Behavior

The chip appears for a moment and then disappears. `sel` is `[]`. Measured with `AppTest` on 1.64.0:

| options | key | value after select | value after next rerun |
|---|---|---|---|
| sorted | no | `['banana']` | `['banana']` |
| sorted | yes | `['banana']` | `['banana']` |
| shuffled | no | `[]` | `[]` |
| shuffled | yes | `['banana']` | `['banana']` |

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info


Field | Value
-- | --
Streamlit version | 1.64.0
Python version | 3.12
Operating System | Linux
Browser | Chrome



### Additional Information

### Why this happens

In `lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/multiselect.py`, when there is no `key`, the widget ID is a hash of the widget parameters, including the **ordered** list of formatted options and the **indices** of the defaults:

```python
element_id = compute_and_register_element_id(
    widget_name,
    user_key=key,
    key_as_main_identity={"max_selections", "accept_new_options"},
    ...
    options=formatted_options,   # order-sensitive
    default=default_values,      # indices into options, also order-sensitive
    ...
)
```

With a new order, the ID changes on every run. When the user clicks, the frontend sends the value under the old ID. The rerun registers a widget with a new ID and no stored state, so it falls back to `default`. The frontend then mounts a new component with that ID, which is the flicker.

For multiselect, including the order isn't needed. The value travels as a list of **formatted option strings** (`string_array_value`), not indices. `MultiSelectSerde.deserialize` maps strings back with `formatted_options.index(v)`, and `validate_and_sync_multiselect_value_with_options` already handles options that change. The same selection means the same thing in any order.

### Proposed fix

Hash the options without regard to order, and hash defaults by value rather than by index:

```diff
             dg=self.dg,
             label=label,
-            options=formatted_options,
-            default=default_values,
+            # Values are stored as formatted strings rather than indices, so the
+            # order of options doesn't change their meaning. Hash options
+            # order-insensitively so reordering them doesn't reset the widget.
+            options=sorted(formatted_options),
+            default=[formatted_options[i] for i in default_values],
             help=help,
             max_selections=max_selections,
```

`proto.options` and `proto.default` are unchanged, so the display order still follows what the user passed. Only the identity hash changes. With this patch applied to 1.64.0, all four rows in the table above keep the selection, including with `default=[...]` set.

Notes:
- Existing keyless multiselects get new IDs once after upgrading. That's the same one-time reset any ID-scheme change causes.
- `selectbox`, `pills`, and `segmented_control` probably need the same change wherever they send values as strings. I haven't checked those.

issues.title: Custom Components v2 trigger is silently lost when another widget updates while its rerun is queued
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A Custom Components v2 (CCv2) `setTriggerValue` call is silently lost when its rerun request is still queued and another widget update arrives before the script runner picks it up: the `on_<event>_change` callback never runs and `result.<event>` is never set. `st.button` survives the identical sequence. With default settings this affects components inside `@st.fragment`, and with `runner.fastReruns = false` it also affects full-app reruns.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time

import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("log", [])

probe = st.components.v2.component(
    "trigger_probe",
    html="<button id='fire'>Fire component trigger</button>",
    js="""
export default function (component) {
  const { parentElement, setTriggerValue } = component;
  parentElement.querySelector("#fire").onclick = () => setTriggerValue("fired", Date.now());
}
""",
)


@st.fragment
def panel():
    # result.fired only exists for events with an on_<event>_change callback.
    result = probe(key="probe", on_fired_change=lambda: None)
    if result.fired:
        st.session_state.log.append("component trigger received")
    if st.button("st.button"):
        st.session_state.log.append("st.button click received")
    st.text_input("Other widget", key="other")
    st.write("Received:", st.session_state.log)
    time.sleep(5)  # a slow fragment, so the next requests queue up


panel()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `streamlit run app.py` and wait for the first run to finish (about 5 s).
2. Click **Fire component trigger** while the app is idle. `Received:` shows `component trigger received`. This is the control.
3. Type `a` into **Other widget** and press Enter. The fragment reruns and sleeps for 5 s.
4. Within those 5 s, click **Fire component trigger**, then replace the text in **Other widget** with `b` and press Enter.
5. Wait for the fragment to finish.
6. Repeat steps 3–5, but click **st.button** instead of **Fire component trigger**.

### Expected Behavior

After step 5 the log gains a second `component trigger received`, the same way step 6 adds `st.button click received`.

### Current Behavior

After step 5 the log still holds only the control entry: the trigger fired in step 4 never reaches Python, although the text input's new value is applied. After step 6, `st.button click received` is appended as expected.

A full-app version of the script (the same body without `@st.fragment`) behaves the same way when started with `--runner.fastReruns false`.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (also reproduced on 1.63.0)
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating System: macOS 27.0
- Browser: Chromium 152

### Additional Information

**Why it happens.** `AppSession.request_rerun` stops the current runner and starts a new one only when `runner.fastReruns` is on and the request has no `fragment_id`. A widget-triggered fragment rerun (or any rerun when `fastReruns` is off) is handed to the existing `ScriptRunner`. A fragment rerun also does not preempt the running script (`_fragment_run_should_not_preempt_script`), so it waits in the queue. If a rerun request is already queued, `ScriptRequests.request_rerun` merges the two requests with `_coalesce_widget_states(old, new)`. That keeps the newer message's widget states and carries forward only `trigger_value` and `chat_input_value` from the older one.

A CCv2 trigger is a `json_trigger_value` on the component's synthetic aggregator ID (`$$STREAMLIT_INTERNAL_KEY_<id>__events`). The frontend deletes trigger values once it has sent them, so the newer message never contains the trigger, and the merge drops it.

`string_trigger_value`, used by `st.menu_button` and `st.column_config.ButtonColumn`, is missing from the same list. Checking `_coalesce_widget_states` directly on 1.64.0, with a queued trigger of each type followed by a newer message for another widget:

| Queued trigger type | Kept after the merge |
|---|---|
| `trigger_value` (`st.button`) | yes |
| `chat_input_value` (`st.chat_input`) | yes |
| `string_trigger_value` (`st.menu_button`, `ButtonColumn`) | no |
| `json_trigger_value` (CCv2 `setTriggerValue`) | no |

I reproduced the CCv2 case in the browser. The `string_trigger_value` row is from the function-level check only.

**Suggested fix.** 1.64.0 already has `_TRIGGER_PROTO_FIELDS` and `_has_active_trigger_value`, and `_coalesce_replay_trigger_states` uses them. `_coalesce_widget_states` could apply its existing carry-forward rule to every active trigger type through the same helper, instead of the hard-coded two-item list. When both messages carry a `json_trigger_value` for the same aggregator ID, concatenating the two event lists would keep both events. A rough sketch:

```python
import json  # not imported in script_requests.py today


def _trigger_events(state):
    events = json.loads(state.json_trigger_value)
    return events if isinstance(events, list) else [events]


# In _coalesce_widget_states, replacing the loop over the two-item list:
for old_state in old_states.widgets:
    if not _has_active_trigger_value(old_state):
        continue
    trigger_type = old_state.WhichOneof("value")
    new_state = states_by_id.get(old_state.id)
    if new_state is None or (
        new_state.WhichOneof("value") == trigger_type
        and not _has_active_trigger_value(new_state)
    ):
        # Today's rule, applied to every trigger type.
        states_by_id[old_state.id] = old_state
    elif trigger_type == "json_trigger_value" == new_state.WhichOneof("value"):
        # Both messages carry CCv2 events for one aggregator: keep both lists.
        merged = WidgetState()
        merged.CopyFrom(new_state)
        merged.json_trigger_value = json.dumps(_trigger_events(old_state) + _trigger_events(new_state))
        states_by_id[old_state.id] = merged
```

With this patched in at startup on 1.64.0, the browser repro above passes: the trigger fired in step 4 reaches Python, and the text input's new value is applied too. At the function level it keeps all four trigger types from the table and merges two events sent to one aggregator into a single list.

**Related.** The automated triage comment on #16732 (mount-time `setTriggerValue` dropped) noted this gap. The fix that closed it, #16833, made one non-test change, to `WidgetStateManager.removeInactive` in the frontend, so this backend path is unchanged. #16765 added the replay-trigger helpers that the fix above could reuse. The tech spec in the open spec PR #16763 (session-owned rerun mailbox) lists all four trigger types as ones that "may not be dropped by coalescing" and calls this the carry-forward already implemented. In 1.64.0, `_coalesce_widget_states` carries two of them. The same two-item list is on `develop` as of 2026-10-01 and in 1.52.0, so this is not a regression.

issues.title: Programmatically set selections fail for empty selection
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The example in https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/data/st.dataframe titled: "Example 2: Programmatically set selections" does not work if we try with empty selections.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st
from numpy.random import default_rng as rng

df = pd.DataFrame(rng(0).standard_normal((12, 5)), columns=["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"])

if st.button("Select the first row"):
    st.session_state["data"] = {"selection": {"rows": [0], "columns": [], "cells": []}}
if st.button("Select no row"):
    st.session_state["data"] = {"selection": {"rows": [], "columns": [], "cells": []}}

event = st.dataframe(
    df,
    key="data",
    on_select="rerun",
    selection_mode=["single-row"],
)

st.code(event.selection)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the code
2. Select a row
3. Click on the button "Select the first row", it works as expected
4. Select a row again
5. Click on the button "Select no row", the dataframe selection state is empty but the table keeps the previous selection.

### Expected Behavior

The row selection should match the dataframe selection state and be empty.

### Current Behavior

The dataframe selection state is empty but the table keeps the previous selection and is not empty.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.63.0
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: WSL Docker
- Browser: Edge


### Additional Information

I remember it worked in Streamlit version 1.57.0 but I am not sure, I may be mistaken.

issues.title: AppTest: an `st.components.v2` component defined in an imported module is "not registered" in later AppTest instances
issues.body:
### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary An app that imports an inline `st.components.v2.component(...)` from another module works under `streamlit run`, but in a test suite only the first `AppTest` that imports that module can render it: every later `AppTest` in the same Python process records `StreamlitAPIException: Component '' is not registered.` in `at.exception`. If anything imports the module before the first `AppTest` runs (a `conftest.py`, another test), that one fails too, so results depend on test order. A component defined in the script body itself is not affected, because it registers again on every run. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python # my_component.py import streamlit as st greeting = st.components.v2.component("greeting", html="

hi

") # app.py from my_component import greeting greeting(key="g") # test_app.py from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest def test_first_apptest_renders_the_component(): at = AppTest.from_file("app.py").run() assert not at.exception, at.exception[0].value def test_second_apptest_renders_the_same_component(): at = AppTest.from_file("app.py").run() assert not at.exception, at.exception[0].value ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Put the three files in one directory. 2. Run `pytest test_app.py`. ### Expected Behavior Both tests pass, the same way `streamlit run app.py` renders the component every time. ### Current Behavior ``` E AssertionError: Component 'greeting' is not registered. 1 failed, 1 passed ``` The first test passes and the second fails. Each test passes when run on its own. If `import my_component` is added at the top of `test_app.py`, both fail. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (also reproduced on 1.63.0) - Python version: 3.14.7 - Operating System: macOS 27.0 - Browser: n/a (AppTest) ### Additional Information **Why it happens.** `st.components.v2.component()` registers the definition once, when it is called (normally at module import), into `get_bidi_component_manager()`. That is the active runtime's registry, or a throwaway local `BidiComponentManager` when no runtime exists. `AppTest` creates one `BidiComponentManager` per instance (reused across that instance's reruns) and only runs `discover_and_register_components()` on it, which scans installed component packages. Python caches the module, so later instances never re-run the `component()` call, and the name is missing from their registry. **Workaround.** Make the module re-import inside each test's run: ```python # conftest.py import sys import pytest @pytest.fixture(autouse=True) def reimport_component_module(): sys.modules.pop("my_component", None) ``` With this fixture both tests pass. Replacing the component callable with a stub in tests also works. **Suggested fix.** `_mount_component` closes over only `component_key` and `isolate_styles`, but `_create_component_callable()` has the raw `html`, `css` and `js` in scope. If it kept them, `_mount_component` could register the definition into the current registry when the name is missing there, before mounting. File-backed definitions would need their paths resolved against that registry. Alternatively, keep a process-level record of inline definitions and seed each new `AppTest` registry from it. **Related.** #15484 (AppTest did not discover installed CCv2 components) and #14274 (AppTest `TypeError` with CCv2) are both closed. #14274's reproducer used this same imported-module pattern with a single test. The regression test added with its fix (#14301) defines the component inside `AppTest.from_function`, so it registers again on every run and does not cover this case.

issues.title: Pills/ToggleButtonGroup: all options render with "selected" style on fresh page load in Safari
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

On fresh page load (before any user interaction), st.pills (multi-select mode) renders ALL options with the "selected" purple-outline style in Safari, even though no option is selected — the underlying server-side state (default=None) is correctly empty. The visual bug appears specifically in real Safari and does not reproduce in Chromium or Playwright's WebKit engine.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

selected = st.pills(
    "Filter",
    options=["Option A", "Option B", "Option C"],
    selection_mode="multi",
    default=None,
)
st.write(selected)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open the app fresh in Safari (macOS or iOS) — a new tab/window, not a warm reload.
2. Before clicking anything, observe the st.pills widget with selection_mode="multi" and default=None.
3. All options render with the "selected" purple-outline styling, even though nothing has been selected yet.
4. The underlying state is correct (st.write(selected) shows an empty list) — this is a visual-only bug.
5. Does NOT reproduce in Chromium or in Playwright's WebKit engine — only in real Safari.

### Expected Behavior

On fresh load with default=None, all pill options should render in the plain/unselected style, matching the actual empty selection state.

### Current Behavior

All pill options render in the "selected" style (purple outline/fill) on fresh page load in Safari, despite no option being selected and the server-side value correctly being an empty list.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: (from your requirements.txt / Railway build — Claude Code can confirm the exact version)
- Browser: Safari (macOS) — reproduces on real Safari; does not reproduce in Chromium or Playwright's WebKit
- OS: macOS

### Additional Information

Extracted the relevant CSS from the live page's compiled stylesheet:
[data-selected]:not([data-disabled]) { background-color: rgba(79,70,229,0.1); border-color: rgb(79,70,229); color: rgb(79,70,229); }

This appears to be an attribute-presence selector issue: in Chromium/WebKit-via-Playwright, react-aria (the underlying ToggleButtonGroup implementation) correctly omits the data-selected attribute entirely on unselected buttons, so the selector doesn't match. It's possible real Safari's DOM/CSS engine handles react-aria's attribute timing differently on initial paint, causing data-selected to be briefly (or persistently) present on all buttons before Safari's own attribute-removal logic runs — worth investigating from the react-aria/Safari interaction side.

issues.title: selectbox clears on rerun if format_func returns new value, even with the same options.
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit selectbox gets re-created when formatted labels change, discarding user output. 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time

if "start_time" not in st.session_state:
  st.session_state["start_time"] = time.time()

start_time = st.session_state["start_time"]

option = st.selectbox(
  label="Single-select Option",
  options=["A", "B", "C"],
  format_func=lambda option: f"{option}: {int(time.time()-start_time)} seconds ago",
  key="option",
  index=None
)

st.write("Single-select Option:", option)

option2 = st.multiselect(
  label="Multi-select Options",
  options=["D", "E", "F"],
  format_func=lambda option: f"{option}: {int(time.time()-start_time)} seconds ago",
  key="option2",
)

st.write("Multi-select Options:", option2)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. In Single-select Option, Select "A"
2. In Multi-select Options, Select "D"
3. In Multi-select Options, Select "E"
4. In Multi-select Options, Select "F"
5. Wait 1 second
6. Click out of the multi select option dropdown

### Expected Behavior

It should have option A selected for 'Single-select Option', and options D, E and F selected for 'Multi-select Options'

### Current Behavior

Single-select option and multi-select options have nothing selected.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.63
- Python version: Python 3.14.7
- Operating System: Ubuntu 26.4
- Browser: Firefox 156.0.1 


### Additional Information

Proposed solution 1: Do not clear the selectbox if the selected options still exist.

Proposed solution 2: Update the selectbox and multiselect documentation with a warning about this. Currently the documentation for format_func says: "This has no impact on the return value of the command." which I would say is incorrect in this case.

This issue seems closely related to issues #11277 and #11268. They seemed to be closed for being fixed in 1.54.1.dev20260204, though I am still seeing this unexpected behavior in 1.63.

Thank you so much for your work on streamlit. It is very amazing!

issues.title: `st.dataframe` toolbar buttons are 22.4px, below the WCAG 2.2 24px minimum target size (axe `target-size`)
issues.body:
### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary
The hover toolbar that `st.dataframe` draws (Show/hide columns, Download as CSV, Search, Fullscreen)
renders each button at 22.4 x 22.4 CSS px, and the buttons sit next to each other, so axe-core's
`target-size` rule (impact: serious, WCAG 2.2 AA, SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)) fails. Cause:
`StyledElementToolbarButton` in `frontend/lib/src/components/shared/BaseButton/styled-components.ts`
(1.64.0, line ~524) sets `padding: theme.spacing.twoXS` and `minHeight: "unset"` around a small icon.

### Reproducible Code Example
Same app as above (the `st.dataframe` line is enough).

### Steps To Reproduce
1. `streamlit run app.py`
2. Hover the dataframe so the toolbar appears.
3. Run axe-core 4.13 with the `wcag22aa` tag.

### Expected Behavior
Each toolbar button is at least 24 x 24 CSS px (or spaced so a 24px circle around each does not overlap
another target).

### Current Behavior
```
target-size (serious, wcag22aa, wcag258) — 4 nodes
<button kind="elementToolbar" data-testid="stBaseButton-elementToolbar" aria-label="Show/hide columns" class="st-emotion-cache-18ac3gt eqzt73c20">
  Target has insufficient size (22.4px by 22.4px, should be at least 24px by 24px)
<button ... aria-label="Download as CSV" ...>   (same)
<button ... aria-label="Search" ...>            (same)
<button ... aria-label="Fullscreen" ...>        (same)
```

### Suggested fix
Give `StyledElementToolbarButton` `minWidth: "1.5rem"` and `minHeight: "1.5rem"` (24px) instead of
`minHeight: "unset"`, or raise the padding one step. The toolbar is already an overlay above the element,
so the extra 1.6px per button does not move page layout. The same styled button is used by other element
toolbars (charts, `st.data_editor`), which would all pass with the one change.

In the same minimal app, axe also reports `target-size` on the `st.date_input` month/day spinbutton
segments (17.9 x 19.6px); that may deserve its own look but is secondary.

### Is this a regression?
- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.
- [x] No.

### Debug info
- Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (latest)
- Python version: 3.12
- OS: Linux (CI) and Windows 11
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright bundled)
- axe-core: 4.13.0

issues.title: `aria-expanded` on elements with no role: sidebar `<section>` and `st.date_input` field fail axe `aria-allowed-attr` (WCAG 4.1.2)
issues.body:
### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary
Every page of an app with a sidebar fails axe-core's `aria-allowed-attr` rule (impact: critical, WCAG 2.0 A,
SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value), and so does every `st.date_input`. In both cases `aria-expanded` is set on an
element whose role does not support it:

1. The sidebar is rendered as a plain `<section>` with no accessible name, so it has no landmark role that
   supports `aria-expanded`. `frontend/app/src/components/Sidebar/Sidebar.tsx` (1.64.0, line ~265):
   `aria-expanded={!isCollapsed}` on the `Resizable` rendered as `StyledSidebar`.
2. The date input's field is a `<div>` with no role carrying `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`.
   `frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/DateInput/SingleDateInput.tsx` (1.64.0, line ~553); the same pattern
   is in `RangeDateInput.tsx`.

Assistive technology ignores (or mis-announces) state on an element it cannot map to a role, so the
expanded/collapsed state is not conveyed, and automated audits (axe, Lighthouse) report a critical failure
that app authors cannot fix from Python.

### Reproducible Code Example
```python
import datetime
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

st.sidebar.write("Sidebar content")
st.date_input("Start date", datetime.date(2026, 1, 1))
st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": ["x", "y", "z"]}))
```

### Steps To Reproduce
1. `streamlit run app.py`
2. Run axe-core 4.13 (e.g. `@axe-core/playwright` with tags `wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa, wcag22aa`)
   against the page, at 1280px or 390px wide.

### Expected Behavior
No `aria-allowed-attr` violations.

### Current Behavior
```
aria-allowed-attr (critical, wcag2a, wcag412) — 2 nodes
<section class="stSidebar st-emotion-cache-1kss9tm e16xr0mu0" data-testid="stSidebar" aria-expanded="true" style="position: relative; ...">
  ARIA attribute is not allowed: aria-expanded="true"
<div aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowDown" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="false" data-testid="stDateInputField" class="st-emotion-cache-11mhraf ekyilc22">
  ARIA attribute is not allowed: aria-expanded="false"
```
(At 390px the sidebar starts collapsed and the same node reports `aria-expanded="false"`.)

### Suggested fix
- **Sidebar:** put the state on the control, not the region. Remove `aria-expanded` from the `<section>`;
  set `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls="<sidebar id>"` on the collapse/expand buttons
  (`stSidebarCollapseButton` / `stExpandSidebarButton`), which already carry `aria-label`s since #14563.
  Optionally give the section an accessible name (`aria-label="Sidebar"`) so it becomes a `region` landmark.
- **Date input:** follow the React Aria DatePicker pattern the widget is now built on: the field is
  `role="group"` (labelled by the widget label) and the popup state lives on the element that opens the
  calendar. Either move `aria-haspopup` / `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` / `aria-keyshortcuts` to a
  calendar toggle `<button>`, or, if the whole field must stay the trigger, give it a role that supports
  them. (It contains spinbuttons, so `role="button"` would nest interactive content; a separate button is
  the clean option.)

### Is this a regression?
- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.
- [x] No — sidebar has had it for several releases; the date input form arrived with the non-BaseWeb
  DateInput (#16460, 1.62).

### Debug info
- Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (latest)
- Python version: 3.12
- OS: Linux (CI, Chromium via Playwright) and Windows 11 (Chromium)
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright bundled)
- axe-core: 4.13.0

### Additional Information
Found by a WCAG 2.2 AA gate that runs axe on every page of several Streamlit apps at 390px and 1280px;
these are the only `aria-allowed-attr` findings left in those apps and none is reachable from app code.

issues.title: `heartbeat_ack` is discarded when a script run starts before the queue flushes
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`ForwardMsgQueue.clear(retain_lifecycle_msgs=True)` keeps only `new_session`, `script_finished`, `session_status_changed`, `parent_message`, `page_info_changed` and toast deltas ([forward_msg_queue.py lines 135-146](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/runtime/forward_msg_queue.py#L135-L146)). `heartbeat_ack` is not in that set, so an ack that is already sitting in the queue is destroyed instead of delivered. `AppSession._clear_queue` calls this on every `SCRIPT_STARTED`, and the runtime flushes queues on a short timer, so an ack enqueued in the window between a heartbeat arriving and the next script run starting never reaches the browser. A host that sends one `SEND_APP_HEARTBEAT` and waits for the ack can wait forever.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from streamlit.proto.ForwardMsg_pb2 import ForwardMsg
from streamlit.runtime.forward_msg_queue import ForwardMsgQueue

queue = ForwardMsgQueue()

ack = ForwardMsg()
ack.heartbeat_ack = True
finished = ForwardMsg()
finished.script_finished = ForwardMsg.FINISHED_SUCCESSFULLY

queue.enqueue(ack)
queue.enqueue(finished)
[m.WhichOneof("type") for m in queue._queue]  # ['heartbeat_ack', 'script_finished']

queue.clear(retain_lifecycle_msgs=True)
[m.WhichOneof("type") for m in queue._queue]  # ['script_finished']  <- ack is gone
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `streamlit run` (or `uv run streamlit run`) the snippet.
2. Observe that the second print no longer contains `heartbeat_ack`.

End to end: open an app in an iframe host that sends `SEND_APP_HEARTBEAT` exactly once while a rerun is being triggered (for example, immediately after a widget interaction). The ack for that heartbeat is never received.

### Expected Behavior

A heartbeat ack is a one-shot reply to a client request, like a toast is a one-shot notification. It should survive the interrupted-run queue clear, or be sent directly rather than queued, so that one heartbeat always produces one ack.

### Current Behavior

The ack is silently removed from the queue when a script run starts before the queue is flushed. Nothing is logged. The client sees no reply.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.63.0 and 1.64.0, both reproduced
- Python version: 3.14.6
- Operating System: Linux Mint 22.3 Zena 64-bit
- Browser: Version 152.0.7977.82 (Official Build) for Linux Mint (x86_64) but **not browser-specific; reproduced as a pure function of `ForwardMsgQueue`**

### Additional Information

The toast case (#7740) was fixed by adding `_is_toast_delta(msg)` to the retain predicate ([forward_msg_queue.py line 146](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/runtime/forward_msg_queue.py#L146)); the same shape would fix this (`msg.WhichOneof("type") == "heartbeat_ack"`). We hit this from a test harness that uses a heartbeat round trip to prove a WebSocket reconnect completed; sending heartbeats on an interval rather than once is the workaround.

issues.title: Support real-time chart updates without rerunning the entire script
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, Streamlit requires rerunning the entire script to refresh visual elements such as charts or plots.
This feature request suggests adding native support for incremental or real-time updates to chart components, allowing smoother dashboards for live data without script reruns.

### Why?

I often build dashboards with data that changes every few seconds (e.g. IoT sensors, live logs, financial data).
The current rerun mechanism makes the app flicker and consume excessive CPU, as every update forces Streamlit to re-execute all widgets and scripts.
A lighter update mechanism would make Streamlit much more efficient for real-time applications.

### How?

Introduce a new method, for example:

chart = st.line_chart(initial_data)
chart.update(new_data)


or a context manager such as:

with st.chart("my_chart") as chart:
    chart.update(data)


This would allow partial UI updates for selected components instead of full script reruns, leading to faster refresh rates and better performance.

### Additional Context

This feature would be highly valuable for real-time dashboards and data streaming use cases.
Similar functionality exists in libraries like Plotly Dash (dcc.Interval) or Bokeh Server.
Discussion inspiration: Streamlit Community Forum – Real-time dashboard performance

### **Summary**
Adding a required=True parameter would allow for built-in browser-level validation and clearer UI signaling that a field must be filled before a form can be submitted.

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Attributes/required


### **Why?**
Adding a required prop would benefit the development in several ways:

- It allows browsers to trigger native "Please fill out this field" tooltips and visually mark fields without the developer needing to manually inject CSS or markdown.
- Save the manual logic to prevent the form from submitting or showing additional messages causing re-renders.
- Allow screen readers to communicate form requirements.


### **How?**
Include an optional argument for required=True into the st.text_input() function

issues.title: 2nd Sidebar (on right side)
issues.body:
### Problem

A neat app often elucidates complex problems. Hence there is often a lot to explain to carry details about the app itself, its backgrounds and further details - especially for public apps. Currently, the little space in the sidebar and main window quickly get filled with explanations and further links. I have written long markdown documents one can hide, but still, either people quickly uncheck the box to head for the box or get overwhelmed with details. Eventually, a good app is not used because of a cluttered layout, long scrolling and still insufficient clarity.

### Solution

**MVP:** A 2nd sidebar on the right side could be a nice designated place for such instructions, background information etc. It would save a lot of real estate in the other sections and still provide novice users with guidance without distracting frequent users. Moreover I consider it rather simple to copy the class from the existing sidebar - just as a right-bound counterpart.

**Possible additions:** Another option cold be an annotation overlay for all controls.

**Preferred solution:** I prefer the simple and straight forward solution

### Additional context

Thanks so much and many cheers.
Conrad

issues.title: [Coming soon] Don't rerun on widget interaction
issues.body:
When a user interacts with a widget, Streamlit always reruns the entire script. There are ways to get around this (forms, caching, ...) but sometimes it would be really useful to just do something like `st.slider(..., rerun=False)`. 

See requests in this very popular forum post: https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/how-to-prevent-the-reloading-of-the-whole-page-when-i-let-the-user-to-perform-an-action/10800/7

This touches on the fundamental of Streamlit so we'll need to think this through carefully. No guarantees that we'll do this anytime soon! If you have use cases, please post them here (and upvote the issue!) so we can prioritize and see what's the best way to solve all problems. 

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

**If you'd like the Streamlit team to prioritize this feature request, please use the 👍 (thumbs up emoji) reaction in response to the initial post.**
