issues.body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary A keyed `st.dataframe` or `st.data_editor` excludes its data from the element identity: `key_as_main_identity={"selection_mode", "is_selection_activated"}` at [arrow.py lines 1280-1284](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/arrow.py#L1280-L1284). The element id therefore survives a data refresh, and the browser resends grid state that was computed against the previous frame. `event.selection.rows` and `edited_rows` are positional, so after a rerun that reorders or inserts rows those positions address different records, and the app receives a selection or an edit for a row the user never touched. There is no error and no warning. The comment directly above that call site acknowledges that selections "can become orphaned when the data changes" and that resetting them "might be a nice enhancement"; the effect on an app that acts on the selection is a wrong-row write, not a cosmetic orphan. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import pandas as pd import streamlit as st st.session_state.setdefault("gen", 0) st.session_state.setdefault("closed", []) # Simulates a queue whose contents change between reruns (a new ticket arrived). rows = ["TICK-101", "TICK-102", "TICK-103", "TICK-104"] if st.session_state["gen"]: rows = ["TICK-100", *rows] df = pd.DataFrame({"ticket": rows}) event = st.dataframe(df, key="queue", on_select="rerun", selection_mode="single-row") if st.button("Simulate new ticket arriving", key="refresh"): st.session_state["gen"] += 1 st.rerun() if st.button("Close selected", key="close") and event.selection.rows: position = event.selection.rows[0] st.session_state["closed"].append(df.iloc[position]["ticket"]) st.write("Selected positions:", event.selection.rows) st.write("Closed:", st.session_state["closed"]) ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. `streamlit run` (or `uv run streamlit run`) the snippet. 2. Click the row showing `TICK-102` (position 1). The app shows `Selected positions: [1]`. 3. Click "Simulate new ticket arriving". `TICK-102` gets bumped down to position 2, but the highlighted row and `event.selection.rows` are still `[1]`, which is now `TICK-101`. 4. Click "Close selected". You get `Closed: ['TICK-101']` even though you had initially selected `TICK-102`. The same holds for `st.data_editor` with the default `num_rows="fixed"`: a pending `edited_rows` entry is re-applied at the same position after the frame changes. The identity part can be shown without a browser, using `AppTest`: ```python from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest def script(): import pandas as pd import streamlit as st st.session_state.setdefault("gen", 0) if st.button("refresh", key="refresh"): st.session_state["gen"] += 1 rows = ["TICK-101", "TICK-102", "TICK-103", "TICK-104"] if st.session_state["gen"]: rows = ["TICK-100", *rows] df = pd.DataFrame({"ticket": rows}) st.dataframe(df, key="queue", on_select="rerun", selection_mode="single-row") st.dataframe(df, on_select="rerun", selection_mode="single-row") at = AppTest.from_function(script).run() keyed, unkeyed = at.dataframe[0].proto.id, at.dataframe[1].proto.id at.button(key="refresh").click().run() print(keyed == at.dataframe[0].proto.id) # True -> keyed id survives the data change print(unkeyed == at.dataframe[1].proto.id) # False -> unkeyed id does not ``` ### Expected Behavior When the data behind a keyed grid changes, stale selection and edit state should be reset (or the state should be keyed by row identity rather than position), so an app never receives positions computed against a frame it is no longer showing. At minimum the docs for `key=` on `st.dataframe` / `st.data_editor` should say that selection and edit state is positional and survives data changes. ### Current Behavior Positional selection and edit state is preserved across data changes for keyed grids. Dropping `key=` makes the id data-dependent and the stale state orphans to empty, which is safe but discards every pending selection or edit on any data change, and contradicts the general advice to always give widgets a key. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. Not a recent regression, at least. The row retarget in steps 1-4 was observed in Chromium on 1.60.0. The `AppTest` demonstration above prints `True` / `False` on both 1.63.0 and 1.64.0 (the latest release at the time of writing), and the identity code is unchanged at the current tip of `develop`. On 1.60.0 and later the `st.data_editor` case is wider than on 1.59.x: a keyed editor with `num_rows="fixed"` re-applies a pending edit at the same position after a reorder, where 1.59.x discarded it. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.63.0 and 1.64.0, both reproduced - Python version: 3.14.6 - Operating System: Linux Mint 22.3 Zena 64-bit - Browser: Version 152.0.7977.82 (Official Build) for Linux Mint (x86_64) ### Additional Information Related: `_apply_dataframe_edits` ([data_editor.py#L560-L564](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/data_editor.py#L560-L564)) receives no `disabled` argument, so `disabled=["_index"]` is enforced only in the browser; a client-sent index edit is applied server-side. Apps that act on grid state currently have to pin the frame they rendered in `st.session_state`, resolve positions against that frame, and reject anything they did not serve.

issues.title: Allow `st.rerun(scope="fragment")` from parallel fragments during full-app runs
issues.body:
## Current behavior

`st.rerun(scope="fragment")` raises a `StreamlitAPIException` during full-app runs, even when called from within a parallel fragment.

## Why it's disallowed today

The guard in `_new_fragment_id_queue()` (in `lib/streamlit/commands/execution_control.py`) was introduced because the correct behavior was unclear for sequential fragments:

- **Blocking**: Rerunning the fragment immediately blocks subsequent script content from executing — the main thread is stuck in the fragment's while loop.
- **Deferring feels wrong**: Waiting until the full run completes to rerun the fragment defers the `st.rerun()` call in a confusing way.
- **Ignoring scope**: Rerunning the full app ignores the `scope` argument entirely.

## Why parallel fragments change the picture

For `parallel=True` fragments, the first concern doesn't apply — the main thread continues immediately after dispatching the fragment to a worker thread. A local rerun in the worker (re-executing `wrapped_fragment()` via `continue` in the while loop) is self-contained:

- It doesn't block downstream script content
- It doesn't affect sibling fragments
- It doesn't require coordination with the main thread

## Open questions

- **What use cases benefit from this?** Potential examples include polling loops, retry logic, or conditional re-execution within a parallel fragment. If you have a use case for this, please share it in the comments — it will help us prioritize.

## Note

This is a tracking issue for future consideration and not a planned feature extension. The parallel fragments MVP preserves the existing behavior (raising `StreamlitAPIException`).

issues.title: Periodic server-driven data refresh shared across sessions (vs. per-session run_every)
issues.body:
## Summary

Provide a way to refresh a data source on a **server-side schedule** — computed
once for the whole app and pushed to every session currently viewing it —
instead of each session running its own `run_every` timer and recomputing the
same query independently. This is the shared "the dashboard refreshes every
minute and everyone sees the latest" pattern that live/ops dashboards need.

## Why?

`@st.fragment(run_every=…)` already gives time-driven updates, but the timer and
the computation are **per session**: with _N_ viewers on the same dashboard you
get _N_ timers and _N_ executions of the same query every interval. A refresh
that is cheap for one user becomes _N×_ load on the warehouse/API for a shared
internal tool.

`@st.cache_data` dedupes the *computation* across sessions, but nothing *drives*
a periodic refresh or *wakes* the sessions when a new value lands — today
`run_every` is the driver, and it's per session. The missing piece is a refresh
that runs once for the whole app and updates every session viewing it.

## How?

Mark a cached data source to refresh on a fixed interval, centrally for the
whole app. Any fragment that reads it shows the current value and re-renders when
a new one lands.

Sketch (names illustrative):

```python
# The value refreshes centrally every 60s; sessions read the current value and
# rerun when a new one lands — no per-session timer, one shared computation.
@st.cache_data(refresh_every="60s")
def latest_metrics():
    return run_warehouse_query()

@st.fragment
def kpis():
    df = latest_metrics()          # returns the current cached value immediately
    st.metric("Orders", len(df))
    st.line_chart(df, x="ts", y="orders")

kpis()
```

## Additional Context

- Split out from [#12980](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12980)
  ("real-time chart updates without rerunning the entire script"), which is being
  closed now that fragments (`run_every`), `st.rerun(scope=…)`, and element
  diffing cover the original per-session/live-update and flicker concerns.
- Related in-flight work: the non-blocking background execution spec
  ([#17067](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17067)) covers shared,
  off-thread cached computation; scheduled/recurring refresh is called out there
  as not-yet-built.
- Companion gap: a **freshness signal**
  ([#17141](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17141)) — a cheap "did
  the source change?" probe (e.g. Snowflake change-tracking / `LAST_ALTERED` /
  `MAX(updated_at)`) to drive **event-driven** invalidation instead of a blind
  timer. That's the push counterpart to this timer-based one.

issues.title: Freshness signal: refresh cached data only when the source actually changes
issues.body:
## Summary

Let a cached data source declare a cheap "has the source changed?" probe, so
Streamlit re-runs the expensive query (and updates dependent fragments) **only
when the underlying data actually changed** — instead of on a blind timer. This
is the event-driven counterpart to timer-based refresh.

## Why?

Timer-based refresh (`@st.fragment(run_every=…)`, or a server-side scheduled
refresh) fires on a fixed clock regardless of whether anything changed. For an
expensive query that forces a bad tradeoff:

- **Poll fast** → the heavy query re-runs every interval even when the data is
  identical, wasting warehouse/API cost.
- **Poll slow** → users stare at stale data between ticks.

Sources usually expose something *cheap* that reveals whether they changed — a
version token, an ETag, a `MAX(updated_at)`, a Snowflake stream or
change-tracking timestamp. There's no built-in way to poll that cheap signal
often and re-run the expensive work only when it moves.

## How?

Attach a cheap freshness function to a cached data source. Streamlit checks the
freshness token; when it changes, it invalidates the cache and re-runs the
fragments that read it. When it's unchanged, the cached value is served and no
expensive work runs.

Sketch (names illustrative):

```python
def orders_version():
    # Cheap probe — cache invalidates when this value changes.
    return conn.query("SELECT MAX(updated_at) FROM orders")

@st.cache_data(freshness=orders_version)
def load_orders():
    return conn.query("SELECT * FROM orders")   # expensive; runs only on change

@st.fragment(run_every="5s")
def orders_panel():
    df = load_orders()      # cheap probe each poll; heavy query only when changed
    st.line_chart(df, x="ts", y="orders")

orders_panel()
```

issues.title: Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.
5. Compare the input 2 field with the printed `st.session_state.get("input2")` value, then press `r`.

### Expected Behavior

After the registered widget remounts, both the rendered input and `st.session_state["input2"]` are the widget default (empty) on that same run. A follow-up rerun is not required to sync them.

A user key written while the widget had **never** registered remains ordinary session state: delayed first mount (and leftover-key remount after edit/hide) should still adopt that stored value on both sides. `persist_state="session"` / `"page"` (same page) should still remount the last edit.

### Current Behavior

After switching back to A (especially after editing the sibling input 3), the input 2 **field is empty** while `st.session_state.get("input2")` still prints `"input 2"` for that run. A follow-up rerun clears the printed backend as well.

Without the sibling edit, A→B→A can keep UI and backend aligned at `"input 2"`. Either interpretation of leftover keys should keep UI and printed state in sync; the #3512 unmount rule for an already-registered `persist_state=None` widget is that both sides reset in the same run.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: current develop / #17106
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright)

### Additional Information

Found during QA of https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17106#issuecomment-5813147965.

Related:

- #3512 — unmount should reset both the widget UI and the Python value in the same run
- #17093 / #17106 — delayed first mount after a leftover pre-registration user key (out of scope here)
- #12880 — identity-by-key (out of scope)

issues.title: BUG: wrong value returned by backend vs frontend, when a widget is rendered after a previous page run set a default value in session state
issues.body:

- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

If a default value is set in session state on one page run, and then subsequently a widget is rendered with a corresponding `key`, then the default value is not picked up properly and the frontend and backend show different values for that widget.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

# Sets default on first page run
st.session_state.setdefault("foo", 100.0)

if st.toggle("Show"):
    foo = st.number_input("Foo", key="foo")  # Shows 0.00
    st.write("You entered:", foo)  # Shows 100.0
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1.Turn on the  toggle
2. Compare the value in the widget vs the value printed underneath

### Expected Behavior

The value in the widget should match the number reported underneath.

### Current Behavior

The input widget displays `0.00`, but the backend reports `You entered: 100`.

If `r` is pressed to trigger a re-run, then the frontend updates to display `0.0` and the default value is lost.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

This bug is problematic for more complex pages, where widgets may need to be "loaded" or "reset" programmatically, and some widgets may be conditionally hidden depending on a toggle or checkbox.

The bug does not happen if `persist_state="page"` is passed to `number_input`.

Possibly related: #15660 seems to have fixed a similar bug for when persist_state is passed, but not for when persist_state=None.

issues.title: GlobalHotkeys crashes on keydown/keyup events without a key
issues.body:
### Checklist

    - [x] I searched the existing issues and pull requests for this bug.
    - [x] I reproduced this on Streamlit 1.63.0 and confirmed the same unguarded code is present on the current develop branch.

    ### Summary

    The global shortcut handler assumes every dispatched keydown/keyup event has a string key. Browser integrations, test harnesses, embedded hosts, or extensions can dispatch an Event without the KeyboardEvent key field. In that case, GlobalHotkeys calls toLowerCase on undefined and throws an uncaught TypeError.

    ### Minimal reproduction

    Run any Streamlit app, open the browser console after the app loads, and execute:

    ~~~js
    document.dispatchEvent(new Event("keydown"))
    document.dispatchEvent(new Event("keyup"))
    ~~~

    The first event reaches GlobalHotkeys.handleKeyDown and calls normalizeKey(event.key). The second reaches handleKeyUp and does the same. Because Event has no key property, normalizeKey receives undefined and key.toLowerCase() throws.

    A plain DOM Event is intentional here: event listeners can receive synthetic events from browser hosts and integrations despite the TypeScript annotation. The handler should be defensive at this external boundary.

    ### Current implementation

    In frontend/app/src/components/GlobalHotkeys/GlobalHotkeys.tsx:

    ~~~ts
    function normalizeKey(key: string): string {
    return key === "Escape" || key === "Esc" ? "esc" : key.toLowerCase()
    }

    const handleKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent): void => {
    const normalizedKey = normalizeKey(event.key)
    // ...
    }

    const handleKeyUp = (event: KeyboardEvent): void => {
    const normalizedKey = normalizeKey(event.key)
    // ...
    }
    ~~~

    ### Expected behavior

    Malformed or non-keyboard keydown/keyup events without a string key should be ignored without throwing. Normal keyboard shortcuts should continue to work.

    ### Suggested fix

    Guard both handlers before normalization, for example:

    ~~~ts
    if (typeof event.key !== "string") {
    return
    }
    ~~~

    Alternatively, make normalizeKey accept unknown and return undefined for invalid values, with callers returning early.

    ### Regression test

    Add cases in GlobalHotkeys.test.tsx that dispatch keydown and keyup events without key and assert that no exception is thrown and no shortcut callback runs.

    ### Environment

    - Streamlit: 1.63.0
    - Also present on the current develop branch as of 2026-09-22
    - Browser: Chromium

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import sys

import streamlit as st
from streamlit import runtime, session_state
from streamlit.web import cli as stcli

_COUNTER_KEY_SUFFIX = "_counter_value"


@st.fragment
def _render_button_in_dialog(page_key: str) -> None:
    """Fragment: increment button rendered inside the dialog."""
    counter_key = f"{page_key}{_COUNTER_KEY_SUFFIX}"
    st.metric("Count", session_state[counter_key])
    if st.button("➕ Increment", key=f"{page_key}_increment_btn", type="primary"):
        session_state[counter_key] += 1
        st.rerun(scope="fragment")

def _render_button(page_key: str) -> None:

    counter_key = f"{page_key}{_COUNTER_KEY_SUFFIX}"

issues.title: [feature] Add copy="cow" option to st.cache_data
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add an opt-in `copy="cow"` mode to `st.cache_data` that uses copy-on-write semantics for cached return values. This avoids unnecessary full-object deserialization on cache hits while preserving isolation between callers, significantly reducing cache-hit latency and memory allocation for large cached objects.

### Why?

`st.cache_data` currently creates an independent copy of the cached value for each call. This provides isolation between callers, but for large objects such as Pandas DataFrames and NumPy arrays, repeatedly deserializing and copying cached values can introduce significant CPU time and memory allocation overhead.

This becomes particularly relevant for applications where large datasets are read repeatedly across multiple sessions, while mutations to returned values are relatively uncommon.

An opt-in copy-on-write mode can preserve the isolation guarantees of `st.cache_data` while avoiding unnecessary full-object duplication on cache hits. The existing behavior would remain unchanged for applications that do not opt into the new mode.

In benchmarks using Python 3.13.15, Pandas 3.0.6, and Streamlit 1.64.0, the prototype reduced observed cache-hit latency by approximately 2.7–3.2× for DataFrames ranging from 5,000 to 1,000,000 rows. In a separate allocation benchmark with 10 consecutive reads, observed allocation decreased from approximately 4.67 MB to 0.02–0.03 MB.

### How?

Introduce an optional `copy` parameter on `st.cache_data`:

```python
@st.cache_data(copy="cow")
def load_data():
    return pd.read_parquet("large_dataset.parquet")

### Additional Context

### Prototype

A working prototype is available in my fork:

https://github.com/Isllanrx/streamlit/tree/feature/cache-data-cow

The implementation is currently limited to the following areas:

- `st.cache_data` API support for `copy="cow"`
- Copy-on-write handling for supported cached return values
- Caller/session mutation isolation
- Integration with existing cache lifecycle and eviction behavior
- Unit tests for mutation isolation
- Static typing coverage for the public API

### Performance Benchmark

The prototype was benchmarked using Python 3.13.15, Pandas 3.0.6, and Streamlit 1.64.0.

| Dataset | Default copy | `copy="cow"` | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5,000 × 12 | 0.155 ms | 0.055 ms | 2.8× |
| 50,000 × 12 | 0.158 ms | 0.049 ms | 3.2× |
| 200,000 × 12 | 0.144 ms | 0.048 ms | 3.0× |
| 1,000,000 × 12 | 0.131 ms | 0.049 ms | 2.7× |

In a separate allocation benchmark using 10 consecutive cache reads, observed allocation decreased from approximately 4.67 MB with the existing behavior to approximately 0.02–0.03 MB with `copy="cow"`.

### Stress Testing

The implementation was also tested under concurrent mutation and cache lifecycle pressure:

| Scenario | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 50 concurrent threads mutating the same 100,000-row DataFrame | Passed |
| Nested dictionaries containing DataFrames, Series, and lists | Passed |
| 200 concurrent cache entries with `max_entries=5` | Passed |
| Concurrent readers while repeatedly calling `.clear()` | Passed |
| 1,000,000-row (~100 MB) DataFrame with mutation isolation | Passed |

The concurrent mutation test completed in approximately 0.046 seconds. The cached DataFrame remained unchanged and no cross-caller mutations were observed.

The 1,000,000-row test also preserved mutation isolation, with subsequent reads completing in approximately 0.08 ms.

These tests were specifically designed to validate both the performance characteristics and the isolation guarantees of the proposed copy-on-write behavior.

- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When pressing the browser back button, the streamlit script does not reexecute, so elements synced with `st.query_params` do not refresh

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-13853)

```Python
import streamlit as st

num_elements = 10

st.set_page_config(page_title="Mock element Slider", layout="centered")

element_ids = [f"mock-element-{i:02d}" for i in range(num_elements)]
element_to_idx = {element_id: idx for idx, element_id in enumerate(element_ids)}

url_element_id = st.query_params.get("element_id")
if (
    "mock_element_id" not in st.session_state
    or st.session_state["mock_element_id"] not in element_to_idx
):
    st.session_state["mock_element_id"] = (
        url_element_id if url_element_id in element_to_idx else element_ids[0]
    )

with st.container(key="mock-element-slider"):
    st.select_slider(
        "element",
        options=element_ids,
        key="mock_element_id",
        label_visibility="collapsed",
    )

st.query_params["element_id"] = st.session_state["mock_element_id"]

current_element_id = st.session_state["mock_element_id"]
current_idx = element_to_idx[current_element_id]
with st.popover(f"element `{current_element_id}`"):
    st.markdown(f"({current_idx}/{num_elements})")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a streamlit app with the above code, and go to http://localhost:8501/?element_id=mock-element-3
2. Drag the element to mock-element-5
3. Press the browser back button. 

### Expected Behavior

You would expect the slider to go back to mock-element-3

### Current Behavior

The slider stays at mock-element-5

### Summary

Open Telemetry (OTEL) has a [Starlette instrumentation](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-contrib/tree/main/instrumentation/opentelemetry-instrumentation-starlette). Streamlit wraps Starlette via [`st.App`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/server/st.app) (https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7667, https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13600). Therefore, I expect to be able to OTEL monitor Streamlit (at least API if not also UI). Instead, `streamlit run` fails to start with `AttributeError: 'App' object has no attribute 'add_middleware'` where same code works for running via `uvicorn`.

    return JSONResponse({"status": "healthy"})

###

)

StarletteInstrumentor.instrument_app(app)
resource = Resource.create(attributes={"service.name": "starlette-service"})
reader = PeriodicExportingMetricReader(ConsoleMetricExporter())
meterProvider = MeterProvider(resource=resource, metric_readers=[reader])
metrics.set_meter_provider(meterProvider)

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Return `None` when accessing an uninitialized `st.session_state` value instead of raising an exception. This would remove common initialization boilerplate and make nested event data easier to consume.

### Why?

Today, initialization requires:

```python
if "foo" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.foo = 123
```

With a `None` default, this could become:

```python
if not st.session_state.foo:
    st.session_state.foo = 123
```

It could also simplify truly empty selection results for charts and dataframes while still allowing checks such as `if event_data.selection.points`.

### How?

Have missing session-state attributes resolve to `None`. The existing `AttributeDict` may already be close to this behavior; [`addict`](https://github.com/mewwts/addict) could also be useful as an implementation reference or dependency.

### Additional Context

This could be breaking for code that intentionally relies on missing values raising an exception, so compatibility and migration behavior would need careful consideration.

issues.title: Native asyncio support
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit needs native asyncio support.

I would like to point the following:

- asyncio interface is also important for snowflake, so usability or applicability of that should be a no brainer
- all modern databases have async interfaces and they will only expand with time
- streamlit is based on asyncio itself, so at least properly exposing the original tornado's event loop would also not require to much work for you

Known problems for now:
- when using asyncio.run() -> RuntimeError: Event loop is closed if the requests follow concurrently in the tornado eventlets
- every eventlet with own event loop -> tasks are getting to the wrong event loop
- cached event loop for all eventlets through session state -> best for now, gets event loop is closed when multile sessions are acessing the app simultaneously

So with that said, very ugly workaround that I found working best for now:

```python
@st.cache_resource(show_spinner=False)
def get_event_loop():
    loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
    asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)
    return loop


if not st.session_state.get("event_loop"):
    st.session_state["event_loop"] = get_event_loop()
```

then pass that event loop wherever your data is coming from, here is motor example:

```python
async def setup_db(force=False):
    if force or not st.session_state.get("db_client"):
        with st.spinner("Loading..."):
            client = AsyncIOMotorClient(
                os.environ["MONGODB_URI"],
                tls=MONGODB_TLS,
                io_loop=st.session_state["event_loop"],
            )
            st.session_state["db_client"] = await init_database(client=client)
            return client
```
init_database is a call to beanie's init database

I understand that making the entire framework async would require too much work and would prb confuse the ML/AI crowd too much, but streamlit is such a gorgeous framework, the only place it fails in misery is the async


### Why?

Asyncio data technologies should be natively or at least easily accessible from streamlit apps.

### How?

Runs with asyncio.run() should not result to errors.
Concurrent access also should not be broken.
Asyncio loop from tornado app should be available in the scripts.

Handling st.* calls async seems quite unimaginable, but at least the functioning asyncio in the eventlets would give us a lot.

Also async support for on_change and on_click callbacks and caching functions.


### Additional Context

Related issues:
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/744
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8308
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12076

issues.title: Non-script blocking functions for long-running tasks (background execution)
issues.body:
### Problem

Many applications require long-running functions. In many cases, `@st.cache_data` and `@st.cache_resource` will suffice to achieve good performance, but these are not suitable when the inputs to the function change very frequently. 

One common sub-case of this is where the output of the function is important, but not time critical. In this case it would be good to render the page and then "fill-in" the missing parts when the function finishes running.

### Solution

**MVP:** What's the smallest possible solution that would get 80% of the problem out of the way?

I propose a decorator `st.run_in_background` that returns a spinner (like the `st.cache_resource` decorator) while a function is running, but does not block the execution of the application. 

To illustrate the idea:

```python
@st.run_in_background(show_spinner='Generating the plot')
def plot_data(data):
    '''Just an example of a slow function'''
    return sns.pairplot(data)

def get_results(data):
    '''Just an example of a fast function'''
    return 'All good' 

st.title('My app')

selected_data = ... # let's assume this changes a lot, eg. due to interactive filters
results = get_results(selected_data)

fig = plot_data(selected_data ) # This is slow to run
st.pyplot(fig)

st.write(results)
```

In the code above, it'd be great if `st.pyplot` displayed a spinner while `plot_data` is executing (without blocking `st.write(results)`) and then "fill-in" the space with the plot once `plot_data` finishes executing.

**Possible additions:** What are other things that could be added to the MVP over time to make it better?

Smart error handling to turn any operation on a "delayed" object would be very cool.

For example, in this code:

```python
fig = plot_data(data)
fig.update_axes(...) # this would error if fig is not a matplotlib figure, it'd be awesome if streamlit could figure out this is still being loaded without blocking execution
```

### Additional context

Ultimately I'm proposing that streamlit replicate the lazy loading as done in PowerBI (for example)

![image](https://apps.provingground.io/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2020/08/Tracer-OfficeSpaceDash.gif)

Note that every chart is "loading separately" as far as the users are concerned. 


---

### Related Issues

[Joining user threads](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5826)
[Trigger a script re-run from another thread](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/2838)

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

**If you'd like the Streamlit team to prioritize this feature request, please use the 👍 (thumbs up emoji) reaction in response to the initial post.**

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-6687)

issues.title: Support `bind="query-params"` in `st.expander` and `st.tabs`
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add support for `bind="query-params"` in `st.expander` and `st.popover`.

### Why?

I love both the new `bind="query-params"` feature, as well as the new "dynamic" `st.expander` (#13888), `st.tabs` (#13910), and `st.popover` (#13914) feature, and I'd like to use them together.

### How?

Support `bind="query-params"` in `st.expander()`, `st.tabs()`, and `st.popover()`.

### Additional Context

As a workaround for `st.tabs(bind="query-params")`, I have been using `st.segmented_control(bind="query-params")`, but it's not as nice visually.

For a while now, in my app, I hacked together a dynamic expander + query param, using a `st.button`. It works, but it's messy.
```py
from typing import Callable

import streamlit as st


def set_bool_query_param(key: str, value: bool):
    """Set a boolean query parameter in the URL."""
    if value:
        st.query_params[key] = value
    else:
        st.query_params.pop(key, None)


@st.fragment
def dynamic_expander(
    label: str,
    content: Callable,
    *,
    key: str,
    help: str | None = None,  # noqa: A002 Shadowing a Python builtin
):
    """Create an expander that only generates the content if it is expanded.

    Unlike `st.expander()`, which is a frontend component that always generates the content,
    this `dynamic_expander()` only generates the content if it is expanded.
    """
    expanded = key in st.query_params

    button = {
        "label": label,
        "help": help,
        "type": "tertiary",
        "icon": f":material/expand_{'less' if expanded else 'more'}:",
    }

    with st.container(border=True, key=key):
        placeholder = st.empty()
        if expanded:
            placeholder.button(key=f"{key}_button_disabled", disabled=True, **button)

            try:
                with st.spinner("Loading..."):
                    content()
            except Exception as e:
                st.exception(e)

        placeholder.button(
            key=f"{key}_button",
            on_click=set_bool_query_param,
            args=(key, not expanded),
            **button,
        )


def example():
    st.write("Content")


dynamic_expander("Example", example, key="example")
```

issues.title: Server shutdown fails to exit while processing infinite loop
issues.body:
### Summary

Python process does not exit when shutting down the server while processing an infinite loop in a script

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet: (using a recent SessionState prototype, before I fixed the implementation)

```
import streamlit as st

state = st.get_state()
st.write("printed something")
st.write("foobar" in state) # this line infinite looped before I fixed the implementation
```

If applicable, please provide the steps we should take to reproduce the bug:

1. Run the above snippet against the [previous state prototype](https://github.com/AnOctopus/streamlit/tree/c17d119aef34ae1f15f0e7dff5051469d8bb745d) (I ran the react server as a separate process from the dev install of that commit, rather than running them together via a wheel, don't know if that affects this)
2. C-c in the shell running the python server

**Expected behavior:**

Python server stops, process exits and control returns to my shell

**Actual behavior:**

Logs indicate server goes into the STOPPING state and then almost immediately the STOPPED state, but after 20 seconds it still has not exited the process. Sending SIGTERM repeatedly afterwards fails to cause the process to exit, and SIGKILL was required to regain control.

### Is this a regression?

Unknown

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: Session state prototype, as linked above, development install
- Python version: 3.8.6
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex?: Pipenv
- OS version: Arch Linux
- Shell version: Zsh 5.8

issues.title: Widget state is not persisted after adding run_every to a fragment
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

To persist widget values I use the interrupt the widget clean-up process documented [here](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/architecture/widget-behavior#interrupting-the-widget-clean-up-process).
I find this works very well for me, until recently, when I added a fragment with `run_every=2`, and now I notice that the session state is not persisting between pages.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
#!/usr/bin/env python3

import streamlit as st

key = "test_radio"
options = ["option 1", "option 2"]
print(f"State value for {key} is {st.session_state.get(key, 'unset')}")
st.session_state[key] = st.session_state.get(key, options[0]) # Interrupt cleanup, and set a default value for the key
st.radio("Test radio", options=options, key=key)

@st.fragment(run_every=2)
def test_fragment():
    pass

test_fragment() # Commenting this changes the behaviour
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create `main.py` and `pages/1_other_page.py` with the code from "Reproducible Code Example"
2. Launch the app and choose "option 2".
3. Wait 2 seconds then navigate to "Other Page".
4. Observe "option 1" is selected.
5. Choose "option 2" then immediately navigate back to main page, in under 2 seconds
6. Observe "option 2" is selected.

=== Successful variants ===
A. Comment out the `test_fragment()` line and repeat the test. This time you'll observe "option 2" is always selected, as expected.
B. Remove the `run_every` parameter and repeat the test. This time you'll observe "option 2" is always selected, as expected.

### Expected Behavior

The state values associated with widgets should be available at the top of a new page, before streamlit cleanup process begins. In the given example, "option 2" should stay selected when switching between pages.

### Current Behavior

Widget state is being cleared out prematurely.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.43.1
- Python version: 3.10.14
- Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04.1
- Browser: Firefox 136.0.1


### Additional Information

issues.title: `st.metric` docs promise gray for a zero delta but only the literal string `"0"` counts for strings, and the bundled skill's examples are all strings
issues.body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary This is a documentation inconsistency, not a runtime bug. The behavior is by design (#15790, closing #15005), and this report does not ask to change it. It asks for the two places that describe `delta` to match it. The `delta` docstring gives four unqualified rules ([metric.py lines 150-158](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L150-L158)): no arrow for `None` or an empty string, "if the delta is zero, no arrow is shown and the delta is gray", red and down for "a negative number or starts with a minus sign", otherwise green and up. `delta_color="normal"` repeats "gray when zero" ([metric.py line 170](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L170)) and `delta_arrow="auto"` says "no arrow is shown if `delta` is zero" ([metric.py line 269](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L269)). Those rules treat strings as first-class input (the minus-sign branch exists only for strings), so a reader expects a zero-valued string such as `"0%"` or `"+0.0%"` to be "zero". The implementation defines zero for strings as the literal `"0"` only ([metric.py lines 598-604](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L598-L604)), with the comment "other numeric-looking strings (e.g. `"0.0"`, `"0%"`) stay positive". #15790 added that deliberately, on the basis that string deltas are opaque display text, and locked it in with an anti-regression test. The docstring was not updated to say so, which is the gap. The packaged `developing-with-streamlit` skill widens the gap in practice. Every `st.metric` example in it passes `delta` as a pre-formatted string: [dashboards.md line 17](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/dashboards.md?plain=1#L17), [dashboards.md lines 47-49](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/dashboards.md?plain=1#L47-L49), and [data-display.md line 363](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/data-display.md?plain=1#L363). The skill never mentions zero, so it does not contradict anything, but an agent that follows its examples and then reads the docstring's "gray when zero" will format a flat period as `"0%"` and get a green up-arrow. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python For reference only. This shows the designed behavior, not a bug; it is here so the mismatch with the docstring wording can be seen without reading the source. import streamlit as st col1, col2, col3 = st.columns(3) # What the skill's examples lead to for a flat period: col1.metric("Orders (skill style)", "1.4k", "0%") # green up-arrow col2.metric("Orders (skill style)", "1.4k", "-0.0%") # red down-arrow # What actually renders neutral: col3.metric("Orders (numeric)", 1400, 0, delta_description="vs last month") "I.e.:" from streamlit.elements.metric import _is_zero_delta for delta in ["0", "0%", "+0.0%", "-0.0%", 0]: repr(delta), _is_zero_delta(delta) # '0' True # '0%' False # '+0.0%' False # '-0.0%' False # 0 True ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Read the `delta` docstring's "if the delta is zero" rule and `delta_color="normal"`'s "gray when zero". 2. `streamlit run` or `uv run streamlit run` the snippet. 3. Compare the first two tiles with the third / see the debug output beneath it. ### Expected Behavior Documentation that states the actual rule: 1. In the `delta` docstring (and the `delta_color` / `delta_arrow` mentions of zero), say that a string delta is displayed as-is and that only the literal string `"0"` is treated as zero; other zero-like strings follow the sign rule (leading minus is negative, anything else is positive). One sentence is enough. 2. In the packaged skill, either show at least one example with a numeric `delta` and qualifier text in `delta_description=`, or add a one-line note next to the string examples that string deltas are never treated as zero. ### Current Behavior The docstring says zero deltas are gray with no qualification about strings. `"0%"` renders as a positive delta with a green up-arrow and `"-0.0%"` as a negative delta with a red down-arrow, which is the designed behavior. The skill's examples are all strings and say nothing about zero. For at-a-glance reference: ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. Not a regression and not a behavior change request. Verified on 1.63.0 and 1.64.0 (the latest release at the time of writing): the docstring text, the skill examples, and `_is_zero_delta` are identical in both, and unchanged at the current tip of `develop`. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.63.0 and 1.64.0, both reproduced - Python version: 3.14.6 - Operating System: Linux Mint 22.3 Zena 64-bit - Browser: Version 152.0.7977.82 (Official Build) for Linux Mint (x86_64) ### Additional Information The behavior was settled in #15790: the PR description lists an anti-regression test that `"0.0"`, `"+0"` and `"0%"` "stay green/up", and review confirmed the numbers-versus-strings split as intended. Nothing here asks to reopen that; it asks for the docstring and the skill to describe it. `format=` is not a way around the string question: it is one format applied to both `value` and `delta`, and `"percent"` multiplies by 100, so a tile whose value is a count and whose delta is a percent change cannot be served by a single `format=`. Numeric `delta` plus `delta_description=` is the pattern that works, and it is the one the skill could show.

issues.title: st.data_editor NumberColumn: typing a value starting with "." (no leading zero) drops the decimal point and reads digits as a whole number
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a NumberColumn cell is selected and you type a value that starts with `.` (e.g. `.01`), the `.` is silently dropped and the remaining digits are committed as a whole number — `.01` becomes `1`, `.07` becomes `7`. Typing the same value with a leading zero (`0.01`) works correctly, and **pasting** `.01` into the cell also works correctly. So this is specific to the character-by-character typed-entry path.

Impact
This is a real-world data-entry trap: any user in the habit of typing .01-style shorthand (common for percentage/margin fields) silently enters a value the cell just shows a plausible-looking wrong number.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st
df = pd.DataFrame({"Customer": ["A", "B"], "Margin": [12.0, 8.0]})
st.data_editor(
    df,
    column_config={
        "Margin": st.column_config.NumberColumn("Margin", format="%.4f", step=0.0001),
    },
)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Click the Margin cell for row A (shows 12.0000).
Type .07 (as literal keystrokes: ., 0, 7).
Press Enter.



### Expected Behavior

Expected: cell shows 0.0700.


### Current Behavior

Actual: cell shows 7.0000.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

Streamlit version: 1.61.1
Python version: 3.12/3.14
Browser: Chrome
OS: Windows


### Additional Information

Unable to drag to copy a value from one cell to a range of cells in the rightmost column of st.data_editor, as the selection handle is underneath the data_editor scrollbar, so when the click and drag happens you just interact with the scrollbar and jump to a different point in the data_editor instead of dragging a selection

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Placing `st.chat_input` inside `st.bottom` causes an otherwise non-chat page to scroll to the bottom immediately on initial load, without any user interaction or chat messages. This hides the heading and initial content when using the bottom container for a persistent assistant alongside a dashboard. Replacing only `st.chat_input` with `st.text_input` prevents the unsolicited scrolling.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.title("Dashboard heading")
for number in range(30):
    st.write(f"Dashboard row {number}")

with st.bottom:
    st.chat_input("Ask about the dashboard")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install `streamlit==1.63.0` and run the example with `streamlit run app.py`.
2. Open a fresh browser tab/context with a viewport around 1280 x 720, so the main content exceeds the viewport height.
3. Do not click, type, or scroll. Wait for rendering to settle.
4. Observe that the main page has scrolled to the bottom and the dashboard heading is offscreen.
5. As a control, replace `st.chat_input` with `st.text_input`, restart/reload in a fresh browser context, and observe that the page stays at the top.

No custom CSS, JavaScript, Snowflake connection, fragments, tabs, navigation, or third-party component is needed to reproduce this.

### Expected Behavior

An initial dashboard load should remain at the top. A bottom-docked input should not make non-chat content above it auto-scroll before any conversation exists. If automatic scrolling is intentional for chat-first apps, an opt-out for this mixed dashboard/assistant use case would be helpful.


### Current Behavior

The page scrolls to the bottom on its own. In three fresh Chrome contexts per variant, measured after rendering settled at a 1280 x 720 viewport:

| Bottom widget | Main scrollTop | Main scrollHeight | Main clientHeight |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `st.chat_input` (all 3 runs) | 843 | 1563 | 720 |
| `st.text_input` (all 3 control runs) | 0 | 1573 | 720 |

The scroll position was read from the main scrollable section (`section.stMain`), not `window.scrollY`. No Streamlit exception was displayed. Measurements used Playwright with installed Chrome in headless mode; the same symptom was first noticed in interactive Chrome in a larger app.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Python version: 3.14.3
- Operating System: macOS 26.6, ARM64
- Browser: Google Chrome 152.0.7977.83
- Deployment: local `streamlit run`, default theme for the minimal example

issues.title: Add `max_stale` parameter to `refresh_mode="background"` for configurable stale grace window
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the existing issues for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

When using `refresh_mode="background"` on `st.cache_data` / `st.cache_resource`, the stale grace window is fixed at 1×TTL (hard expiry at 2×TTL). This means an app idle overnight (longer than 2×TTL) has its cache evicted and the first morning user blocks on a cold miss.

A `max_stale` parameter would let users configure the stale grace window independently from TTL:

```python
@st.cache_data(ttl="2m", max_stale="12h", refresh_mode="background")
def load_data():
    return expensive_query()
```

This separates two concerns: **how often to refresh** (`ttl="2m"`) from **how long stale data is acceptable** (`max_stale="12h"`). Users who want frequent freshness checks but never want to block get exactly that.

### Why?

From [#11050](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11050) (comment by @itsToggle):

> Is there any way that we can influence the "2 × ttl" background cache timeout? In my use case I want a short ttl so the values are updated often, but I never want my users to have to wait for a response. I would like to set the ttl to something like 2 minutes, but the oldest background cache that's allowed to be served can be much older than four minutes.

This is also the more practical solution for the "first user of the day" problem compared to cron scheduling, since it does not require an always-on server and works on scale-to-zero deployments.

### How?

The [background refresh spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/specs/2026-04-08-cache-background-refresh/product-spec.md) already calls this out as future work:

> **`max_stale` parameter**: Explicitly configure the stale grace window (default: equal to `ttl`), e.g. `ttl="1h", max_stale="12h"` to serve stale data across an overnight idle gap without blocking the first morning user

### Additional Context

- Related (closed): [#5871](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5871), [#11050](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11050)

issues.title: Typeahead/autocomplete (async) st.selectbox / st.text_input widget
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

This would be a standard typeahead/autocomplete text input. Imagine the `st.selectbox` widget, but instead of showing a list of static elements the dropdown, the options are queried from a backend service based on the user's text input. As the user types in characters, the options in the dropdown menu are updated.

### Why?

Often times I want to allow a user to select from a large list of options  (>1k). Depending on the data size, it's prohibitive to load all those options into memory at once and display them. Even if the data size of the options is less than the Streamlit memory limit, it often significantly slows down the responsiveness of my Streamlit app.

The standard solution for this in web applications is to wait for the user to begin typing some minimum number of characters, and then query a backend data source with the user's input filter applied. This narrows down the available options and limits the load on the network and browser memory.

It would be great if Streamlit had a native widget similar to `st.selectbox` where the datasource for `options` could be a backend query/api call and the `on_change` handler would trigger it and load new options.

### How?

This functionality would be a bit of a departure from the standard Streamlit runtime model, because it would require rerunning a specific function, and not the entire Streamlit script. Until there is some solution for that in place, I don't really think this feature I'm asking for is feasible.

Assuming the ability to do a partial rerun is adopted into Streamlit, then I could imagine a modification to `st.selectbox` would work, where the `options` could be a function call to some backend service (either an api or a database query) that would return an array. Then the `on_change` function would trigger the call to get new options.

### Additional Context

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When using `st.query_params` to modify the current URL, new items are added to the browser history so one can navigate forwards and backwards to the URLs that have previously been set.

- On using the forwards and backwards buttons in the browser, the URL changes as expected, but calls to `st.query_params` see only the final version of the URL.
    - This only happens if `st.navigation` is used - if the app is single-page, the forwards and backwards buttons don't trigger a rerun of the back end at all (as in #13853). 
- If the user navigates to a different page, the forwards and backwards buttons DO cause the `st.query_params` to change.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import datetime

import streamlit as st

def page():
    st.write(datetime.datetime.now())

    if st.button("Increment Query Param"):
        value = int(st.query_params.get("value", "0"))
        st.query_params["value"] = value + 1

    st.write(st.query_params)

st.navigation([
    st.Page(page, title="Query Params", default=True),
    st.Page(lambda: None, title="Other Page", url_path="other"),
]).run()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open the app URL in a browser
2. Press the "Increment Query Param" button twice - the URL should now end `?value=2`
3. Press the browser's back button
4. Press the browser's forwards button
5. Click on "Other Page" in the nav bar
6. Press the browser's back button
7. Press the browser's back button again

### Expected Behavior

1. The URL has no query parameters and the printed `st.query_params` are empty
2. The URL ends with `?value=2` and the printed `st.query_params` shows `"value": "2"`
3. The URL ends with `?value=1` and the printed `st.query_params` shows `"value": "1"`
4. The URL ends with `?value=2` and the printed `st.query_params` shows `"value": "2"`
5. The URL has no query parameters, no content is shown
6. The URL ends with `?value=2` and the printed `st.query_params` shows `"value": "2"`
7. The URL ends with `?value=1` and the printed `st.query_params` shows `"value": "1"`

### Current Behavior

After step 3: the printed `st.query_params` shows `"value": "2"` (the timestamp and URL do update, but the `st.query_params` appear to be cached)

Notes:
- after steps 5 and 6 (navigate to a different page and back), step 7 (apparently identical to step 3) works as expected
- replacing step 5 with "navigate to an external site" also makes step 7 work, albeit now in a new session

### Is this a regression?

issues.title: Unsafe `shell=True` grep interpolates snapshot filenames in `scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py`
issues.body:
**Description**

`scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py` builds a `grep` command by interpolating snapshot
filenames from the working tree into a shell string that is then executed with
`shell=True`, so shell metacharacters in committed snapshot filenames execute
arbitrary commands when the script is run.

In `scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py` (lines 225-228):

```python
cmd = f'grep -r --include="*.py" "{snapshot_name}" e2e_playwright/'
result = subprocess.run(
    cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
)
```

The `snapshot_name` is derived from on-disk filenames (lines 288-311):

```python
for dirpath, _, filenames in os.walk(snapshot_root):  # e2e_playwright/__snapshots__/linux
    for filename in filenames:
        if filename.endswith(".png"):
            all_snapshot_files.append(os.path.join(dirpath, filename))
...
snapshot_name = re.sub(r"\[.*\]\.png$", "", filename)
```

`filename` comes straight from the repository working tree (the snapshot PNGs
are committed to git), so anyone whose snapshot file gets merged controls part
of the command string. Because the value is placed inside double quotes,
`/bin/sh` still interprets `"`, `;`, `|`, `$()` and backticks — for example a
file named `st_button"; touch /tmp/pwned; "[chromium].png` is reduced to the
snapshot name `st_button"; touch /tmp/pwned; "` and produces

    grep -r --include="*.py" "st_button"; touch /tmp/pwned; "" e2e_playwright/

which runs `touch /tmp/pwned` as a separate command. The remaining grep then
searches for the same injected string, keeping the script's normal flow intact.

**Trigger scenario**

1. A PR adds (or renames) a snapshot file under
   `e2e_playwright/__snapshots__/linux/` with a filename containing shell
   metacharacters (the name is visible in the diff, but its effect is easy to
   miss in review).
2. The PR is merged.
3. A maintainer runs `python scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py` locally, or CI runs
   it in `--ci` mode — both paths execute the grep above.
4. The injected command executes in the maintainer's environment / CI runner.

**Impact**

Arbitrary command execution in the environment of whoever runs the cleanup
script. In practice the attacker already needs write access to the repository
(a merged PR), so I'd class this as a hardening issue rather than a security
vulnerability — which is why I'm opening a regular issue instead of using a
security channel. Still, it's an easy footgun to eliminate: the `find` call a
few lines above (lines 157-160) also uses `shell=True` (its string is static,
so it is harmless, but it could be cleaned up in the same pass).

**Suggested fix**

Drop the shell entirely and pass an argument list, keeping `--` to avoid
option injection:

```python
result = subprocess.run(
    ["grep", "-r", "--include=*.py", "--", snapshot_name, "e2e_playwright/"],
    capture_output=True, text=True, check=False,
)
```

Optionally validate the name as defense in depth, e.g.
`re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+", snapshot_name)` (or use `shlex.quote()` if a
shell must be kept).

I'd be happy to open a PR switching both `shell=True` call sites to the
argument-list form if that's welcome. Thanks for maintaining a great project!

issues.title: Add server-side (callable) input validation to `st.text_input`
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Extend the existing `validate` parameter of `st.text_input` to also accept a **callable** for server-side validation, executed on the backend when the value is submitted. When validation fails, the input shows an error state with a message and the value is **not** committed (no rerun). Client-side regex validation (`str` / `(regex, message)` tuple) is already implemented and shipped; this issue tracks the remaining **server-side** part of the approved [product spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/specs/2025-12-03-text-input-validation/product-spec.md).

### Why?

Client-side regex validation gives instant feedback but can be bypassed and can't express checks that need backend resources (e.g. database lookups) or must be secure. Server-side callable validation covers those cases — username availability, complex business logic, and security-sensitive validation — without the developer having to manually track/display errors or trigger extra reruns.

### How?

Widen the `validate` type to also accept a callable:

```python
st.text_input(
    ...,
    validate: str | tuple[str, str] | Callable[[str], bool | str] | None = None,
    #                                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ NEW (callable)
)
```

The callable is executed on the backend on submit (Enter/blur/form submit) via a deferred-execution pattern (like `st.download_button` with callable data), without a full rerun. It returns `True` (valid), `False` (generic error), or a `str` (custom error message):

```python
def check_username(value: str) -> bool | str:
    if len(value) < 3:
        return "Username must be at least 3 characters."
    if db.username_exists(value):
        return "Username already taken."
    return True

st.text_input("Username", validate=check_username)
```

Key behaviors (from the spec):
- Runs on commit (blur/Enter/form submit), not on initial render; error state clears as the user types.
- Empty string / `None` bypasses validation (requiredness stays a separate future `required` parameter).
- On success: the deferred commit goes through and triggers the normal rerun / `on_change`. On failure: error state, no rerun.
- While validating: loading spinner, submit disabled, 10s timeout, in-progress validation cancelled if the user edits the value.
- Non-`bool`/`str` return or a raised exception → value rejected with a generic error; exception + traceback logged to the backend console (not sent to the frontend).
- Forms: validation runs on form submit (client-side regex first, then callables); all fields must pass before the single submit rerun.

### Additional Context

- Approved product spec: [`specs/2025-12-03-text-input-validation/product-spec.md`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/specs/2025-12-03-text-input-validation/product-spec.md) (client-side portion already shipped; this issue covers the server-side callable).
- Future extensions noted in the spec: server-side callable validation for `st.text_area`, `st.column_config.TextColumn`, `st.number_input`, `st.date_input`, `st.selectbox`, and `st.chat_input`.

If the cursor is hovering over a chart data point while the rerender is in progress and a Bokeh hover tooltip is visible, the tooltip remains rendered on the screen after the rerender completes. The hover overlay becomes detached from the chart lifecycle and persists across page transitions. The artifact remains visible even when navigating to different Streamlit pages. The issue disappears only after performing a full browser hard refresh (Ctrl + F5 / Ctrl + Shift + R). ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import streamlit as st import numpy as np import pandas as pd from bokeh.plotting import figure from bokeh.models import ColumnDataSource, HoverTool, Span from bokeh.layouts import gridplot from bokeh.models import CustomJS from streamlit_bokeh import streamlit_bokeh st.set_page_config(layout="wide") st.title("Sales by Country (Hourly Data - 10,000 Points) - Shared Crosshair Pointer") # ── Generate data ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── np.random.seed(42) timestamps = pd.date_range(start="2015-01-01", periods=10000, freq="H") years = np.arange(len(timestamps)) n_years = len(years) countries = ["USA", "Germany", "France", "Japan", "Canada", "UK", "India", "Brazil"] colors = ["navy", "firebrick", "green", "purple", "orange", "brown", "pink", "cyan"] # ── Build ColumnDataSource ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── data = { "hour_index": years_filtered, "timestamp": timestamps_filtered.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M").values, } for country in countries: base_sales = np.random.uniform(50, 500) growth = np.random.uniform(1.001, 1.002) sales = base_sales * (growth ** np.arange(n_years)) sales += np.random.normal(0, 20, n_years) data[country] = sales[year_mask] source = ColumnDataSource(data) # ── Build individual plots ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── plots = [] vline_sources = [] hline_sources = [] for idx, country in enumerate(countries): p = figure( title=f"{country} Sales Trend", width=350, height=280, toolbar_location="right", tools="pan,wheel_zoom,box_zoom,reset,save", ) p.line( x="hour_index", y=country, source=source, line_width=3, color=colors[idx], legend_label=country, name=country, ) p.scatter( x="hour_index", y=country, source=source, size=8, color=colors[idx], alpha=0.7, legend_label=country, ) # ── HoverTool kept for data access but tooltip div hidden via CSS ───────── tooltips = [("Timestamp", "@timestamp"), ("Hour", "@hour_index")] for c in countries: tooltips.append((c, f"@{c}{{$0,0.00}}")) p.add_tools(HoverTool(tooltips=tooltips)) vline = Span(location=0, dimension="height", line_color="red", line_dash="dashed", line_width=2, line_alpha=0.6) hline = Span(location=0, dimension="width", line_color="blue", line_dash="dotted", line_width=1.5, line_alpha=0.5) p.add_layout(vline) p.add_layout(hline) vline_sources.append(vline) hline_sources.append(hline) p.legend.location = "center_right" p.legend.click_policy = "hide" p.legend.label_text_font_size = "8pt" p.legend.glyph_height = 10 p.legend.glyph_width = 15 p.legend.spacing = 2 p.legend.padding = 5 p.add_layout(p.legend[0], "right") p.xaxis.axis_label = "Hour Index" p.yaxis.axis_label = "Sales ($M)" p.title.text_font_size = "13pt" plots.append(p) # ── JS that runs inside Bokeh's shadow DOM ──────────────────────────────────── # Injected once on document_ready: hides ALL .bk-Tooltip elements permanently # via a stylesheet scoped to the shadow root. This is the only JS context that # can reach inside Bokeh's shadow DOM — st.markdown scripts cannot. HIDE_TOOLTIP_CSS_JS = """ const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas'); const root = canvas ? canvas.getRootNode() : document; if (root && !root._bkTooltipHidden) { root._bkTooltipHidden = true; const style = document.createElement('style'); style.textContent = '.bk-Tooltip { display: none !important; visibility: hidden !important; }'; (root.head || root).appendChild(style); } """ CROSSHAIR_JS = """ const x = cb_obj.x; for (let i = 0; i < vlines.length; i++) { vlines[i].location = x; } const hours = source.data['hour_index']; let closest_idx = 0; let min_dist = Math.abs(hours[0] - x); for (let i = 1; i < hours.length; i++) { const dist = Math.abs(hours[i] - x); if (dist < min_dist) { min_dist = dist; closest_idx = i; } } for (let i = 0; i < countries.length; i++) { hlines[i].location = source.data[countries[i]][closest_idx]; } """ for p in plots: # Hide tooltip via shadow-DOM CSS on load p.js_on_event("document_ready", CustomJS(code=HIDE_TOOLTIP_CSS_JS)) # Shared crosshair p.js_on_event( "mousemove", CustomJS( args=dict(vlines=vline_sources, hlines=hline_sources, source=source, countries=countries), code=CROSSHAIR_JS, ), ) # ── Grid layout ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── grid = gridplot([plots[0:4], plots[4:8]], toolbar_location=None) streamlit_bokeh(grid, use_container_width=True, theme="streamlit", key="bokeh_sales_grid") # ── Data table ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── st.subheader("Sales Data") st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame(data), use_container_width=True) ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. install libraries 2. run the main.py (or however you named file) 3. chaneg slicer value and while page is reloading quicly point onto any dot in graph 4. the hover shoud be stacked on left side after the reload finishes ### Expected Behavior No stucked hover woud appear ### Current Behavior Hover stacked on left side of the page remain on page and even on other pages if you create them.
