issues.title: Timeout on Android Chrome Browser for st.file_uploader, cant upload file
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The st.file_uploader widget **on mobile phones** exhibits a timeout issue specifically when tested on Android using the Chrome browser. If there is a delay (e.g., around 15 seconds) after opening a file selection application and before selecting a file, the widget fails to upload properly. The issue can be reproduced using the example provided in the official documentation:
[Streamlit File Uploader Documentation](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.file_uploader).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# use official demo
# https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.file_uploader

import streamlit as st

uploaded_files = st.file_uploader(
    "Choose a CSV file", accept_multiple_files=True
)
for uploaded_file in uploaded_files:
    bytes_data = uploaded_file.read()
    st.write("filename:", uploaded_file.name)
```

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-11419)

### Steps To Reproduce

- Open a mobile browser on an Android device (tested with Chrome).
- Visit the official Streamlit documentation for st.file_uploader:
- [URL: https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.file_uploader](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.file_uploader).
- Scroll down to the example for st.file_uploader.
- On the widget, click the "Browse files" button, which prompts Android to ask which application to use.
- Select any file management app (e.g., Samsung's File Browser) but **wait for 15 seconds** before choosing a file.
- Select a file from the file manager app and confirm.

### Expected Behavior

On mobile phone, after selecting the file in the file manager app, the uploaded file name should appear in the Streamlit app, as expected.

### Current Behavior

- On mobile phone, when waiting 15 seconds before selecting the file, the Streamlit app shows "connecting" after selecting the file and then fails to display the uploaded file name.
- On mobile phone, if a file is selected immediately without delay, the widget works as expected, file name is displayed, and no timeout occurs.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Device: Samsung S24
- OS: Android 15.0
- Browser: Chrome 136.0.7103.125
- Python version: 3.10
- Streamlit Version: 1.45.0
- Internet Connection: Stable WiFi during testing.


### Additional Information

- This issue seems time-sensitive and suggests a possible timeout behavior when Android switches between File Manager App and the Browser.
- No issues observed on desktop browsers with the same testing process.

issues.title: [Bug] st.dataframe() / st.table() silently kill WebSocket when DataFrame has non-ASCII column names + emoji data (no traceback, session loss)
issues.body:
## Summary

`st.dataframe()` and `st.table()` silently close the WebSocket connection when the DataFrame contains **non-ASCII column names** (e.g. `ç`, `ê`, `/`) **combined with emoji in cell data**. No Python exception is raised, no error appears in the terminal — the browser simply reconnects with a brand-new session, wiping `st.session_state` entirely.

This is one of the hardest bugs to debug in Streamlit because it produces **zero tracebacks** and presents itself as an unrelated UX problem ("users keep getting logged out").

---

## Versions

| Package | Version |
|---|---|
| streamlit | 1.41.0 |
| pandas | 2.2.3 |
| Python | 3.11 |
| OS | Linux (Docker, python:3.11-slim) |

---

## Minimal Reproduction

```python
# app.py
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# This persists fine
if "logged_in" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["logged_in"] = False

if not st.session_state["logged_in"]:
    if st.button("Login"):
        st.session_state["logged_in"] = True
        st.rerun()
    st.stop()

st.write("✅ Logged in — session_state alive")

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Serviço": ["Manutenção Website", "Hospedagem"],   # ← non-ASCII column name (cedilha)
    "Valor/mês": ["R$ 100,00", "R$ 200,00"],           # ← non-ASCII + slash in column name  
    "Status": ["🟢 Ativo", "🔴 Pausado"],              # ← emoji in cell data
})

st.dataframe(df)   # 💥 WebSocket dies here — no exception raised
st.write("This line never renders — session is already dead")
```

Run with Docker:

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install streamlit==1.41.0 pandas==2.2.3
COPY app.py .
ENTRYPOINT ["streamlit", "run", "app.py", "--server.headless=true", "--server.fileWatcherType=none"]
```

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Build and run the container
2. Open `http://localhost:8501`
3. Click "Login" → session is alive (`session_state["logged_in"] = True`)
4. `st.dataframe(df)` renders (or tries to)
5. Browser reconnects → `session_state` is empty → "Login" button appears again

---

## Observed Behavior

- `st.dataframe(df)` call executes without raising any Python exception
- The line after `st.dataframe()` **never executes** (confirmed via `print()` to stdout)
- Browser-side: WebSocket closes and immediately reconnects with a fresh session
- `st.session_state` is wiped clean — any auth/navigation state is lost
- **Identical behavior with `st.table(df)`** — same root cause

### Diagnostic method that revealed the bug

Since no traceback is produced, the only way to isolate it was:

1. Store a UUID in `session_state` on first load: `st.session_state["sid"] = uuid4()`
2. Display it on every render: `st.caption(f"sid: {st.session_state['sid']}")`
3. Add `print()` statements throughout the render function (visible in Docker logs)
4. The `print()` output stopped exactly at the `st.dataframe()` call
5. The displayed `sid` changed to a new value on the next render → confirmed new WebSocket session

---

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The bug appears to occur during **Arrow/protobuf serialization** of the DataFrame when:
- Column names contain multi-byte UTF-8 characters (`ç` = U+00E7, `ê` = U+00EA, `/` combined with accented chars)
- AND cell data contains 4-byte Unicode emoji (`🟢` = U+1F7E2, `🔴` = U+1F534)

The serialization fails at the **protocol level** (WebSocket frame), not at the Python level. The exception is caught internally by Streamlit/PyArrow and manifests as a connection close rather than an error message.

The bug does **not** occur when:
- Column names are ASCII-only
- Cell data has no emoji
- `st.write(df.to_dict(orient="records"))` is used instead (routes through JSON, not Arrow)

---

## Workaround

Replace `st.dataframe()` / `st.table()` with a **GFM markdown table** rendered via `st.markdown()`:

```python
def _esc(v) -> str:
    """Escape pipe to prevent breaking markdown table structure."""
    return str(v).replace("|", "\\|")

lines = [
    "| Servico | Valor_mes | Status |",
    "|---|---|---|",
]
for _, row in df.iterrows():
    lines.append(f"| {_esc(row['Serviço'])} | {_esc(row['Valor/mês'])} | {row['Status']} |")

st.markdown("\n".join(lines))
```

This bypasses the Arrow serialization layer entirely.

---

## Expected Behavior

- `st.dataframe()` should either render the DataFrame correctly OR raise a visible Python exception / display an in-app error
- The WebSocket connection should **never** be closed silently due to a data rendering issue
- If Arrow serialization fails, Streamlit should fall back to a JSON/HTML representation rather than terminating the session

---

## Additional Notes

- `fileWatcherType = "none"` was confirmed active — rules out hot-reload as the cause
- The Docker container did **not** restart (verified via log message count)
- The bug is **100% reproducible** in the described environment
- Changing column names to ASCII-only (`Servico`, `Valor_mes`) likely resolves the Arrow schema issue

Would appreciate confirmation of the root cause and whether a fix is planned for 1.41.x or 1.42.0.

issues.title: Tick styling inconsistent in `st.bokeh_chart()` vs `streamlit_bokeh()` for caliber theme
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`streamlit_bokeh` fails to generate correct axes using the caliber theme after setting the plot background and border colors.  The tick styling fails to output ticks of the requested color.  Legacy `st.bokeh_chart()` renders the ticks as expected.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# See: https://github.com/pr3d4t0r/SSScoring/blob/master/LICENSE.txtl

# Streamlit Bokeh bug report runner


import bokeh.models as bm
import bokeh.plotting as bp
import streamlit as st

backgroundColorName='#2c2c2c'
colorName = 'lightsteelblue'
THEME='caliber'
x = [ x for x in range(1,6) ]
y = [ 6, 7, 6, 4, 5, ]


def BUG_st_bokeh():
    # REQUIRES: pip install streamlit_bokeh
    from streamlit_bokeh import streamlit_bokeh

    plot = bp.figure(
                title='TICK MARKS MISSING - theme: %s' % THEME,
                width=500,
                height=300,
                background_fill_color=backgroundColorName,
                border_fill_color=backgroundColorName,
    )
    plot.title.text_font = 'Arial'
    plot.title.text_color = 'red'
    plot.xaxis.axis_label_text_color=colorName
    plot.xaxis.major_label_text_color=colorName
    plot.xaxis.axis_line_color=colorName
    plot.xaxis.major_tick_line_color=colorName
    plot.xaxis.minor_tick_line_color=colorName
    plot.yaxis.axis_label_text_color=colorName
    plot.yaxis.major_label_text_color=colorName
    plot.yaxis.axis_line_color=colorName
    plot.yaxis.major_tick_line_color=colorName
    plot.yaxis.minor_tick_line_color=colorName
    plot.line(x, y, line_color='orange')
    linearAxis = bm.LinearAxis(
            axis_label_text_color = colorName,
            axis_line_color = colorName,
            major_label_text_color = colorName,
            axis_label = 'Foo',
            major_tick_line_color='yellow',
            minor_tick_line_color='yellow',
            y_range_name = 'Bar'
    )
    plot.extra_y_ranges = { 'Bar': bm.Range1d(start = 0, end = 10) }
    plot.add_layout(linearAxis, 'left')
    streamlit_bokeh(plot, use_container_width=False, theme=THEME)


def WORKS_st_bokeh_chart():
    # REQUIRES: pip install bokeh==2.4.3
    import bokeh.io as bi

    bi.curdoc.theme = THEME
    plot = bp.figure(
                title='TICK MARKS SHOW - theme: %s' % THEME,
                width=500,
                height=300,
                background_fill_color=backgroundColorName,
                border_fill_color=backgroundColorName,
    )
    plot.title.text_font = 'Arial'
    plot.title.text_color = colorName
    plot.xaxis.axis_label_text_color=colorName
    plot.xaxis.major_label_text_color=colorName
    plot.xaxis.axis_line_color=colorName
    plot.xaxis.major_tick_line_color=colorName
    plot.xaxis.minor_tick_line_color=colorName
    plot.yaxis.axis_label_text_color=colorName
    plot.yaxis.major_label_text_color=colorName
    plot.yaxis.axis_line_color=colorName
    plot.yaxis.major_tick_line_color=colorName
    plot.yaxis.minor_tick_line_color=colorName
    plot.line(x, y, line_color='orange')
    linearAxis = bm.LinearAxis(
            axis_label_text_color = colorName,
            axis_line_color = colorName,
            major_label_text_color = colorName,
            axis_label = 'Foo',
            major_tick_line_color='yellow',
            minor_tick_line_color='yellow',
            y_range_name = 'Bar'
    )
    plot.extra_y_ranges = { 'Bar': bm.Range1d(start = 0, end = 10) }
    plot.add_layout(linearAxis, 'left')
    st.bokeh_chart(plot, use_container_width=False)


if '__main__' == __name__:
    WORKS_st_bokeh_chart()
    # BUG_st_bokeh()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Save the reproducible code example as buggy.py
2. Ensure that `bokeh==2.4.3` is installed and that `streamlit_bokeh` is not present in the current environment
3. `streamlit run buggy.py` - This code uses `st.bokeh_chart()` and renders the ticks for the x, y, and extra y axes/ranges
4. Close the browser and `Ctrl-C` to exit `streamlit`
5. Go to line 95 of the reproducible example and comment out `# WORKS_st_bokeh_chart()`
6. Go to line 96 of the reproducible example and enable `BUG_st_bokeh()`
7. Install `streamlit_bokeh` and its dependencies
8. `streamlit run buggy.py` - This code uses `streamlit_bokeh()` and fails to render ticks for the x, y, and extra y axes/ranges.  Inspecting the output shows that the ticks are present in a dark grey color, unaffected by rendeding settings in `bm.LinearAxis` construction and `bp.plot` instance configuration.

The implementations of `WORKS_st_bokeh_chart()` and `BUG_st_bokeh()` are identical (check with `diff -y` if needed).

### Expected Behavior

Plots rendered using the caliber theme feature tick marks along the axes.  When using `st.bokeh_chart()` and Bokeh 2.4.3 (legacy) the plots render the tick marks for the main axes and for any extra X or Y ranges and axes.


### Current Behavior

`streamlit_bokeh` fails to generate correct axes using the caliber theme after setting the plot background and border colors.  The tick styling fails to output ticks of the requested color.  Legacy `st.bokeh_chart()` renders the ticks as expected.

Compare the output from both function calls (legacy `st.bokeh_chart()` vs `streamlit_bokeh()` generated by identical code.  This must be executed to experience the differences.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.45.1
- Python version: 3.13.3, others prior
- Operating System: macOS 15.4.1
- Browser: Firefox, Safari, LibreWolf, Brave

All browsers run at their latest available GA version.

_No response_

### Summary

The streamlit module reloading has race conditions that lead to "KeyError: 'mylib'" from deep inside python import machinery. It has been mentioned in passing in other issues before but here I'm making it reproducible.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
A single code example is not enough to reproduce, but I managed to create a stress test setup that should reproduce the issue quickly by simulating editing files in the background with randomized timing while streamlit is trying to keep up with hotreloading.
```

1. Go to https://github.com/martinal/streamlit-stresstest
2. Download repo
3. Run stress test per the repo README

No exceptions.

### Current Behavior

```
────────────────────────── Traceback (most recent call last) ───────────────────────────
  /.../streamlit-stresstest/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py:565 in _run_script                                        
                                                                                        
  /.../streamlit-stresstest/main.py:5 in <module>                                   

...                                                                                        
  ❱  5 import mylib                                                                     
...

  in _find_and_load:1027                                                                
  in _find_and_load_unlocked:1006                                                       
  in _load_unlocked:699                                                                 
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
KeyError: 'mylib'
```

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- Streamlit version: 1.20
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Any
- Virtual environment: Minimal plus editable modules in PYTHONPATH, see linked gitrepo.


### Additional Information

I won't pretend to comprehend the full picture here, this is tricky stuff! Some clues I've found:

The KeyError issue was mentioned in passing in the comments on this issue in October 2022 but that issue is about another topic:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4595

A possible source of the problem was pointed out in this issue in 2020:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1430

The problem probably stems from non-threadsafe manipulation of sys.modules such as in this code:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py#L558

This is similar to what you can optionally have the runpy module do with alter_sys=True, explained in the python documentation as not threadsafe here:
https://docs.python.org/3/library/runpy.html#runpy.run_module

A better solution then might be using runpy.run_module with alter_sys=False. This will however have some side effects, as you mention in comments in script_runner.py. I may be willing to help out fixing this but these side effect issues seem to run deep so the streamlit core developers would need to give their blessing to the approach.

issues.title: Deprecate the `persist` option of `st.cache_data` in favor of configurable cache storage
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Deprecate the [`persist` parameter of `st.cache_data`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.cache_data) (`persist="disk"`). It doesn't fit well with the rest of the API and is incompatible with more recent features. A better, more flexible alternative is to make the **cache storage backend configurable** (e.g. via `st.App`), so users can plug in a storage that persists to disk — or Redis/S3 — consistently across the whole app.

### Why?

`persist="disk"` is a narrow, awkward escape hatch:
- It only supports a single hardcoded mode (`"disk"`) with a non-configurable location (#3018).
- It doesn't compose cleanly with other cache features — e.g. it ignores `ttl` (#4859).
- It's a per-function flag for what is really a deployment/storage concern, so it's easy to misuse and inconsistent across an app.
- It doesn't scale to multi-instance deployments (each replica has its own local disk), where users actually want a shared/central store.

A configurable storage backend addresses all of this in one coherent mechanism, and persistence becomes just one storage implementation rather than a special-cased parameter.

### How?

- **Introduce a configurable cache storage API** (per the [custom storage API spec, PR #14902](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14902)) — e.g. a `cache_storage_manager` parameter on `st.App` — that lets users supply a custom backend (disk, Redis, S3, …) applied consistently to `st.cache_data`.
  - A built-in/example disk-persisting storage would cover today's `persist="disk"` use case (with configurable location, and without the `ttl` incompatibility).
- **Deprecate `persist`** on `st.cache_data` with a long, clearly-communicated window and a documented migration path (it keeps working during deprecation). Follow "Graceful Evolution" — 3+ months notice, clear migration guidance.

### Additional Context

- Docs: [`st.cache_data`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.cache_data).
- Replacement direction: [PR #14902 — custom storage API for `st.App`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14902) (also motivated by #5849 "bring your own Redis cache").
- Related persist limitations: #4859 (`persist='disk'` ignores `ttl`), #3018 (configurable location for persistent cache).

issues.title: Add a first-party Playwright-based e2e testing API (`streamlit.testing.e2e`) alongside AppTest
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a first-party, Playwright-based **end-to-end (browser) testing API** for Streamlit apps — `streamlit.testing.e2e` — as an optional `streamlit[testing]` extra, complementing the existing browserless unit-testing API (`AppTest`). It would provide a Streamlit-aware semantic facade for finding and operating elements in a real browser, rerun/navigation-aware synchronization, useful failure artifacts, and an escape hatch to native Playwright `Page`/`Locator`. Design thoughts are in the [app testing toolkit spec (PR #16041)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16041).

### Why?

Today users face an unhelpful choice: `AppTest` is fast and Python-native but runs no real frontend (so it can disagree with a real app, and can't cover rendering, custom components, accessibility, media, charts, or real user journeys), while browser testing can validate the real product but Streamlit provides **no supported way** to start the app, wait for reruns, select elements, collect logs, or test a deployed/embedded app — users must assemble and maintain all that infrastructure. Streamlit's own mature `e2e_playwright/` suite solves these hard problems (process lifecycle, ephemeral ports, app-idle detection, traces, iframes, uploads, dataframes/charts, etc.) but is coupled to the repo layout and private DOM test IDs, so it isn't a releasable public API.

This is especially costly for **AI coding agents**, which need a deterministic run command, semantic element identity, a compact description of the current UI, and actionable failure artifacts to validate their work — indexes, private CSS/test IDs, sleeps, and screenshots alone make brittle tests.

### How?

Ship a two-layer testing story with clear boundaries (don't build a third UI-testing engine, and don't turn AppTest into a browser emulator):

- **AppTest (browserless)** stays the fast option for logic/state/basic widget workflows — with improved runtime fidelity and typed + universal semantic queries (`get_by_key`/`get_by_label`/`get_by_text`) and a compact `snapshot()`.
- **`streamlit.testing.e2e` (browser)** — the new Playwright-based API, installed via `pip install "streamlit[testing]"`.

Proposed shape (from the spec):

```python
from playwright.sync_api import expect
from streamlit.testing.e2e import StreamlitPage, app_fixture

app = app_fixture("app.py")

def test_sign_in(app: StreamlitPage):
    app.get_element_by_label("Username", type="text_input").set_value("ada")
    app.get_element_by_label("Password", type="text_input").set_value("correct horse battery staple")
    app.get_element_by_label("Sign in", type="button").click()

    welcome = app.get_element_by_text("Welcome, ada", type="heading")
    expect(welcome.locator).to_be_visible()
```

Key capabilities:
- **App lifecycle fixture:** `app_fixture()` starts one app server per test module on an ephemeral localhost port, gives an isolated browser page per test, and waits until the initial run is idle. Also target direct/external URLs (deployed/embedded apps).
- **Semantic selection:** strict, retrying finders that understand Streamlit elements and layout containers — `get_element_by_key` / `get_element_by_label` / `get_element_by_text`, plus `get_element(type=...)` / `get_elements(type=...)`; a returned element that is a container (sidebar, form, expander, popover, dialog, tab, column, container) can scope further queries. An optional `type` discriminator maps to a generated public `ElementType` taxonomy for IDE completion.
- **Rerun/navigation-aware synchronization** so tests don't rely on sleeps.
- **Actionable failure artifacts** (text/logs/traces/screenshots) and a **semantic snapshot** (`semantic_snapshot()`) as a token-efficient interface for humans and agents.
- **Escape hatch** to native Playwright `Page`/`Locator` for anything the facade doesn't cover.
- A shared **testability vocabulary** across both layers (public element types, labels, keys, containers), explicitly optimized for AI agents.

### Additional Context

- Spec: [PR #16041 — \`[spec] Streamlit app testing toolkit\`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16041) (`specs/2026-07-16-streamlit-app-testing-toolkit/product-spec.md`).
- Related: open `feature:app-testing` issues, e.g. #9786, #13163, #9128.

issues.title: st.dialog Does Not Close Immediately After User Action if Followed by Blocking Operation (e.g. time.sleep(15))
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When using `st.dialog` to collect feedback from a user, if the feedback submission is followed by a blocking operation (e.g., `time.sleep(15)`), the dialog's title remains visible on the screen until the blocking operation is complete. This creates a poor user experience because the user may expect the dialog to disappear immediately after submitting their input, but the dialog remains visible until the blocking operation finishes.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time
import streamlit as st

@st.dialog("Cast your vote")
def vote(item):
    st.write(f"Why is {item} your favorite?")
    reason = st.text_input("Because...")
    if st.button("Submit"):
        st.session_state.vote = {"item": item, "reason": reason}
        st.rerun()

if "vote" not in st.session_state:
    st.write("Vote for your favorite")

    if st.button("A"):
        vote("A")
    if st.button("B"):
        vote("B")
else:
    time.sleep(15)
    f"You voted for {st.session_state.vote['item']} because {st.session_state.vote['reason']}"
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Use the provided code below to mimic collecting user feedback using `st.dialog`.
2. After the user submits their feedback, the code simulates a blocking operation using `time.sleep(15)`.
3. Notice that the dialog's title ("Cast your vote") remains visible for the full 15 seconds while `time.sleep(15)` is running.

### Expected Behavior

The dialog should close immediately after the user submits their input, regardless of any blocking operation that follows, so that the UI responds promptly to the user's action.

### Current Behavior

The dialog remains open until the blocking operation (`time.sleep(15)`) is completed. This means the title "Cast your vote" is displayed on the screen for 15 seconds.

![2024-09-04_21-39-12 (1)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f664f9f7-24cf-4b3b-8fad-d5fdcf0dcfdb)


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.37.1
- Python version: 3.9
- Operating System: Mac OS / Linux Ubuntu 
- Browser: Chrome 


### Additional Information

### GIF:
_Attach a GIF that shows the issue occurring._

### Additional Context:

I plan to use `st.dialog` to collect user confirmation before running a long operation. However, due to this behavior, the dialog title remains visible until the operation completes, making the user experience confusing. Ideally, the dialog should close immediately after the user interaction, regardless of subsequent operations.

issues.title: Minimize `StreamlitDuplicateElementId` errors
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Reduce how often developers hit `StreamlitDuplicateElementId` (duplicate widget/element ID) errors by making element ID generation smarter about the surrounding container context — so that identical widgets placed in different containers (chat messages, fragments, columns, etc.) don't collide without the developer having to manually craft unique `key`s everywhere.

### Why?

It's increasingly common to have repeating identical widgets across different chat messages, fragment calls, or columns. Today the developer must manage and track a unique `key` for each, which adds a lot of boilerplate and complexity. This is especially painful in chat/LLM apps (in-chat interactive widgets, code-eval "run" buttons, generated suggestion buttons) — and for LLM-generated code it can be nearly impossible to solve, since the model may emit duplicate widgets across messages. `st.form` already avoids this within forms (the `form_id` is part of the ID), which shows the approach can work more broadly.

This is a high-impact papercut: `StreamlitDuplicateElementId` is the **No. 3 most thrown uncaught exception type**, occurring in ~**0.5% of all apps**.

A related pain point: some elements raise `StreamlitDuplicateElementId` and tell you to add a `key`, but **don't actually support a `key` argument**, leaving no clean fix. Examples:
- #11424 — showing the same `st.plotly_chart` multiple times raises `StreamlitDuplicateElementId`.
- #11360 — multiple `st.audio` calls with the same parameters and `autoplay=True` raise a duplicate error that prompts you to add a key, but `st.audio` has no `key`.

### How?

Incorporate more of the container context into an element's ID computation, focusing on **stable, explicit signals** (not user-facing text). Ideas:

- **Wrapping container keys:** automatically include the `key` of wrapping containers / `st.fragment` / `st.form` (those that support keys) in the child element's ID computation. Only for containers that have an explicit key set.
  - If we do this, it strengthens the case for **adding `key` to more containers and elements** — see #9580 and the concrete cases #11424 (`st.plotly_chart`) and #11360 (`st.audio`), plus #6152.
- **Re-evaluate key namespaces and parent-key reuse:** regular element keys, form IDs, and fragment definition keys are currently tracked in separate registries. `st.form` already contributes its `form_id` to the auto-generated IDs of unkeyed children; fragment keys identify fragment definitions but are not currently part of regular child element ID computation. Consider both:
  - Reusing explicit form / fragment / keyed-container keys as stable parent context for **unkeyed** descendants.
  - Whether form and fragment keys should participate in the same duplicate-key checks as regular element keys, or remain separate namespaces that only contribute parent context.

  Treat registry unification as a compatibility decision: the same string can currently be reused between some form / fragment and regular-element keys, and one keyed fragment definition can intentionally run from multiple call sites. Preserve the rule that an explicit child `key` is authoritative and independent of its container.
- **Column index in `st.columns`:** include the column number in the ID computation so the same widget in different columns of the same `st.columns` call doesn't collide.
- **Parent container types:** include the parent container type(s) as part of the ID computation.

**Important caution — be conservative about what goes into ID generation.** Adding container context to the ID changes element identity, which has a subtle downside: a widget that **dynamically moves between containers** (e.g. its wrapping container changes across reruns) would get a new ID and thus lose its identity and state. This is the main risk to weigh (more so than existing widget state resetting on upgrade), and it can be fixed by explicitly setting a `key` on that element so its identity no longer depends on the container context. In particular:
- **Do not** include user-facing **labels/titles** of wrapping containers (e.g. expander label, dialog title, popover label, tab name) in the ID — these change often and would be fragile/surprising. Prefer **explicitly set keys** for disambiguation instead.
- Auto-added context must apply **only to widgets without an explicit `key`**. When a user sets an explicit `key="x"`, the ID must **not** include the added container context — an explicit key should always behave predictably and stay stable regardless of the surrounding containers. Think through backwards compatibility / migration carefully.

### Additional Context

- Add `key` to more elements/containers: #9580, and concrete duplicate-ID cases where no `key` is available today: #11424 (`st.plotly_chart`), #11360 (`st.audio`).
- Related: #6152 (composable/reusable component API for larger apps).
- `st.form` already includes `form_id` in widget ID generation — a useful precedent.
- There is an older internal product spec exploring options (implicit container key-prefix, adding `key`/`key_prefix` to containers, best-practice docs, or fixing duplicate IDs via enumeration). This issue intentionally leans toward the conservative, explicit-key-based approaches from that discussion.

issues.title: st.slider corrupts min_value/max_value when bounds are reversed, silently producing a wrong range
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`_slider()` tries to swap reversed bounds with two sequential statements, but the second one reads the variable the first one just overwrote:

```python
# lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/slider.py:1081-1083
# Ensure that min <= value(s) <= max, adjusting the bounds as necessary.
min_value = min(min_value, max_value)
max_value = max(min_value, max_value)   # <-- min_value is already the new (smaller) value
```

After line 1082, `min_value` is `min(a, b)`, so line 1083 evaluates `max(min(a, b), b)`, which is always `b`. The original `min_value` can never become the upper bound, so the intended swap never happens. Depending on what `value` is, this silently produces a wrong range or raises an exception quoting numbers the user never passed.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

# 1. Bounds silently reinterpreted
st.slider("a", 10, 1)                                  # -> range 1..10, value 10

# 2. Upper bound silently invented from `value`
st.slider("b", min_value=10, max_value=1, value=5)     # -> range 1..5  (max_value=1 is gone)

# 3. Spurious exception quoting numbers the user never passed
st.slider("c", min_value=10, max_value=1, value=1)     # -> StreamlitAPIException
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run any of the three lines above.
2. Compare the resulting slider bounds against the arguments passed.

### Expected Behavior

Either of the following would be self-consistent:

- Reject reversed bounds with a clear error naming the two values the caller actually supplied, the way `st.date_input` already does:
  > The `min_value`, set to 2024-01-02, shouldn't be larger than the `max_value`, set to 2024-01-01.
- Or genuinely swap them, so `st.slider("a", 10, 1)` yields a `1..10` slider — which is what the code comment says it intends.

Today it does neither reliably.

### Current Behavior

Verified with `streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest`:

```
slider(min=10, max=1)            -> min=1.0 max=10.0 value=10
slider(min=10, max=1, value=5)   -> min=1.0 max=5.0  value=5
slider(min=10, max=1, value=1)   -> RAISED: Slider `min_value` must be less than the `max_value`.
                                            The values were 1 and 1.
```

Note case 3: the user passed `10` and `1`, but the error reports "The values were 1 and 1" — both numbers have been overwritten by the faulty normalization. Case 2 is the most damaging, because it silently produces a slider whose upper bound (`5`) was never supplied as a bound at all; it leaked in from `value`.

Isolating just the two lines:

```python
min_value, max_value = 10, 1
min_value = min(min_value, max_value)
max_value = max(min_value, max_value)
print(min_value, max_value)   # 1 1     <-- current behavior

min_value, max_value = 10, 1
min_value, max_value = min(min_value, max_value), max(min_value, max_value)
print(min_value, max_value)   # 1 10    <-- intended
```

The `min_value == max_value` guard at line 1137 then fires on values that are an artifact of this bug rather than of user input, and it only catches the case where the corruption happens to collapse both bounds to the same number — which is why `st.slider("x", 5, 5)` errors while `st.slider("x", 10, 1)` does not.

### Suggested Fix

Assign both bounds simultaneously (or compute the max from the original value):

```python
min_value, max_value = min(min_value, max_value), max(min_value, max_value)
```

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `st.slider("b", min_value=10, max_value=1, value=5)` no longer produces a slider whose upper bound came from `value`.
- [ ] Reversed bounds either swap correctly or raise an error that quotes the values the caller actually passed.
- [ ] Test coverage for reversed `min_value`/`max_value` with `value` below, inside, and above the range.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Unknown.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (`develop`, commit `2ac0d77d3`)
- Python version: 3.13.6
- Operating System: Windows 11 (logic is platform-independent)
- Browser: n/a (reproduced headlessly via `streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest`)

### Additional Information

Related but distinct: #5099 covers `value` falling outside `(min_value, max_value)`. This report is specifically about the bound-normalization statements corrupting `min_value`/`max_value` themselves.

issues.title: Modernize `st.chat_message` design to match modern agentic chat UIs
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Refresh the visual design and interaction model of `st.chat_message` so chat/agentic apps look modern out of the box — closer to the chat UIs people expect from tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and other assistants. This includes rethinking avatars, message alignment, per-message actions, and how the message background is themed.

### Why?

`st.chat_message` is central to Streamlit's most compelling demos (LLM/agentic apps), but its default look feels dated compared to modern chat UIs. Users routinely reach for CSS hacks or custom components to get a contemporary look (hidden avatars, right-aligned user bubbles, hover actions). Making the default modern — and the common tweaks first-class — would make agentic apps look polished with no effort and reduce reliance on fragile workarounds.

### How?

Modernize the design and add a few high-value options, for example:

- **Avatars:** make the design look clean when avatars are hidden, and consider hiding them by default (or an easy option to hide them). Today an avatar is always shown.
- **User vs. assistant alignment:** support right-aligned user messages (bubble style) and left-aligned assistant messages, matching common chat UIs.
- **Per-message actions:** built-in, hover-revealed actions on a message (e.g. copy, thumbs up/down, regenerate, custom actions) that can trigger callbacks/reruns.
- **General styling refresh:** spacing, bubble/background treatment, and typography that feel modern and cohesive with the rest of the app theme.

**Background & nested-element theming:** Apply the message background via **theming** and update nested elements so they render correctly against it — like the **sidebar** does. Using the **secondary background color** is a promising approach (nested elements already look right in the sidebar), and it should also fix cases like charts not looking good against the current gray background. This is closely related to the background handling in the [`st.container` background/shadow spec (#14683)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14683).

Keep everything backwards compatible (opt-in where it changes existing looks) and themeable.

- [Figma Mockups](https://www.figma.com/design/fzBM3vuV1Dh0lznSzKxOh4/Streamlit-Open-Source-design-system?node-id=3973-16463&t=waRdSwMGoWbMj4A1-4)

### Additional Context

Related issues to fold into this modernization:
- #10740 — configurable toolbar / clickable actions on `st.chat_message`.
- #6921 — "Copy to Clipboard" button in `st.chat_message`.
- #11380 — color and background color support for `st.chat_message` avatars.

### Summary

We have an application where we process a set of files, sometimes more than 2000.
The file_uploader widget hangs, then eventually produces a network error when the number of images exceeds 980.

This issue wasn't previously occurring. We did run into one issue where we had to increase the Python recursion limit since we iterate over each file and the default Python recursion limit is 1000 (I assumed ~20 or so iterations went to setup/config), and would produce an error. So we set the recursion limit to the number of files uploaded + 50.

Now, the `file_uploader` widget fails to upload >980 files. 980 works fine, and 981 uploads all but one. I looked at the source code and didn't see any upper limit defined for this operation. Logs don't show anything besides hanging until there are exactly 980 files, at which point it returns the list of uploaded files and continues executing the script. 

Wondering if internally the recursion limit is being met, and might need to be increased. 
Otherwise, please help us determine why we are now running into this issue. We were previously using streamlit version 1.29.0, and upgraded to 1.33.0 to find the issue still persists.

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add opt-in support for Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) to the native authentication flow, so the _streamlit_user cookie set by st.login() becomes useless when copied off the device it was issued on.

Currently only Chrome takes advantage of this but I am happy to implement it and open a pull request
W3C draft: https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-dbsc/

### Why?

Since 1.42, st.login() stores the user's identity in a signed cookie with a 30-day lifetime. The cookie is HttpOnly and Secure, which is right, but there is no server-side session state: a cookie copied from a browser profile by malware or a colleague with the laptop works on any other machine until it expires, and st.logout() only clears the local copy. The app-level mitigations available today are shortening the session age in application code and re-checking an allowlist on every rerun. Neither stops a stolen cookie from being used within its window.

DBSC is the web platform's answer to exactly this. The browser generates a key pair in the device's secure hardware at login, and the server issues a short-lived cookie that the browser can only renew by signing a challenge with that key. A copied cookie expires within minutes and cannot be refreshed elsewhere. Chrome shipped it as generally available on Windows in Chrome 146 and is rolling it out on macOS in Chrome 147, and it is a W3C WebAppSec draft. Browsers without support ignore the header and keep working as today, so it degrades cleanly.

Streamlit apps are frequently internal dashboards with real data behind Google or Entra logins, which is the population this protects.

### How?

The change is contained in the Starlette auth layer and needs no frontend work. Sketch:

1. **Registration header.** In the OAuth callback, alongside the existing cookies, send `Secure-Session-Registration` pointing at a new route, with the supported algorithms (ES256, RS256).
2. **Two new routes** next to `/auth/login`, `/auth/logout` and `/auth/callback`:
   - `/auth/dbsc/register`: verifies the browser's signed registration JWT, records the device public key, returns the session config, and sets a short-lived `__Host-` bound cookie.
   - `/auth/dbsc/refresh`: on a missing or expired bound cookie the browser calls this with a signed challenge; the server verifies it against the registered key and reissues the bound cookie.
3. **Stateless key storage.** Streamlit has no server-side session store and runs as one process, so rather than adding one, the device key's thumbprint is written into the existing signed `_streamlit_user` cookie at registration. Refresh verifies the challenge signature against the thumbprint carried in the cookie. Restarts and multiple replicas are then unaffected, matching how the current cookie works.
4. **Websocket check.** The `/_stcore/stream` endpoint, which already decodes the identity cookie on connect, refuses a connection whose identity cookie is bound but whose bound cookie is absent.
5. **Configuration.** A new `[auth]` option, off by default, for example `device_bound_sessions = true`. Requires HTTPS, since `__Host-` cookies are refused otherwise, which is already true of production `st.login()` deployments.

Signature verification can use authlib's JOSE support, which is already a dependency of the auth feature.

One point to verify during implementation: Chrome defers ordinary requests while it refreshes an expired bound cookie, and the behaviour for a WebSocket upgrade is not spelled out in the spec. The frontend fetches `/_stcore/host-config` and `/_stcore/health` over HTTP before opening the stream, which should trigger the refresh first, but this needs a real-browser test.


### Additional Context

- Chrome for Developers, DBSC overview and server integration: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/device-bound-session-credentials
- Chrome 147 macOS rollout: https://scotthelme.co.uk/device-bound-session-credentials-lands-in-chrome-on-macos/

issues.title: Stale output from a long-running computation erroneously shows as not stale when app rerun
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

This is a bug report on behalf of Thiago in order to keep it tracked.

When a Streamlit app with long-running computation is stopped and then re-run, old stale data from the previous run show up as if it was not stale until the old thread completes execution, at which point the data is properly cleaned up.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import platform
import time

import streamlit as st

st.caption(
    f"""
Running with Python {platform.python_version()} and Streamlit {st.__version__}.
"""
)

"""
This is an app!!
"""


def slow_computation(x):
    st.write("Starting slow computation...")
    time.sleep(10)
    st.write("Stopping slow computation...")
    return f"Done, {x + 1}"


out = slow_computation(1)

st.write(out)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

This is a Playwright test that simulates the current behavior (which is to say, this test currently passes, but should fail once the underlying issue is fixed). There are `NOTE`s inline that describe expected behavior


```py
import time

from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_threading_behavior(page: Page):
    # This uses `localhost:8501` since I was running different versions of Streamlit
    # in an attempt to bisect this issue in case it was introduced at some point in time
    page.goto("http://localhost:8501/")

    page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...").wait_for(timeout=20000)
    expect(page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...")).to_be_visible()

    print(page.query_selector_all(".element-container")[0].inner_text())

    # At this point, the first run of the thread completed
    expect(page.get_by_text("Done, 2")).to_be_visible()

    # conditional logic to make it work with older versions of Streamlit
    if page.query_selector('div[data-testid="stMainMenu"]'):
        page.get_by_test_id("stMainMenu").click()
    elif page.query_selector('[id="MainMenu"]'):
        main_menu = page.query_selector('[id="MainMenu"]')
        if main_menu:
            main_menu.click()

    # Now we are re-running the app
    page.get_by_text("Rerun").click()

    # Some time delay so that the new thread is started and some elements are marked as stable
    time.sleep(2)

    # Expect some of the elements to be marked as stale
    assert len(page.query_selector_all('div[data-stale="true"]')) == 2
    expect(page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...")).to_be_visible()
    expect(page.get_by_text("Done, 2")).to_be_visible()

    # Stop the new thread
    page.get_by_role("button", name="Stop").click()

    time.sleep(2)

    # NOTE: This should not pass. Stale elements shouldn't suddenly be marked as not stale
    # since these are old results from a thread that was supposed to have been stopped
    assert len(page.query_selector_all('div[data-stale="true"]')) == 0

    # NOTE: This should not pass. It is unexpected that the results from the old thread
    # are still showing up, despite us re-running
    expect(page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...")).to_be_visible()
    expect(page.get_by_text("Done, 2")).to_be_visible()

    # wait for the thread to complete
    time.sleep(10)

    # Expect old elements to be cleared out
    expect(page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...")).not_to_be_visible()
    expect(page.get_by_text("Done, 2")).not_to_be_visible()
```

### Expected Behavior

_No response_

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.0.0 -> 1.40.1 all show this behavior (I didn't test versions before)
- Python version: 3.8
- Operating System: Mac
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

issues.title: `setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`
issues.body:
### Summary

When a Components V2 component calls `setTriggerValue` during mount (inside the default function, rather than from a user event handler), values are silently lost if the component remounts because its `data` changed — even when an explicit `key` is passed, which keeps the element id stable.

Measured roughly a quarter loss: **5 of 21 values sent were never received by Python at all.** They are not late — a scan of the entire session log shows they never arrive in any subsequent run.

This is split out of #14710, where it surfaced during investigation. It is distinct from the two by-design mechanisms discussed there (`data` participating in element identity for unkeyed components, and trigger values resetting after each run).

**Update — measured root cause.** A frontend race in `WidgetStateManager.removeInactive`: it destroys the synthetic trigger-aggregator widget state while that state is still awaiting its batched flush, so the app reruns with no trigger at all. Not a backend discard. Measured on a production build with the repro below: 10/85 values lost unpatched vs 0/85 patched, and with instrumentation, 14/14 losses correlated exactly with the destroying call. Mechanism and open question under Additional Information.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

comp = st.components.v2.component(
    "repro.mount_trigger",
    js="""
    export default function (component) {
        const v = "val" + component.data.nonce;
        console.log("SEND " + v);
        component.setTriggerValue("v", v);
    }
    """,
)

if "clicks" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.clicks = 0
if st.button("bump"):
    st.session_state.clicks += 1

nonce = f"c{st.session_state.clicks}"
result = comp(data={"nonce": nonce}, key="stable_key")

received = result.get("v")
st.write(f"data nonce {nonce} -> received {received!r}")
print(f"nonce={nonce} received={received!r}", flush=True)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and open the browser console.
2. Click **bump** ~20 times, letting the app settle between clicks. Each click changes `data`, so the component remounts and sends one value.
3. Compare the `SEND val…` lines in the console against the `received=…` lines in the terminal.
4. Roughly one in four sent values never appears on the Python side.

### Expected Behavior

Every value the mounted component sends is readable on the following script run. The explicit `key` makes the element id stable, so a changing `data` payload should not affect delivery.

### Current Behavior

About 25% of values are never delivered. Verified as lost rather than late by scanning the full backend log after all clicks — 0 arrived in a later run.

The element id was logged each run and confirmed identical throughout (`$$ID-b4c118c7288cf7d656c205e58a384db6-stable_key`), so this is not the identity churn that affects unkeyed components.

Three controls on the same harness came out clean. They do not isolate the bug to trigger-on-mount — see Additional Information — but they do narrow which write path is affected:

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| `setStateValue` on mount, same conditions | 21/21 delivered |
| `setTriggerValue` from a user event handler, stable `data` | 20/20 delivered |
| `setTriggerValue` from a user event handler, churning `data` | 20/20 delivered |
| **`setTriggerValue` on mount, churning `data`** | **5 of 21 lost** |

### Additional Information

**Mechanism.** `setTriggerValue` writes to a synthetic aggregator widget id (`makeTriggerAggregatorId` → `$$STREAMLIT_INTERNAL_KEY_<componentId>__events`) and the flush is deferred to a `setTimeout(…, 0)` macrotask. `App.removeInactiveWidgetState()` runs from the `ScriptFinished` → `clearStaleNodes` setState callback and deletes every widget state whose id is not an active *element* id — the aggregator id never is, because it isn't part of the element tree. When that lands before the flush, the trigger is deleted but the rerun is still sent (`sendUpdateWidgetsMessage` uses unfiltered `createWidgetStatesMsg()`), so the script reruns with no trigger.

Mount-time triggers are the most exposed path: the component's `default function` runs behind `await loadAndRunModule(...)` (dynamic `import()` of a blob URL), so it executes a macrotask or more after the commit that mounted it. This also explains the control table — `setStateValue` is immune because it writes the component's real element id, and the event-handler controls passed because letting the app settle means `removeInactive` has already run.

**The `_pending_resets` theory is ruled out.** It is only populated by `mark_page_switch_drops`, which runs on page transitions and skips widgets whose recorded page is the current page, so a single-page app never populates it. (For the record, the original hypothesis was that `_pending_resets` in `lib/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py` discarded a frontend-resent value on re-registration, which would have made this by design.)

**Related blind spot.** The same synthetic id is invisible to other active-id filters, not just this one: `App.tsx` `onPageChange` sends `getActiveWidgetStates(activeWidgetIds)`, which would likewise drop a pending aggregator. Reaching it would require a trigger and a page navigation in the same macrotask, and dropping a trigger while navigating away is defensible, so no change is planned there. Recorded as an observation only.

**Scope of what was tested.** Measured against this repro on one machine, 235 trials total. It establishes this race as the cause of the loss seen here; it does not rule out other trigger-loss paths. The same race also appears to explain the recurring `bidi_components/basics_test.py::test_trigger_interactions` CI flake — the failure signature (counts unchanged plus `Result` reset to `None`) is what a trigger-less rerun produces — but that link is inferred from the signature, not directly observed. Two prior automated PRs (#14542, #14843) misattributed that flake to a slow iframe round-trip and raised timeouts.

**Open question for Components V2** (replacing the original question here, which is now answered — the drop is a race, not intentional): should `setTriggerValue` during mount be a supported pattern at all? Fixing the race makes it reliable, but it fires on every remount, so churning `data` produces one trigger per remount. That is a semantics decision independent of this bug, and it determines whether this issue closes as fixed or splits into a fix plus a documentation/warning change.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (released wheel, production frontend build)
- Python version: 3.11 · macOS · Chromium
- The ~25% figure is one 21-trial sample on a single machine; treat it as "roughly a quarter" rather than a precise rate.

issues.title: Add page and app descriptions (`page_description`, `st.Page`, `st.App`)
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add first-class authored descriptions at the page and app level: `page_description` on `st.set_page_config`, optionally `description` on `st.Page`, and a static title + description on `st.App`. Today a page can declare a title and icon, and an app has no catalog-level identity at all — so SEO, assistive tech, navigation, and non-browser clients all have to infer meaning from body copy.

### Why?

A Streamlit page already has `page_title` / `title` and `page_icon` / `icon`. There is no matching place to say what the page or the app *is*. Authors stuff that into `st.caption`, `st.markdown`, or `menu_items["About"]`, none of which is structured metadata.

That gap shows up in several places that all want the same authored sentence:

- **SEO and link previews.** Search and social crawlers need a description (and today only Community Cloud injects sharing tags). Related: #16634, #6567, #2469, #9058.
- **Accessibility.** A document-level description is the page analogue of alt text (#8563 covers elements; this is the page/app layer).
- **Multipage navigation.** `st.Page` can name a page but cannot explain it, so a nav list or catalog cannot tell "Regional revenue" from "Reports" without running the page.
- **Non-browser clients.** An agent snapshot currently serializes `url_path`, `title`, and `icon` only. A static app descriptor should be able to return title + description *without executing app code* — which is why the app-level fields belong on `st.App`, not only inside the script.

### How?

**Page description on `st.set_page_config`**, matching `page_title` / `page_icon`:

```python
st.set_page_config(
    page_title="Regional revenue",
    page_icon=":material/payments:",
    page_description=(
        "Net revenue by billing region. Excludes refunds. Periods are UTC."
    ),
)
```

**Optional `description` on `st.Page`**, so the page list carries copy without running each page (consistent with `title` / `icon`, not `page_*`):

```python
st.Page(
    "revenue.py",
    title="Regional revenue",
    icon=":material/payments:",
    description="Net revenue by billing region. Excludes refunds.",
)
```

**Static title and description on `st.App`**, available without executing the script:

```python
app = st.App(
    "main.py",
    title="Finance apps",
    description=(
        "Internal finance dashboards. Net revenue excludes refunds and is in EUR."
    ),
)
```

Suggested behavior:

- `st.Page.description` is the default for that page; `st.set_page_config(page_description=...)` overrides it for the current run (same additive pattern as today's page title).
- Single-page apps that never call `st.Page` still get a description via `set_page_config`.
- `st.App` title/description are app-level and static. They do not replace per-page title/description. For `streamlit run` apps without `st.App`, the default page's title/description (or a future config option) can stand in.
- Consumers of the same strings: HTML `<meta name="description">` / Open Graph, assistive tech, navigation (if we choose to surface it), and structured snapshots / a static app descriptor.

**Naming.** `page_description` on `set_page_config` matches `page_title`. On `st.Page` and `st.App`, `description` / `title` match the existing `title` parameter (the [agent-app interface spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/docs/agent-app-interface/specs/2026-08-28-agent-app-interface/product-spec.md) also floated `app_title` / `app_description` on `st.App` if we want the prefix explicit).

**Not in this request:** element-level alternative text for images, charts, and tables (#8563) and `help` on media (#3133). Arbitrary extra `<meta>` tags (GSC verification, etc.) stay with #16634.

### Additional Context

- Suggested as a standalone follow-up in the [agent-app interface spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/docs/agent-app-interface/specs/2026-08-28-agent-app-interface/product-spec.md) ([#16843](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16843), follow-up #3): apps should explain themselves in authored metadata, not only in body widgets. Worth doing on accessibility and SEO merits even without the agent interface.
- Related:
  - #16634 — inject `<meta>` tags; a first-class `page_description` is the content those tags would publish, not a general meta-tag API
  - #6567 — social sharing meta tags outside Community Cloud
  - #2469 (closed) — `st.set_page_config(description=...)`
  - #9058 — title/favicon in the initial HTML (same "available before JS" problem)
  - #8563 — element-level alt text
  - #5673 (closed) — config-file website metadata

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`use_container_width` was deprecated with a stated removal date of **2025-12-31**. That date is well past (today is 2026-09-08), but the parameter is still accepted on current Streamlit and still logs a warning that claims it will be removed after 2025-12-31.

Please either actually remove `use_container_width` now that the advertised cutoff has passed, or keep the compatibility shim and update the warning copy so it does not cite a date in the past.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.button("Hello", use_container_width=True)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the snippet above on a recent Streamlit version (the warning is still present on `develop`).
2. Observe the terminal / app logs.

### Expected Behavior

After 2025-12-31, either:

- `use_container_width` is rejected / removed, as the deprecation message promised, **or**
- the warning no longer claims a 2025-12-31 removal date (for example, “will be removed in a future release”).

### Current Behavior

The call still works and prints:

```
Please replace `use_container_width` with `width`.

`use_container_width` will be removed after 2025-12-31.

For `use_container_width=True`, use `width='stretch'`. For `use_container_width=False`, use `width='content'`.
```

The date is a hardcoded string in `make_deprecated_name_warning(...)` (for example in `st.image` and the same pattern on other elements). It is not gated on the calendar date, and there is no follow-up removal.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: current `develop` (also observed in Community Cloud apps on 2026-09-08)
- Python version: n/a (API deprecation warning)
- Operating System: n/a
- Browser: n/a

### Additional Information

- Deprecation was introduced with Advanced Layouts, e.g. [PR #11719](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/11719) (“We will remove `use_container_width` after 12-31-2025”).
- I could not find an open GitHub issue or STREAMLIT Jira ticket tracking the actual removal after that date.
- Nearby precedent: [PR #15786](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15786) already removed the older `use_column_width` parameter from `st.image`.
- Related but different: [#12519](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12519) quoted the same warning in the context of `st.image` + `width="stretch"` (closed as a separate bug).

This is not a Community Cloud platform issue; it is OSS Streamlit still advertising an expired deprecation date.

issues.title: Rerun on each new keystroke in `st.text_input`
issues.body:
### Problem

I wanted to create a Streamlit application which has an input text field which immediately responds to user input, e.g. like the Google search field does. Something like this:

```py
def search_callback():
  st.write("You searched for:", st.session_state.input)


search_str = st.text_input('Search', key='input', placeholder='Life of Brian', on_input=search_callback)
```

### Solution

I couldn't find any way to achieve this with Streamlit. I think what would be necessary is a new type of `on_input` callback or similar.

Further, I think it would make sense to have a kwarg containing the current input. I would also have liked this for the `on_change` callback. As a workaround I have been using the session state instead:

```py
def search_callback():
  st.write("You searched for:", st.session_state.input)


search_str = st.text_input('Search', key='input', placeholder='Life of Brian', on_change=search_callback)
```

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

**If you'd like the Streamlit team to prioritize this feature request, please use the 👍 (thumbs up emoji) reaction in response to the initial post.**

issues.title: `st.cache_resource` and `st.cache_data` should support async functions (coroutines)
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

This was originally requested in #3651 for the deprecated `st.cache`, and the same problem still exists with  `st.cache_resource` and `st.cache_data`.

### `st.cache_data`
```python
import asyncio

import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data
async def get_data():
    return 42


async def main():
    data = await get_data()
    st.write(data)


asyncio.run(main())
```
This results in the following error because the returned value of `get_data()`, a coroutine object, is not pickleable.
```
UnserializableReturnValueError: Cannot serialize the return value (of type get_data()) in get_data(). st.cache_data uses [pickle](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pickle.html) to serialize the function’s return value and safely store it in the cache without mutating the original object. Please convert the return value to a pickle-serializable type. If you want to cache unserializable objects such as database connections or Tensorflow sessions, use st.cache_resource instead (see [our docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/caching) for differences).
```

### `st.cache_resource`

```python
import asyncio

import streamlit as st


@st.cache_resource
async def get_resource():
    return 42


async def main():
    resource = await get_resource()
    st.write(resource)


asyncio.run(main())
```

It runs successfully at the first run, but the following error occurs in the second run and later because the coroutine object returned from `get_resource()` is cached and the same coroutine object is awaited again.
```
RuntimeError: cannot reuse already awaited coroutine
```

### Why?

_No response_

### How?

I think it's enough the sample code snippets above work as expected.

### Additional Context

I'm an author of [stlite](https://github.com/whitphx/stlite) (Wasm ver. of Streamlit) and [Transformers.js.py](https://github.com/whitphx/transformers.js.py) (a Python wrapper for FWs like stlite to use Transformers),
and I encountered a situation where I wanted this feature: https://github.com/whitphx/transformers.js.py?tab=readme-ov-file#stlite-serverless-streamlit
The Transformers' object can only be obtained in an async way, and it's a compute-intensive task so I wanted to cache it. Now I do it using the session state as a workaround.

issues.title: Support caching event-loop-bound async resources across reruns
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched the existing issues for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary.

### Summary

Explore supporting reusable event-loop-bound resources, such as async database connections and HTTP or LLM clients, with `st.cache_resource`.

Async cache support in #16168 awaits a coroutine function and caches its completed return value. This works for loop-independent values such as dataframes, API responses, and configuration.

It does not make a cached resource's event loop persistent. A client created on one short-lived loop—for example, through `asyncio.run()`—may fail when reused from another loop on a later rerun:

```python
@st.cache_resource
async def get_client():
    return SomeAsyncClient()
```

Async `validate` and `on_release` callbacks are also unsupported today. Supporting them is part of the same lifecycle problem tracked by this issue: Streamlit must await validation before deciding whether to serve a cache entry and run cleanup on the resource's owning event loop during eviction, clearing, background replacement, or session shutdown.

### Why isn't this currently supported?

Supporting these resources requires more than awaiting the cached function. Streamlit would need defined behavior for:

- persistent event-loop ownership;
- ensuring resource operations execute on the owning loop;
- global versus session-scoped resources;
- async `validate` and `on_release` callback execution;
- cleanup when a cache, session, or server shuts down;
- thread safety and concurrent access;
- reconnects and reruns.

The common case—caching an inert value produced asynchronously—does not require this lifecycle machinery and is covered separately by #16168.

Users can currently avoid the problem by:

- creating, using, and closing the client within one coroutine invocation;
- caching the inert result rather than the client;
- using a synchronous client when one is available; or
- managing a dedicated long-lived event loop themselves.

Given these workarounds and currently limited evidence of demand, this is not planned as part of the initial async cache support.

### Feedback wanted

Please react with a thumbs-up and describe your use case if the workarounds are insufficient. In particular, it would help to know:

- which client or resource you need to cache;
- whether it should be shared globally or only within one session;
- why creating it per operation is impractical; and
- how you currently manage async execution in your Streamlit app.

### Relationship to rerun-resilient streaming

Rerun-resilient streaming is planned separately in #14524. That work addresses streams being interrupted by reruns and may resolve the specific `st.write_stream` workflow in #12076. This feature request covers the broader lifecycle problem of reusing cached event-loop-bound resources across reruns and APIs.

### Additional context

- General async cache request: #8308
- Example `Event loop is closed` failure: #12076
- Initial async cache implementation: #16168

issues.title: Fragments are awesome but must to be more: Selective Rerun and Execution Control
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

### Feature Request: Selective Rerun and Execution Control for `st.fragment`

Hi Streamlit team 👋

First of all, great job with the `st.fragment` feature — it’s super useful for improving interactivity and modularizing Streamlit apps.

I’d like to suggest two improvements for `st.fragment` that would make it even more powerful in terms of performance and control.

1. [also covered in #10603] The first is the ability to explicitly trigger the rerun of specific fragments from anywhere in the app, instead of being limited to interactions within that fragment. This would allow for more coordinated updates between fragments without requiring a full app rerun.

2. The second idea is to let developers prevent certain fragments from re-executing during a full rerun, keeping their state and UI output intact unless their input parameters change or they are explicitly refreshed. This would improve performance and user experience by avoiding unnecessary recomputation and visual flickering.

Overall, these additions would give developers finer control over fragment behavior and app performance.

Thanks for considering this! 🙏

### Why?

#### Why this would be useful

These two ideas would allow for finer-grained control over how fragments behave during reruns, enabling developers to:

* Improve performance in apps with multiple heavy components.
* Avoid unnecessary recomputation and UI flicker.
* Trigger coordinated updates between fragments dynamically.

Internally, I imagine Streamlit already tracks the execution scope and state for each fragment, so this might be feasible with some form of dependency or caching mechanism.

Thanks a lot for considering this! 🙏
I’d be happy to help clarify or provide examples if needed.

### How?

#### 1. Selective rerun of specific fragments

Right now, when something inside a fragment is interacted with, Streamlit reruns that fragment only, which is great.
However, it would be even better if we could *trigger reruns of specific fragments programmatically* — for example, from another fragment or from the main app.

Imagine something like:

```python
st.fragment(key="fragment_a")
def my_fragmen_a(param1, param2):
    ...

st.fragment(key="fragment_b")
def my_fragmen_b(param1, param2):
    ...

# Somewhere else:
st.rerun(scope=["fragment_a", "fragment_b"])
```

So if you define a fragment with a key, you could explicitly trigger its rerun (with or without passing new parameters).
This would make it possible to coordinate updates between fragments in a controlled way, without forcing a full rerun of the app.

---

#### 2. Ability to skip rerun for some fragments on full app rerun

Another idea: when the app performs a full rerun, it would be great to have a way to mark certain fragments so they *don’t* re-execute — keeping their current state and UI output as-is.

For example, you might have a heavy fragment (long computation, visualization, etc.) that you don’t want to rerun unless its input parameters have actually changed.

Something like:

```python
@st.fragment(key="heavy_plot", rerun="explicit")
def heavy_plot(data):
    ...
```

If the fragment’s inputs haven’t changed and no internal interaction happened, Streamlit could just reuse the previous rendered output instead of re-running the code.
This would not only improve performance but also help avoid UI flickering (the “greyed out” state that appears during reruns).

### Additional Context

_No response_

issues.title: Fragment to fragment (co-fragment) communication instead of rerunning entire app
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Would be great to create a functionality for co-fragment communication directly rather than re-running the entire app. This could be streamlit's blockhain moment - no middle men (in this case the entire app).

### Why?

Re-rendering the entire app for co-fragment communication is frustration slow. Co-fragment communication would drastically increase the speed and performance of a streamlit app. 

### How?

My app looks like the below:

![fragments](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5e0ea57-452c-4696-89c2-112ac27dd9b2)

The black outlines are fragments. The purple/pink outlines are nested fragments. I understand co-fragment communication occurs through session_state which is great but for this communication to be recognised, one must re-run the whole app. This makes the app more slow and somewhat buggy in my experience of operating my app. 

Seeing as fragments can be re-run periodically, it would be great to add the possibility to communicate between specific fragments via an action. For example, in my app image, After I input details in the "Contact Details" expander, I want to update the CV Preview fragment. But to do that, I have to re-run the entire app. Perhaps the possibility to rerun specific fragments based on some unique Id (like a key of a streamlit widget) when I say click on the submit form button in the Contact Details expander would be great. 

Just an example
```
@st.fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"])
```

The issue with the above is for every rerun action, the `keys to update` will rerun. So perhaps, we could create a trigger command parameter.

```
@st.fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"], trigger_keys=["form_submit_btn"])
```

We could also get fancy and connect trigger keys to keys to update:


```
@st.fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"], trigger_keys=[{"frag1":"form_submit_btn"}])
```

issues.title: Rerun fragment from anywhere, not just from within itself
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Related to #8511 and #10045.

Currently the only way to rerun a fragment is calling `st.rerun(scope="fragment")` from within itself. Allowing a fragment rerun to be triggered from anywhere (another fragment or the main app) would unlock new powerful use-cases.  

### Why?

When a fragment is dependent on another fragment or on a change on the main app, the only current way to reflect that dependency is to rerun the full application whenever a dependency changes.

### How?

I think adding a key to each fragment would allow the user to build his custom logic to manage the dependency chain and take full control on when to run a given fragment:

```python
@st.fragment(key="depends_on_b")
def a():
    st.write(st.session_state.input_for_a)

@st.fragment(key="depends_on_main")
def b():
    st.session_state.input_for_a = ...
    if st.button("Should rerun a"):
        st.rerun(scope="fragment", key="depends_on_b")

if other_condition:
    st.rerun(scope="fragment", key="depends_on_main")
```

This implementation doesn't go the full mile to describe the dependency chain in the fragment's definition and let streamlit handle the rerun logic as suggested in #10045, but provides more flexibility for the user to rerun a fragment from anywhere and under any conditions that fits his use-case

### Additional Context
