issues.title: Add `st.sidebar.bottom` container to pin elements to the bottom of the sidebar
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `st.sidebar.bottom` container that pins its elements to the bottom of the sidebar, analogous to how `st.bottom` pins elements to the bottom of the main app section.

### Why?

It's a very common pattern to keep certain sidebar content anchored at the bottom — user/account info, a logout button, app version, links, or a settings/theme toggle — while the rest of the sidebar scrolls above it. Today there's no clean way to do this; users resort to spacers or CSS hacks that break across screen sizes and content lengths.

### How?

Mirror the existing `st.bottom` API, scoped to the sidebar:

```python
with st.sidebar.bottom():
    st.caption("Logged in as [REDACTED_EMAIL]")
    st.button("Log out")
```

The container sticks to the bottom of the sidebar, with the normal (scrollable) sidebar content flowing above it.

### Additional Context

- Analogous to the existing `st.bottom` container for the main app section.
- Related: #7311 (sidebar position), #9545 (sticky top/bottom containers).

issues.title: Add a `type="cards"` variant to `st.radio` for a card/bordered design
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `type` parameter to `st.radio` with a `"cards"` variant that renders each option as a bordered, selectable card (with the selected card highlighted) instead of the default radio-button list. Same widget behavior — only the visual style changes. See [Tremor's Radio Card Group](https://www.tremor.so/docs/inputs/radio-card-group) for the look.

### Why?

Card-style single-select is a very common, more prominent and touch-friendly pattern for choosing between a few richer options (e.g. plans, payment methods, layouts, modes). Today users approximate it with columns + bordered containers + buttons/`st.radio` and a lot of manual state/CSS work. A built-in `"cards"` variant makes this polished pattern a one-liner.

### How?

Add a `type` parameter (default preserves today's look):

```python
choice = st.radio(
    "Choose a plan",
    ["Starter", "Pro", "Enterprise"],
    captions=[
        "For individuals getting started",
        "For growing teams",
        "Advanced controls & support",
    ],
    type="cards",
)
```

- `type="default"` — current radio-button list.
- `type="cards"` — render each option as a bordered card; the selected option is visually highlighted.
- Keep existing params working (`captions`, `horizontal`, `format_func`, `index=None`, etc.). Captions map naturally to a description line inside each card.

**Alternative solution — a `border: bool` parameter:** Instead of a `type` enum, just add `st.radio(..., border=True)` that wraps each option in a bordered card. This mirrors the `border` parameter on `st.container` and keeps the API minimal. Downside: it's less extensible than a `type` enum if we later want more visual variants (e.g. `"pills"`), and it's a boolean rather than a named style.

### Additional Context

- Reference designs:
  - [Tremor — Radio Card Group](https://www.tremor.so/docs/inputs/radio-card-group)
  - [Tailwind Plus — Radio Groups (card designs)](https://tailwindcss.com/plus/ui-blocks/application-ui/forms/radio-groups)
  - [streamlit-extras — Card Selector](https://extras.streamlit.app/?extra=%F0%9F%83%8F+Card+Selector) (existing community implementation)
- Related: #2325 (`st.radio` with sections), #7184 (stretch horizontal radio), #11959 (consistent API for selectbox/pills/segmented_control/radio).

issues.title: Easier cross-filtering between charts/dataframes
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

In BI dashboards, you often want to cross-filter between charts and/or dataframes. Building this in Streamlit via chart/dataframe selections isn't very straightforward. Could we find an easier solution?

### Why?

Two example use cases to illustrate the problem:

- Simple example: You have one chart and one dataframe. If you select some rows in the dataframe, the chart updates to show only those data points. If you select some data points in the chart, the dataframe updates to show only the corresponding rows. 
- Complex example: A dashboard with multiple charts. If you click on any chart, all the other charts update to only the data that was selected in the first chart. Ideally, this should also support then selecting data in a 2nd or 3rd chart to further drill down. 

It's possible to build this in Streamlit with chart/dataframe selections, but not very straightforward since:

1. You need to parse the selection and then manually filter the data in other visualizations based on what was selected. 
2. It's not easy to update a visualization that is "above" the one where data was selected, due to Streamlit's rerun model. You'd need to save all selections centrally in `st.session_state` and then update charts from there. 
3. The entire page will rerun on every selection, making this potentially slow. 

### How?

Probably needs a good amount of thinking but some rough ideas:

1. Allow passing the key of another element to `on_select`. This would then automatically sync that element whenever some data is selected in the current one. Or maybe it should even sync in both ways?

  ```python
  st.line_chart(..., key="chart1")
  st.dataframe(..., on_select="chart1")
  ```

2. Adding a command like `st.cross_filter` to cross filter between multiple charts/dataframes.

  ```python
  st.line_chart(..., key="chart1")
  st.plotly_chart(..., key="chart2")
  st.dataframe(..., key="dataframe")
  st.cross_filter("chart1", "chart2", "dataframe")
  ```

One big problem here is probably making sure all visualizations have access to the same data/can filter. E.g. if I have a pie chart showing the gender of all people, how can we make sure clicking on "Female" lets the other charts know how to filter their own data?

### Additional Context

_No response_

issues.title: Compact layout and compact widgets to get the most from the available screen space
issues.body:
### Problem

Streamlit's overall layout and individual components are quite wasteful with screen space – there is a lot of white space everywhere.

This is great for simple apps for casual users, but it creates a usability problem in applications where you want to give power users many options to tweak without scrolling away from the main visualization or data table, or just provide a high information density on one screen. Tabs and expanders offer some relief, but they limit what you can have on the screen at one time. 

Applications like Tableau, R shiny, and the ubiquitous Excel based tools have a much higher information density than Streamlit apps. If Streamlit aims to be an alternative to those applications in "power user" scenarios (think finance, BI, scientific visualization,...), it needs the capability to present UIs with higher density.

Examples of very generous use of space:

* large font size in widgets like `selectbox`, `multiselect`, `slider`, and others
* large size of the main widget "box" in `selectbox`, `number_input` and others
* `file_uploader` is huge!
* tables aren't particularly compact either
* lots of white space between components
* whitespace on top of screen (see #6336, but the issue here is wider) 

Things that go in the right direction:

* wide mode
* horizontal layout for `radio`
* the new options for label placement, including the option to ditch the labels altogether
* sometimes it just helps to zoom out in the browser, but of course that is not a solution

### Solution

**MVP:** What's the smallest possible solution that would get 80% of the problem out of the way?

* provide a "compact layout" and/or "small fonts"  option for the chunkiest controls; see examples above
* solve #6336
* provide an alternative style option that reduces whitespace between components

**Possible additions:** What are other things that could be added to the MVP over time to make it better?

* more options for label placement, for example left of control (I realize, though, that this probably generates ugly alignment problem; maybe there could be some sort of "form table", where labels are in one column and controls next to it)
* just more layout options in general – grids, complex multicolumn alignment – would help to make use of screen space

### Additional context

Where I work, I'm heavily advertising replacing insanely complex Excel-tools with proper Python code + Streamlit UI. While there is a lot of buy-in for replacing the actual logic with Python, I frequently meet resistance when it comes to the UI. As much as I dislike Excel – you can get a lot of control on a single screen there. I have seem similar arguments when it comes to pitching Streamlit + Altair as an alternative to Tableau.

This issue was created as suggested in the forum [on this thread](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/compact-layout-and-components/45639/3).

issues.title: Session State convenience function for initialization
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

It'd be nice for Session State to have a convenience method for initializing it.

### Why?

Many apps have boilerplate code:
```python
if "my_key" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.my_key = "default_value"
```
If there are multiple keys, you might shortcut the logical test to check for one and initialize all others:
```python
if "A" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.A = "A"
    st.session_state.B = "B"
    st.session_state.C = "C"
```
If any of the keys were associated to a widget and the widget wasn't continuously rendered, you could have a situation will all keys initialized on session start, but maybe "B" or "C" got deleted later. Thus, to be really thorough, you'd need:

```python
session_init = {"A":"A", "B":"B", "C":"C"}
for key, value in session_init.items():
    st.session_state[key] = value
```

It might be nice to have a convenience function to handle the latter:

```python
st.session_state.from_dict({"A":"A", "B":"B", "C":"C"})
```

A parameter could be used to distinguish between initializing (set if not exists), updating (dictionary merge), or full replacement (delete other keys).


### How?

Similar to how `st.query_params` is a dict-like interface with a few extra functions, `st.session_state` could get a convenience function or two.

### Additional Context

_No response_

issues.title: Type-hint values in session_state
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

I use a streamlit app that has a `session_state` and I call methods on some of these values a lot. It would be helpful if it was possible to type-hint the values so that we can make use of it on Pylance etc.

issues.title: Limiting maximum and minimum of st.date_input's selectable dates to the maximum/minimum of datetime.datetime
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Setting the maximum available value of Python's datetime as default for st.date_input causes issues.
The function internally tries to set a value 10 years later for the selection widget and then crashes.

To reproduce the behaviour, run this code: 
```
import streamlit as st
from datetime import datetime
st.date_input('Enter Timespan:', value=[datetime.today() , datetime.max])
```
The documentation for st.date_input includes a parameter to control the maximum value of the selection widget: 
> max_value : datetime.date or datetime.datetime
>     The maximum selectable date. If value is a date, defaults to value + 10 years.
>     If value is the interval [start, end], defaults to end + 10 years.

Setting the parameter max_value of st.date_input to datetime.max solves the issue.
`st.date_input('Enter Date:',  max_value=datetime.max, value=[datetime.today(), datetime.max])`

### Why?

This result is expected behaviour and can be inferred from the documentation. 
However, it seems rather inelegant/unintuitive to explicitly have to set an additional max_value when using the maximum value of the data type used.

### How?

Since date_input works with datetime internally, I'd set it to check datetime.max (and datetime.min, similarily) itself and not try to set its maximum to an impossible value.  
So to get the max selectable value in pseudocode would be:
```
max_value = max( value + 10 years, datetime.max)
```

If this behaviour is not desired, a nicer warning would be in order. 
```
Error message: 
ValueError: year 10009 is out of range
```
Took me a while to trace that back to streamlit internally adding 10 years. Maybe something like:
```
ValueError: Cannot set value 9999. Default value range for date_input [9989-10009] would be out of range for datetime. Please set max_value.
```

issues.title: st.metric sparkline (chart_data) fails to render after a no-data -> data transition
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When an `st.metric` (that has previously been rendered with a sparkline and then again with no data) is re-rendered with `chart_data` going from empty/None (no sparkline) to a populated list (sparkline expected), the sparkline frequently fails to mount. The metric value and delta update correctly; only the embedded chart is missing. It reproduces reliably on the first
"no data -> data" transition and is unaffected by the data itself.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time

import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(page_title="Metric Chart Issue Demo", layout="wide")

# Realistic-looking weekly data (~52 weeks)
# fmt: off
CHART_DATA_WITH = [
    5, 8, 12, 7, 9, 15, 11, 13, 8, 10, 14, 6, 9, 11, 13, 7,
    10, 12, 8, 14, 9, 11, 7, 13, 10, 8, 12, 9, 11, 14, 7, 10,
    13, 8, 11, 9, 12, 7, 14, 10, 8, 13, 11, 9, 12, 7, 10, 14,
    8, 11, 13, 9,
]  # 52 values
# fmt: on

CHART_DATA_WITHOUT = []

st.title("Metric Chart Rendering Issue")

use_workaround = st.toggle("Enable Container Workaround", value=False)
st.caption("Toggle ON to see the mitigation that reduces (but doesn't eliminate) the issue")

# Dropdown (default to "With Data")
dataset = st.selectbox("Select Dataset", ["With Data", "Without Data"], index=0)

# Determine data based on selection
if dataset == "With Data":
    chart_1 = CHART_DATA_WITH
    chart_2 = [x * 2 for x in CHART_DATA_WITH]
    chart_3 = [x * 0.5 for x in CHART_DATA_WITH]
    chart_4 = [x * 1.5 for x in CHART_DATA_WITH]
    metric_val = 42
    delta_val = 5
else:
    chart_1 = CHART_DATA_WITHOUT
    chart_2 = CHART_DATA_WITHOUT
    chart_3 = CHART_DATA_WITHOUT
    chart_4 = CHART_DATA_WITHOUT
    metric_val = 0
    delta_val = 0

# Generate timestamp for workaround keys
if use_workaround:
    base_timestamp = int(time.time() * 1000)

# Four metric cards - conditional rendering based on workaround toggle
if not use_workaround:
    # Path A: No workaround (default)
    col1, col2, col3, col4 = st.columns(4)

    with col1:
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 1",
            value=metric_val,
            delta=delta_val,
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_1 if chart_1 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col2:
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 2",
            value=int(metric_val * 2),
            delta=int(delta_val * 2),
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_2 if chart_2 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col3:
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 3",
            value=metric_val,
            delta=delta_val,
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_3 if chart_3 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col4:
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 4",
            value=int(metric_val * 1.5),
            delta=round(delta_val * 1.5, 1),
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_4 if chart_4 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )
else:
    # Path B: With single-container workaround
    col1, col2, col3, col4 = st.columns(4)

    with col1, st.container(key=f"col1_{dataset}_{base_timestamp}"):
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 1",
            value=metric_val,
            delta=delta_val,
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_1 if chart_1 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col2, st.container(key=f"col2_{dataset}_{base_timestamp}"):
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 2",
            value=int(metric_val * 2),
            delta=int(delta_val * 2),
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_2 if chart_2 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col3, st.container(key=f"col3_{dataset}_{base_timestamp}"):
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 3",
            value=metric_val,
            delta=delta_val,
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_3 if chart_3 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col4, st.container(key=f"col4_{dataset}_{base_timestamp}"):
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 4",
            value=int(metric_val * 1.5),
            delta=round(delta_val * 1.5, 1),
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_4 if chart_4 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

st.markdown("---")
st.markdown("""
### How to Reproduce

**Without Workaround (Toggle OFF - default):**
1. Start with "With Data" selected (default)
2. Switch to "Without Data" - charts should disappear
3. Switch back to "With Data" - **charts are expected to fail to appear**

**With Workaround (Toggle ON):**
1. Enable the "Container Workaround" toggle above
2. Repeat steps 1-3 - charts should appear more reliably (but may still occasionally fail)

---

**Expected**: Charts appear when switching to "With Data"  
**Actual (no workaround)**: Charts consistently fail to render after first transition  
**Actual (with workaround)**: Charts usually render, but may still occasionally fail

**Workaround**: Wrap each metric in a keyed container with a timestamp-based unique key. 
This forces Streamlit to create fresh component instances on each render, which appears 
to reduce (but not eliminate) the rendering issue.

---

**Environment**: Streamlit 1.57.0, 1.60.0, and 1.61.1 (reproduces on all)

**Other Mitigation Strategies Attempted:**
- Double-container wrapping (nested containers with unique keys) - slightly better than 
  single container
- Using `st.empty()` placeholders before containers - no improvement
- Session state counters for key generation - worse performance
- Explicit data validation (converting empty lists to None) - no improvement

The single-container workaround shown in this demo provides the best balance of simplicity 
and reliability improvement.
""")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Instructions also included inline in code example to view while executing.

Steps (with the "Container Workaround" toggle OFF):

1. Load the page with "With Data" selected. All four metric cards show sparklines.
2. Select "Without Data". Charts clear; values go to 0. (expected)
3. Select "With Data" again. Values return, but the sparklines do NOT render.

Additional browser console check:

The sparkline renders as `[data-testid="stMetricChart"]` containing an `<svg>`.
Run in the browser console after step 3:

```
    (() => {
      const m = [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="stMetric"]')];
      return {
        cards: m.length,
        withChart: m.filter(c => c.querySelector('[data-testid="stMetricChart"] svg')).length,
      };
    })()
```

Healthy: `withChart === cards`. Bug: `withChart < cards` (typically 0) after
the transition, even though the metric values are correct.



### Expected Behavior

- Expected: selecting "With Data" repopulates both the values and the sparklines. Continually going between data/no data should update the chart correctly each time
- Actual: values repopulate; sparklines are sometimes absent after the transition. Somewhat better with extra container hacks, but never 100% correct

### Current Behavior

All covered in the code, but in general:
* I display a few metric cards with data to start.
* Then I change to the card not being backed by any data by setting `chart_data` to None or an empty list (this is an approximation of what my app is doing, but gets the point across...I have data sometimes and then users can switch to selections that have no data for whatever reason). Everything works to here
* Then another selection adds data back to the the card. 
* Everything on the cards functions as expected except the sparkline chart. The chart may or may not re-render. In my experience, without any mitigation the chart will not re-render the vast majority of the time. With shenanigans like additional container indirection, it might re-render more often but never have I seen it work every time.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit: reproduced on 1.57.0, 1.60.0, and 1.61.1 (not fixed by the upgrades)
- Python: 3.13
- Browser: Chromium 149.0.7827.200 and Firefox 140.12.0esr (also observed in normal app use across browsers and operating systems including MacOS and Windows of various versions. I cannot tell you what browsers were involved there tho)
- OS: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 (Plow)


### Additional Information

- Direction-specific: "no data -> data" fails; "data -> no data" is fine.
- Wrapping each metric in a keyed `st.container` with a per-run unique key reduces the failure rate but does not eliminate it. A second nested keyed container helps marginally more.
- Using a monotonic session-state counter for the keys made it worse, and converting empty lists to None had no effect - suggesting the issue is a frontend component-lifecycle timing race, not key collision or data handling.
- In case it's useful, in my case the dropdown selection would map to a DB query that is returned in a pandas dataframe. Once the query has been fetched once, it's cached for 24 hrs

issues.title: @st.cache_data: distinct arguments can collide on one cache key
issues.body:
### Summary

`@st.cache_data` (and `@st.cache_resource`) can return one call's cached result for a **different** set of arguments. The per-call cache key is built by folding each argument name and value into a single hasher in sequence, with no marker between fields, so the boundaries between arguments are not part of the key. As a result, two distinct argument tuples can encode to the same bytes and collide on one cache entry, producing a silent false cache hit.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data
def load(doc, org=""):
    # This line only prints on a real cache miss (a real computation).
    st.write(f"computing for doc={doc!r}, org={org!r}")
    return f"{doc}|{org}"


# First call: computes and caches under some key.
st.write(load("doc1", "acme"))

# Different arguments, but they hash to the SAME key as the call above,
# so this returns the first call's cached value instead of computing its own.
st.write(load("doc1str:orgstr:acme"))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above.
2. Note that only the first `load(...)` prints its `computing for ...` line.
3. The second call, `load("doc1str:orgstr:acme")`, prints no `computing` line and returns `"doc1|acme"` (the first call's result) instead of `"doc1str:orgstr:acme|"`.

### Expected Behavior

Two calls with different arguments should never share a cache entry. `load("doc1", "acme")` and `load("doc1str:orgstr:acme")` are different calls and should each compute and cache their own result.

### Current Behavior

Both calls map to the same value key, so the second call is a false cache hit and returns the first call's value. The cause is in `_make_value_key` in `lib/streamlit/runtime/caching/cache_utils.py`: each argument name and value is folded into the args hasher back to back with nothing encoding where one field ends and the next begins, so `("doc", "doc1", "org", "acme")` and `("doc", "doc1str:orgstr:acme")` produce the same digest. Concretely, the encoded fields concatenate to the same byte string:

```
"str:doc" + "str:doc1" + "str:org" + "str:acme"
== "str:doc" + "str:doc1str:orgstr:acme"
```

The key derivation is therefore non-injective: distinct argument tuples can produce identical keys.

### Fix direction

Make the key derivation injective by length-prefixing each field before folding it into the value-key hasher, so the boundary between an argument's name and value, and between successive arguments, is part of the key. Identical calls still produce the same key; distinct calls no longer collide. Because the key format changes, persisted (`persist="disk"`) and in-memory caches take a one-time miss and recompute on the first call after upgrade.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: develop (reproduced against the current `lib/streamlit/runtime/caching/cache_utils.py`)
- Python version: 3.10-3.14
- Operating System: any
- Browser: n/a (backend logic)

- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

After Altair/Vega-Lite charts started using the native Streamlit toolbar, clicking the download icon next to Fullscreen saves a PNG only. Please keep that native download icon, and on hover show a small toolbar-styled dropdown so the user can choose PNG or SVG.

### Why?

I'm always frustrated when I hover an Altair/Vega-Lite chart, see the native download icon beside Fullscreen, click it, and can only get PNG.

For reports and papers I often need SVG (vector, scalable) as well as PNG. The old Vega-Embed ⋯ menu offered "Save as PNG" / "Save as SVG". After https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15806, that menu is gone, SVG export is gone, and `usermeta.embedOptions` can no longer restore export actions.

Workarounds (custom HTML components, extra `st.download_button`s, or DOM hacks) either leave the native toolbar unused or drift out of style as Streamlit's toolbar design changes. There is no public API to attach a format menu to the existing toolbar download button.

Related but different: #8177 is about PNG resolution, not choosing a format.

### How?

Keep the existing native download icon on Altair/Vega-Lite (and other Vega) charts, in the same toolbar row as Fullscreen.

When the pointer hovers that download icon, show a compact dropdown that matches the toolbar (same icon size, radius, colors, light/dark theme). Suggested items:

- Download PNG
- Download SVG

Clicking an item exports from the current Vega view (`toImageURL("png")` / `toImageURL("svg")`) and starts a browser download.

A click with no menu selection can keep today's PNG-only behavior as the default.

I do not need a new `st` command. Optional later: `st.altair_chart(..., download_formats=("png", "svg"))` to choose which items appear. A Python API is nice-to-have; the hover menu on the native icon is the main request.

Please do not bring back the old Vega-Embed ⋯ menu (View Source / Open in Vega Editor). This should stay a Streamlit toolbar control.

### Additional Context

- Native toolbar change that removed SVG: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15806
- Older embedOptions / actions discussion: https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/does-altairs-set-embed-options-work-with-streamlit/1675
- PNG quality (related, not this request): https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8177

I am building a Streamlit questionnaire analysis app that shows many static Altair charts. Users expect the hover toolbar download icon (same family as Fullscreen) to let them pick PNG vs SVG, without a separate download widget beside every chart.

### Summary

Our enterprise application uses Streamlit WebSockets for application communication.

During an enterprise DAST/security assessment, the scanner tested the WebSocket Origin validation by modifying the Origin header to an unauthorized domain.

The WebSocket connection was still accepted.

For example, the legitimate request contains an approved Origin:

Origin: https://<approved-application-domain>

The DAST scanner changes this to:

Origin: https://malicious-example.com

The WebSocket connection is still established.

## Security Concern

Without strict Origin validation, an authenticated WebSocket connection may potentially be initiated from an unauthorized website.

This creates a security concern for enterprise applications where access is restricted to specific trusted domains.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

Streamlit should provide a supported configuration option to define an explicit WebSocket Origin allow-list.

For example:

server.websocketAllowedOrigins = [
    "https://<approved-domain>"
]

or an equivalent configuration.

The application should reject the WebSocket upgrade when the Origin is not present in the configured allow-list.

### Current Behavior

Missing WebSocket Origin Validation

Test performed by DAST:

1. Establish normal WebSocket connection.
2. Modify the Origin header to another domain.
3. Send the WebSocket upgrade request.
4. Connection is still accepted.

issues.title: st.slider silently mis-represents dates outside the frontend number range
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`st.slider` accepts `date`/`datetime` bounds that the frontend cannot represent exactly, and silently snaps them to a different instant instead of reporting the problem. The `int` and `float` paths already validate and raise a helpful `StreamlitAPIException`; the timelike path does not.

Timelike values are serialized as microseconds since the epoch and held in a JavaScript number on the frontend, so only about **1684-07-28 to 2255-06-05** round-trips exactly. Outside that, precision is lost.

`lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/slider.py` acknowledges the gap:

```python
elif all_timelikes:
    # No validation yet. TODO: check between 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31
    pass
```

Worth noting the TODO's own target range is wrong — most of `0001`–`9999` is not representable, so validating to those limits would not have fixed it.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import datetime as dt
import streamlit as st

# Silently accepted, but min_value cannot be represented exactly:
st.slider("historical", min_value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(1700, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1))

# Also silently accepted, both bounds unrepresentable:
st.slider("projection", min_value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(2400, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1))

# Raises a bare OverflowError instead of a StreamlitAPIException:
st.slider("ancient", value=dt.date(1, 1, 1))
```

### Actual Behavior

Inspecting the serialized proto shows the bounds exceeding JavaScript's `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` with no error raised:

```
in-range 1900..2000      -> NO ERROR. min=-2208988800000000 max=946684800000000  JS-unsafe: none
historical 1600..1700    -> NO ERROR. min=-11676096000000000                      JS-unsafe: ['min']
far future 2300..2400    -> NO ERROR. min=10413792000000000 max=13569465600000000 JS-unsafe: ['min', 'max']
min date 0001..0002      -> OverflowError: date value out of range
```

Two distinct problems:

1. **Moderately out-of-range values are accepted and lose precision.** Years like 1600 or 2300 are ordinary in historical datasets and long-range projections, so this is not just an exotic edge case.
2. **Extreme values raise a bare `OverflowError`.** It comes from `prepared_value[0] - timedelta(days=14)`, which computes the *default* `min_value`/`max_value` even when the caller supplied both explicitly, and overflows next to `date.min`/`date.max`. This is not a `StreamlitAPIException`, so it surfaces as an unhandled Python error rather than actionable guidance.

### Expected Behavior

Out-of-range timelike bounds should raise a `StreamlitAPIException` naming the representable range, matching how the int and float paths already behave. Extreme values should produce that same message rather than an `OverflowError`.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: `develop` (reproduced at `f2648d7237`)
- Python version: 3.14.5
- OS: macOS 15.5

### Additional Information

Contrast with the existing int path, which is what the timelike path should mirror:

```
`max_value` (9007199254740992) must be <= (1 << 53) - 1
```

issues.title: Add a `type="pills"` variant to `st.tabs` to show tabs as pills
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `type` parameter to `st.tabs` with a `"pills"` variant that renders the tab headers as pills (rounded, button-like segments) instead of the default underlined tab bar. Keep the same tab behavior — only the visual style of the tab headers changes.

### Why?

The underlined tab style is great for section navigation, but pill-style tabs are a very common, more compact and prominent look — especially for filters, view switchers, and dashboards. Today users approximate this with `st.pills`/`st.segmented_control` plus manual conditional rendering, which is more boilerplate and doesn't give the clean container-per-tab model that `st.tabs` provides.

### How?

Add a `type` parameter (default preserves today's look):

```python
tab1, tab2, tab3 = st.tabs(["Overview", "Details", "Settings"], type="pills")
with tab1:
    st.write("...")
```

- `type="default"` (or `"underline"`) — current tab bar.
- `type="pills"` — render the tab headers as pills.
- Everything else (content containers, active-tab state, etc.) stays identical.

### Additional Context

- Visually aligns `st.tabs` with the existing pill styling used by `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`, but with the `st.tabs` container model.
- Design references for the pills style:
  - [Tailwind Plus — Tabs (pill variant)](https://tailwindcss.com/plus/ui-blocks/application-ui/navigation/tabs#component-2a66fc822e8ad55f59321825e5af0980)
  - [Tremor — Tabs, solid variant](https://tremor.so/docs/ui/tabs#example-tabs-solid-variant)

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

You can pass a list to `st.date_input`'s `value` parameter. An empty list will initialize the widget with an empty interval (showing placeholder text). A pair of values will initialize the widget with the given interval (showing the dates as an initial selection). However, if you pass a list of size one, the widget has only the starting date of the interval initialized with no end date. Instead of showing placeholder text for the end date, it's blank.

```
import streamlit as st
from datetime import date, datetime

a = st.selectbox("A", ["today", "2024-10-01", date(2024,9,1), datetime(2024,8,1,12,0,0,0), None])
b = st.selectbox("B", ["today", "2024-10-01", date(2024,9,1), datetime(2024,8,1,12,0,0,0), None])

x = st.date_input("Two-list", [a,b])
x
y = st.date_input("One-list", [a])
y
z = st.date_input("Empty-list", [])
z
```

### Why?

Presumably, it would look better to show placeholder text for the end date when only the initial date of a range is selected. This is also how an intermediate state looks if someone selects a new start date and clicks out of the widget before selecting the end date.

### How?

If someone unfocuses an (interval) date widget with only the start date selected, show the placeholder text for the missing end date.

issues.title: st.user is empty in apps that use an external host auth token, because the token shares a subprotocol slot with XSRF
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The frontend sends either a host auth token or the XSRF cookie in one `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` entry, and the host auth token wins when both exist. Because of that, an app that receives an external auth token from its host page cannot also send the XSRF token. The server cannot validate the token for those handshakes, so it does not read the signed user cookie and `st.user` stays empty.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.write(st.user)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Serve the app to a host page that sets `useExternalAuthToken: true` in `/_stcore/host-config`.
2. Configure an `[auth]` section so the app can sign a user in.
3. Leave `server.enableXsrfProtection` at its default value of `true`.
4. Sign in and let the host page pass its auth token to the app.
5. Read `st.user` in the app and see that it holds no user fields.

### Expected Behavior

An app should be able to send both the host auth token and the XSRF token on the handshake, so host-auth deployments get user identity without turning XSRF protection off.

### Current Behavior

`WebsocketConnection.getSessionTokens` builds the second subprotocol entry as `hostAuthToken ?? xsrfCookie ?? "PLACEHOLDER_AUTH_TOKEN"`. The server reads that one entry as the XSRF token (`_parse_subprotocols` in `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_websocket.py`). A host auth token in that slot fails `validate_xsrf_token`, so the handler skips the signed user cookie.

The handshake itself still succeeds, because an embed is same-origin and XSRF admission only applies to cross-origin handshakes. Only identity is affected.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1 and `develop`
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Any
- Browser: Any

### Additional Information

Split out of #16476, which made the XSRF token admission control for cross-origin WebSocket handshakes. That change documents this limitation in the `server.enableXsrfProtection` help text. Options worth weighing: carry both tokens in distinct subprotocol entries, or validate the host auth token on a separate path.

issues.title: FIPS friendliness
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit should support [FIPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Information_Processing_Standards)  friendliness.

When a library or package is not FIPS friendly, it significantly limits your ability to use it commercially since you cant sell that software to the US gov or anyone that works with them.

### Why?

Streamlit is not officially [FIPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Information_Processing_Standards) compliant. Any current FIPS friendliness seems to be [maintained by the community](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Astreamlit%2Fstreamlit+fips&type=issues). This means that sometimes new Streamlit features are developed that break FIPS requirements. 

The FIPS regressions seem to have been trivial, so it would be nice if they could be caught before release.

### How?

1. Streamlit should run it's pre-release CI suite on a FIPS compliant image and check for crashes. The suite should set up a FIPS environment (like the python-fips chainguard container) and executes a test script to see if unapproved paths are blocked. 
2. Streamlit should run a linter so that we pass `usedforsecurity=False` flag on non-cryptographic internal hashes; like cache key generation, file watchers, session IDs, or anything else we would use MD5 for. 



### Additional Context

_No response_

issues.body:

## Summary

When XSRF protection is enabled and `server.enableCORS=false`, Streamlit logs a warning that says `server.enableCORS` is "being overridden to 'true'." The current code only logs the warning. It does not change the config value. This can make operators think that Origin checks are stricter than they are.

## Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.write("hello")
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a config with `server.enableCORS=false`.
2. Leave `server.enableXsrfProtection=true` enabled.
3. Start the app.
4. Read the startup warning in the logs.
5. Inspect behavior or code paths and see that `server.enableCORS` is still treated as false.

## Expected Behavior

The warning text should describe the real behavior. If Streamlit says it overrides the option to true, the code should do that. Otherwise the warning should say that the setting stays false and that Origin checks are still wide open.

## Current Behavior

The warning says:

```text
Warning: the config option 'server.enableCORS=false' is not compatible with
'server.enableXsrfProtection=true'.
As a result, 'server.enableCORS' is being overridden to 'true'.
```

But the code only logs this message. There is no code path that changes the option to true. The Origin allow logic still short-circuits when `server.enableCORS=false`.

## Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

## Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Any
- Browser: N/A

## Additional Information

Split from [issue #16386](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16386). This is operator-facing and related to security because the warning can create a false sense of protection in reverse-proxy deployments.

issues.title: WebSocket protocol error path ignores client.showErrorDetails and leaks stack traces
issues.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

## Summary

When a malformed WebSocket `BackMsg` frame fails protobuf deserialization, Streamlit uses a path that bypasses uncaught app exception redaction. Because of this, `client.showErrorDetails` does not apply. Stack traces with file paths and line numbers can reach the client. I reproduced this on 1.61.1.

## Reproducible Code Example

```python
# app.py
import streamlit as st

st.write("hello")

# send_malformed_frame.py
import asyncio
import websockets


async def main():
    async with websockets.connect(
        "ws://localhost:8501/_stcore/stream",
        subprotocols=["streamlit"],
    ) as ws:
        # b"\\xff" is not a valid BackMsg protobuf frame.
        await ws.send(b"\\xff")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Run `app.py` on Streamlit 1.61.1.
2. Set `client.showErrorDetails = "none"`.
3. In a second terminal, run `send_malformed_frame.py`.
4. The script connects to `ws://localhost:8501/_stcore/stream` with subprotocol `streamlit` and sends `b"\xff"`.
5. Observe that the script receives a `ForwardMsg` Exception payload.
6. Observe that the Exception payload contains `DecodeError` and a stack trace entry with an absolute file path.

## Expected Behavior

Protocol-level WebSocket errors should return a generic client error or close the connection. They should not expose stack traces, file paths, or line numbers to the client. `client.showErrorDetails` should not be bypassed.

## Current Behavior

The deserialization exception goes through `AppSession._create_exception_message()`. That method calls `exception_utils.marshall(...)` without `is_uncaught_app_exception=True`. The redaction logic does not run. On the event-loop thread there is no script run context, so traceback filtering does not remove internal frames. In my local repro, the returned Exception payload had message `Error parsing message with type 'BackMsg'`, type `DecodeError`, and a stack trace entry that exposed `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_websocket.py`.

## Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

## Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Any
- Browser: N/A

## Additional Information

Split from [issue #16386](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16386). This also affects the generic `AppSession.handle_backmsg()` exception path, not only protobuf deserialization failures.

issues.title: Deleting a widget's session_state key leaves the frontend showing the stale value (backend/frontend divergence for one rerun)
issues.body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary Deleting a keyed widget's entry from `st.session_state` (e.g. `del st.session_state["foo"]` inside a callback) does not reset the widget, but can lead to an inconsistency between frontend and backend. The Python side returns the widget's *default* value for that run, but the frontend keeps displaying the old value, so backend and frontend disagree. On the **next** rerun the backend silently re-adopts the stale frontend value, so the deletion is effectively undone. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import streamlit as st text = st.text_input("Foo", value="default", key="foo") st.write("widget returned:", repr(text)) def populate(): st.session_state["foo"] = "hello" def delete(): del st.session_state["foo"] st.button("Populate", on_click=populate) st.button("Delete", on_click=delete) st.button("Noop") ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Run the app. 2. Click **Populate** (callback sets `st.session_state["foo"] = "hello"`). The text input now shows `hello` and `widget returned: 'hello'`. 3. Click **Delete** (callback runs `del st.session_state["foo"]`). 4. Observe the text input on screen vs. the `widget returned:` line. 5. Click **Noop** (any interaction that triggers a plain rerun) and observe again. ### Expected Behavior The widget value in the frontent and backend should be consistent. After deleting a widget's key in session state, it should presumably fall back to its default value. ### Current Behavior - After clicking Delete, the backend returns `widget returned: "default''` , but the frontend widget still displays `"hello"`. - After the next rerun (step 5), the backend re-adopts the stale frontend value, and both show `"hello"`. ### Screenshot ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.59.2 - Python version: 3.14.6 - Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04 - Browser: Chromium ### Additional Information Likely related: #5442

issues.title: bug: `st.pyplot` crashes with an opaque PIL error for `format="pdf"`, `"eps"`, `"ps"`, `"svgz"`
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`st.pyplot` forwards `**kwargs` to `savefig`, so `format=` accepts anything Matplotlib supports. But only raster output survives the image path. `format="svg"` was fixed in #16283; the remaining vector formats still fail, and they fail with an error from inside PIL that names neither the format nor a way forward.

`svgz` is the odd one out: it is simply gzipped SVG, so it is renderable in principle — the gzip magic bytes just aren't recognised as SVG and get handed to PIL instead.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import streamlit as st

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3])

st.pyplot(fig, format="pdf")   # UnidentifiedImageError
st.pyplot(fig, format="eps")   # OSError
st.pyplot(fig, format="ps")    # OSError
st.pyplot(fig, format="svgz")  # UnidentifiedImageError
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run an app containing any one of the four calls above.
2. The app raises from inside PIL rather than reporting anything about the format.

### Expected Behavior

- `svgz` should render, since it is gzipped SVG and SVG already renders.
- `pdf` / `eps` / `ps` cannot be rasterised without an external tool (Ghostscript or Poppler), which Streamlit does not bundle. These should fail with a clear message that names the format and points at `format="png"` or `format="svg"`.

### Current Behavior

Each format reaches PIL and raises there. Sniffing the buffer the way the current SVG check does shows why:

```
format  first bytes                        detected as SVG?  PIL result
png     b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n\x00\x00\x00\r'  False            OK
svg     b'<?xml versio'                     True             (bypasses PIL)
pdf     b'%PDF-1.4\n%\xac\xdc'              False            UnidentifiedImageError
eps     b'%!PS-Adobe-3'                     False            OSError
ps      b'%!PS-Adobe-3'                     False            OSError
svgz    b'\x1f\x8b\x08\x00p\xf0xj\x02\xff'  False            UnidentifiedImageError
```

`svgz` starts with the gzip magic `\x1f\x8b`, so the existing `<svg` / `<?xml` check cannot see the SVG inside it. `eps` and `ps` share the `%!PS-Adobe-3` prefix, so they are indistinguishable by magic bytes and are both PostScript.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.
- [x] No, this is a new problem.

Not a regression — these formats have never worked. #16283 fixed `format="svg"` only; this is the remainder of the same class of bug.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: `develop` (verified at `97eada51b4`)
- Python version: 3.14.5
- Operating System: macOS 15.5
- Matplotlib backend: Agg

### Additional Information

Related: #16283 (fixed `format="svg"`), #11489 (the original SVG crash report).

issues.title: Measurement: is the 50k sampling threshold right for polars cache hashing?
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Opening this to record a measurement rather than to assert a bug, because it corrects an assumption I had been carrying.

Large pandas/polars/numpy objects are hashed from a sample rather than in full (`_PANDAS_ROWS_LARGE = 50_000`, `_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE = 10_000` in `lib/streamlit/runtime/caching/hashing.py`). I had noted "polars sampling is a pessimization between 50k and 100k rows" as a follow-up while working on #16284. **Measuring it shows that framing is wrong** — sampling is never slower for polars. But the numbers do raise a different, narrower question about the threshold that seemed worth writing down.

### The measurement

Median of 5–7 runs, comparing the full content hash against sample-then-hash, using the same call shape as `hashing.py` (`hash_rows(seed=0).hash(seed=0)`).

Narrow frame (2 columns, ints):

```
     rows   full_ms  sampled_ms      verdict
    50000      0.32        0.31 sampling helps
    60000      0.25        0.24 sampling helps
   100000      0.31        0.21 sampling helps
   200000      0.42        0.24 sampling helps
   500000      1.24        0.29 sampling helps
  1000000      3.24        0.35 sampling helps
```

Wide frame (10 columns, half of them strings) — closer to real-world use:

```
    rows   full_ms  sampled_ms  saved_ms  rows_seen
   50000      0.58        0.57      0.01      20.0%
   60000      0.59        0.41      0.19      16.7%
  100000      1.32        0.83      0.49      10.0%
  300000      3.11        1.23      1.88       3.3%
```

### What this shows

Sampling is equal-or-faster at every size, so there is no performance regression to fix. The scaling is also clearly worth keeping at the large end — 9x at 1M rows.

The narrower observation is at the bottom of the range. At 50k rows, sampling saves **0.01 ms** (inside noise) while hashing only **20%** of the rows. At 60k it saves 0.19 ms for 16.7% coverage. So immediately above the threshold, the collision exposure is taken on for essentially no time saved.

### The question, not a proposal

Is `_PANDAS_ROWS_LARGE = 50_000` the right point for polars, given a full hash of a 50k-row frame costs well under a millisecond?

I am explicitly **not** proposing a change, for two reasons:

1. **It changes cache keys.** Any object in the affected size range would hash differently, invalidating live cache entries on upgrade — a user-visible effect that needs a deliberate decision, not a tuning tweak.
2. **The trade is a judgement about collision risk, not a measurement.** Both maintainers assessed the collision risk on #14622 as negligible, which is a reasonable basis for leaving this exactly as it is. My data can say what sampling costs; it cannot say how much collision exposure is acceptable.

The threshold is also shared with pandas (`_PANDAS_ROWS_LARGE` gates both), so a polars-specific change would mean splitting a currently-shared constant — additional complexity that only pays off if the answer to the above is "yes".

Happy to run more measurements (pandas at the same sizes, or other dtypes) if that would help settle it. Equally happy for this to be closed as working-as-intended — the measurement is the useful part.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: `develop` (measured at `a2414ead3f`)
- polars 1.43.2, Python 3.14.5, macOS 15.5

### Additional Information

Context: #14622 / #16284, where `runner.cacheHashSeed` was added as an escape hatch for sampling collisions. That option relocates collisions; it does not reduce them, which is what made the threshold worth measuring.

issues.title: bug: @st.cache_data hash collision via fixed sampling seed and PIL P-mode palette omission
issues.body:
## Summary

Two distinct cache-key collision bugs exist in `lib/streamlit/runtime/caching/hashing.py` that can cause `@st.cache_data` and `@st.cache_resource` to return stale or wrong data without any error.

---

## Bug 1 — Deterministic sampling seed enables adversarial hash collisions

**Affected code:** `_to_bytes()` in `hashing.py`, large-object sampling branches for Pandas Series/DataFrame, Polars Series/DataFrame, and NumPy arrays.

**Root cause:** When a data structure exceeds the sampling threshold (`_PANDAS_ROWS_LARGE = 50_000` rows or `_NP_SIZE_LARGE = 500_000` elements), the code samples a smaller subset before hashing. The sampling seed is hardcoded:

```python
# Pandas
series_obj.sample(n=_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE, random_state=0)
df_obj.sample(n=_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE, random_state=0)

# Polars
obj.sample(n=_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE, seed=0)

# NumPy
state = np.random.RandomState(0)
np_obj = state.choice(flat, size=_NP_SAMPLE_SIZE)
```

Because the seed is always `0`, the sampled row indices are globally fixed and known in advance. An adversary who knows which indices will be sampled can craft two structurally different inputs that produce the same hash by only modifying non-sampled positions.

**Minimal reproduction (NumPy):**

```python
import numpy as np, hashlib
from streamlit.runtime.caching.hashing import update_hash
from streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_type import CacheType

_NP_SIZE_LARGE  = 500_000
_NP_SAMPLE_SIZE = 100_000

def get_hash(obj):
    h = hashlib.md5(usedforsecurity=False)
    update_hash(obj, h, CacheType.DATA)
    return h.hexdigest()

total = _NP_SIZE_LARGE + 10_000
arr_a = np.zeros(total, dtype=np.float64)
arr_b = arr_a.copy()

# Compute which indices are NOT sampled (fixed because seed=0)
sampled = np.random.RandomState(0).choice(np.arange(total), size=_NP_SAMPLE_SIZE)
mask = np.ones(total, dtype=bool)
mask[sampled] = False
arr_b[mask] = 255.0  # modify only non-sampled positions

print(get_hash(arr_a))  # same hash
print(get_hash(arr_b))  # same hash — COLLISION
```

**Minimal reproduction (Pandas):**

```python
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, hashlib
from streamlit.runtime.caching.hashing import update_hash
from streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_type import CacheType

_PANDAS_ROWS_LARGE  = 50_000
_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE = 10_000

def get_hash(obj):
    h = hashlib.md5(usedforsecurity=False)
    update_hash(obj, h, CacheType.DATA)
    return h.hexdigest()

n = _PANDAS_ROWS_LARGE + 5_000
df_a = pd.DataFrame({"val": np.zeros(n)})
df_b = df_a.copy()

sampled = df_a.sample(n=_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE, random_state=0).index
all_idx = pd.Index(range(n))
non_sampled = all_idx.difference(sampled)
df_b.loc[non_sampled, "val"] = 99.0

print(get_hash(df_a))  # same hash
print(get_hash(df_b))  # same hash — COLLISION
```

**Impact:** `@st.cache_resource` is shared across all user sessions. An adversary who can send a request to the app can pre-compute a colliding payload and silently poison the cache, causing all subsequent users to receive the adversary's data instead of the real result — with no error raised.

---

## Bug 2 — PIL P-mode images: palette bytes omitted from hash

**Affected code:** PIL `Image.Image` branch in `_to_bytes()`.

**Root cause:** For palette-indexed (`mode="P"`) PIL images, `tobytes()` returns only the palette index per pixel, not the actual color table. Two images with identical pixel indices but different color palettes produce identical hashes despite being visually distinct.

```python
# current code
np_array = np.frombuffer(pil_obj.tobytes(), dtype="uint8")
return self.to_bytes(np_array)
```

**Minimal reproduction:**

```python
from PIL import Image
import hashlib, numpy as np
from streamlit.runtime.caching.hashing import update_hash
from streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_type import CacheType

def get_hash(obj):
    h = hashlib.md5(usedforsecurity=False)
    update_hash(obj, h, CacheType.DATA)
    return h.hexdigest()

img_a = Image.new("P", (100, 100), 0)
img_b = Image.new("P", (100, 100), 0)

palette_a = [0] * 768
palette_b = [0] * 768
palette_a[0:3] = [0, 0, 0]    # index 0 → black
palette_b[0:3] = [255, 0, 0]  # index 0 → red

img_a.putpalette(palette_a)
img_b.putpalette(palette_b)

print(get_hash(img_a))  # same hash
print(get_hash(img_b))  # same hash — COLLISION, despite different colors
```

**Impact:** Two visually different images (e.g., a legitimate chart vs. a manipulated one) share the same cache key. The first cached result is returned for all subsequent inputs regardless of actual image content.

---

## Proposed Fix

A fix has been submitted as PR #14610. The approach:

1. **Sampling seed**: Derive the seed from the data (hash of first row / first 64 elements) so that sampled indices are content-dependent. Falls back to `seed=0` for unhashable payloads to preserve the existing pickle fallback path.
2. **PIL P-mode**: Prepend `getpalette()` bytes to `tobytes()` output before hashing.

---

## Environment

- Streamlit version: all versions with large-object sampling (introduced with the sampling optimization)
- Python: 3.10+
- OS: Linux / macOS / Windows (platform-independent)

issues.title: Custom `secondaryBackgroundColor`/`backgroundColor` not applied to derived `codeBackgroundColor` and `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When you set a custom `theme.secondaryBackgroundColor` and/or `theme.backgroundColor` (but don't set `theme.codeBackgroundColor` / `theme.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`), code blocks and dataframe headers still use the default derived colors from the base theme instead of recomputing them from the custom colors.

By default, both `codeBackgroundColor` and `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor` should be `bgMix` = a 50/50 mix of `backgroundColor` and `secondaryBackgroundColor`. That derivation happens correctly in `createEmotionColors`, but then gets overwritten with the base theme value.

### Reproducible Code Example

`.streamlit/config.toml`:

```toml
[theme]
backgroundColor = "#ffffff"
secondaryBackgroundColor = "#FAFAF9"
```

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.code("print('hello')")
st.dataframe({"a": [1, 2, 3]})
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Set the theme config above
2. Run the app
3. Inspect the code block background color

### Expected Behavior

Code background should be the mix of `#ffffff` and `#FAFAF9`, i.e. roughly `#FDFDFC`.

### Current Behavior

Code background is `#F8F9FB`, which is the *default* `bgMix` (`mix(#ffffff, #f0f2f6, 0.5)`), ignoring the custom `secondaryBackgroundColor`.

Same issue for dataframe header background (`dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`).

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: develop
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:

### Additional Information

Root cause in `frontend/lib/src/theme/utils.ts` (`createEmotionTheme`):

```ts
conditionalOverrides.colors.codeBackgroundColor =
  codeBackgroundColor ?? colors.codeBackgroundColor

conditionalOverrides.colors.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor =
  dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor ?? colors.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor
```

`colors` here is the *base* theme's colors, so when the config option isn't set, we throw away the correctly derived value from `createEmotionColors(newGenericColors)` and replace it with the base default.

Contrast with the correct pattern used for `link` / `codeTextColor` a few lines below:

```ts
conditionalOverrides.colors.link =
  linkColor ?? conditionalOverrides.colors.blueTextColor

conditionalOverrides.colors.codeTextColor =
  codeTextColor ?? conditionalOverrides.colors.greenTextColor
```

These two (`codeBackgroundColor` and `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`) seem to be the only instances of this bug — other derived colors from `bgMix` (e.g. `darkenedBgMix*`) are not overwritten and should pick up the custom colors correctly.

Fix should be something like:

```ts
conditionalOverrides.colors.codeBackgroundColor =
  codeBackgroundColor ?? conditionalOverrides.colors.codeBackgroundColor

conditionalOverrides.colors.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor =
  dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor ??
  conditionalOverrides.colors.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor
```

issues.title: Deduplicate identical `st.cache_data` return values to save memory
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

`st.cache_data` stores one serialized (pickled) blob per cache key, where the key is derived only from the function + input arguments. If a function returns the *same* value (e.g. the same dataframe) for many different inputs, each of those cache entries stores a full, redundant copy. We could recognize identical serialized return values (e.g. by hashing the serialized value bytes) and store the payload only once, with each cache key referencing it — saving memory (and disk when persisted).

### Why?

- **Memory savings:** Functions that frequently return the same object under different arguments currently blow up memory with duplicate copies. Content-addressed storage would keep a single shared copy.
- Could also help mitigate memory issues when replaying widgets in cached functions (a common source of memory crashes), since the shared thing would be the stored bytes.
- Complements existing cache memory work like #2911 (limit cache size by memory footprint) and #14558 (inspect cache memory usage).

### How?

Introduce a content-addressed layer for cached values:

- On write, hash the serialized **value payload** and store it once in a blob store keyed by that digest; the per-argument cache key stores a lightweight reference (digest + metadata) plus a reference count.
- On read, resolve the reference to the shared blob and deserialize as usual.
- Evict a blob only when no cache key references it anymore.

Key implementation note: today the pickled entry is a `CachedResult` that bundles the value **and** per-call metadata (replayed `messages`, `main_id`/`sidebar_id`, `stored_at`). Because that metadata differs per key, hashing the whole `CachedResult` blob wouldn't dedup much — the design should **separate the value payload (content-addressable, shared) from the per-key metadata** so identical values actually collide.

Notes:
- Copy semantics are preserved: `st.cache_data` still returns independent copies on each read (values are deserialized per call); only the *stored bytes* are shared.
- Likely only worth it above a size threshold, given the hashing/bookkeeping overhead.

### Additional Context

Current behavior (from a code investigation): storage keys are built from input args only (`_make_value_key`), the return value is `pickle.dumps(CachedResult(...))` and written via `storage.set(value_key, bytes)`, and the in-memory layer is a `TTLCache[str, bytes]` with one independent blob per key. There is no hashing of the return-value bytes and no cross-key dedup today (the only "dedup" in the caching code is background-refresh scheduling).

- Related: #2911 (limit cache by memory footprint), #14558 (inspect cache memory usage), #13992 (cache observability).

issues.title: Send dataframe (Arrow) data via HTTP instead of the WebSocket
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Send dataframe (Arrow) data over HTTP rather than through the WebSocket, similar to how we already serve images, video, and audio. HTTP appears to be faster than the WebSocket *and* gets parallelized by the browser, which should speed up BI-style apps with many charts/tables containing thousands of datapoints each.

### Why?

- Browsers make HTTP requests in parallel, so the rest of the app can keep loading *while* the dataframe data downloads (instead of serializing everything through a single WebSocket).
- Anecdotally, the WebSocket seems a bit slower than plain HTTP requests for large payloads.
- If it works well for dataframes, it could be extended to charts (which carry large datasets too).

### How?

An MVP could extend the existing **forward message cache** mechanism to support a *reference message* that carries a URL instead of a hash. If the URL is set, the frontend downloads the message body over HTTP. This would let us put the Arrow data in media file storage and send only a lightweight reference over the WebSocket.

Considerations:
- Likely only beneficial above a certain size threshold, since there's overhead to uploading to storage, exchanging metadata, and cleaning up.
- `st.dataframe` lazy data loading could keep the initial payload small and might pair well with this (e.g. auto-enable for large dataframes).
- **SiS caveat:** new HTTP endpoints have historically been very painful there (file uploader, custom components, download button, forward message cache, static file serving). Prefer reusing existing media-file-storage plumbing rather than introducing a new endpoint, and validate end-to-end upload efficiency in that environment.

### Additional Context

- Could later be extended to charts / other elements that transfer large datasets.
- Related mechanisms: media file storage (used for images/video/audio) and the forward message cache.

issues.title: Add a button group widget with trigger (click) mode
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Provide a button group that supports **trigger (click) mode** instead of selection mode — i.e. a horizontal group of buttons that returns the clicked value once (like `st.button`) and clears after the rerun, rather than persisting a selection. This can either be a new `st.button_group` command or an extension of the existing `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`.

### Why?

It's currently a bit complicated to build things like quick selections / quick replies for chat UIs (a major need for LLM-powered apps), button toolbars, dialog action rows (Confirm / Cancel / Clear), or clickable example grids. Today you have to combine many individual `st.button`s across `st.columns`, which is a lot of boilerplate and looks messy because wrapping depends on each button's label length.

### How?

Two main options:

**Option 1 — Extend `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control` with a trigger mode:**

```python
st.pills(..., selection_mode="single" | "multi" | "trigger")
```

In `trigger` mode the widget doesn't keep state: it returns the clicked value and clears it after the rerun (like a button), returning `None` otherwise. `default` wouldn't be allowed in this mode.

**Option 2 — Add a dedicated `st.button_group` command (preferred):**

```python
st.button_group(
    options,
    *,
    format_func=None,
    key=None,
    on_click=None,
    args=None,
    kwargs=None,
    disabled=False,
    type="default" | "rounded",
    wrap=True,
)
```

Behaves like `st.pills` but tailored for triggers: no top label/help (not needed for quick selections), `on_click` instead of `on_change` (aligns with `st.button`), a `type` option for a rounded pill-like look, and a `wrap` option. Keeping triggers in a separate command avoids overloading the selection API (e.g. `selection_mode="trigger"` reads oddly, `default` becomes incompatible, and typing gets awkward).

### Additional Context

- Related: #8318 (quick replies/suggestions for chat responses) — one of the primary motivating use cases.
- Other use cases: button toolbars, dialog action rows, and clickable example grids.

issues.title: `st.status` created on a container outside a fragment corrupts the element tree and crashes the app with "Cannot set a node at a delta path"
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a fragment calls `.status()` on a container that was declared outside the fragment, and then opens that status block a second time with a separate `with` statement, the app crashes to a blank page with `Uncaught Error: Cannot set a node at a delta path`. The status container re-emits its own block at the wrong delta path, which destroys an intermediate container in the frontend element tree, so the next element written inside it has no parent. This is a regression: it works in 1.58.0 and fails in every version from 1.59.0 onward.

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-16281)

```Python
import streamlit as st


@st.fragment
def frag(outside):
    block = outside.status("query")
    with block:
        st.code("first")
    with block:  # second, separate `with` on the same status block
        st.text("second")


st.title("Repro")
frag(st.container())
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Save the example above and run it with `streamlit run app.py`.
2. Open the app in a browser and open the developer console.
3. No interaction is needed. The crash happens during the initial page load.

### Expected Behavior

The app renders the title and a `query` status container holding both writes. Opening a status block twice with two separate `with` statements should behave the same whether the status was created on a container inside or outside the fragment.

### Current Behavior

The app area goes blank and the "running" indicator returns to a rerun control. The console logs this error, thrown at `frontend/lib/src/render-tree/visitors/SetNodeByDeltaPathVisitor.ts:125` (bundle paths shortened to `index.js`):

```
Uncaught Error: Cannot set a node at a delta path
    at e.visitBlockNode (index.js:14:6488)
    at bu.accept (index.js:14:2717)
    at e.visitBlockNode (index.js:14:6366)
    at bu.accept (index.js:14:2717)
    at e.visitBlockNode (index.js:14:6366)
    at bu.accept (index.js:14:2717)
    at e.visitBlockNode (index.js:14:6366)
    at bu.accept (index.js:14:2717)
    at e.setNodeAtPath (index.js:14:6730)
    at e.addElement (index.js:14:9426)
```

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.60.0
- Python version: 3.11.13
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chromium

### Additional Information

#### Affected versions

Same repro, one browser check per version, each version serving its own frontend:

| Streamlit version | Crashes on initial load |
| --- | --- |
| 1.58.0 | no |
| 1.59.0 | yes |
| 1.59.1 | yes |
| 1.59.2 | yes |
| 1.60.0 | yes |
| `1.60.1.dev20260729` (nightly) | yes |

The regression enters in 1.59.0. No released version fixes it, and the nightly above still fails.

#### The delta stream

These are the deltas the backend emits for the example above on the first script run. The defect is the sixth delta:

```
[0, 1]           block=flex_container   fragment=-      <- the outside container
[0, 2]           block=flex_container   fragment=X      <- the fragment's own container
[0, 1, 0]        block=transparent      fragment=X      <- outside-write wrapper
[0, 1, 0, 0]     block=expandable       fragment=X      <- the status, inside the wrapper
[0, 1, 0, 0, 0]  element=code           fragment=X      <- first `with` write
[0, 1, 0]        block=expandable       fragment=X      <- BUG: re-emitted at the wrapper's path
[0, 1, 0, 0, 1]  element=text           fragment=X      <- crashes here
```

The sixth delta replaces the `transparent` wrapper at `[0, 1, 0]` with an `expandable` block. `AppRoot.addBlock` only inherits the existing children when the block type matches (`frontend/lib/src/render-tree/AppRoot.ts:469`), and `transparent` is not `expandable`, so the frontend drops the whole subtree. The next delta targets `[0, 1, 0, 0, 1]`, its parent at `[0, 1, 0, 0]` no longer exists, and the visitor throws.

#### Root cause

`StatusContainer._create` captures the delta path for later re-emits from the **parent's** cursor **before** the block is created (`lib/streamlit/elements/lib/mutable_status_container.py:81-91`):

```python
delta_path: list[int] = (
    parent._active_dg._cursor.delta_path if parent._active_dg._cursor else []
)

status_container = cast(
    "StatusContainer",
    parent._block(block_proto=block_proto, dg_type=StatusContainer),
)

# Apply initial configuration
status_container._delta_path = delta_path
```

Normally the parent cursor points at exactly the index where the new block lands, so the captured path identifies the status block correctly.

Since 1.59.0, a write from a fragment into a container declared outside that fragment is redirected into a per-fragment layout-transparent wrapper block. The status block therefore lands one level deeper than the captured path predicted, so `_delta_path` points at the wrapper instead of the status.

`update()` does not use the cursor. It builds a message and sets that stale path directly (`mutable_status_container.py:151`):

```python
msg.metadata.delta_path[:] = self._delta_path
msg.delta.add_block.CopyFrom(self._current_proto)
```

`__exit__` calls `update(state="complete")` whenever the state is still `running` (`mutable_status_container.py:185-204`), so an explicit `update()` call is not required to trigger this.

#### Scope of the trigger

Each row was checked in a browser against 1.59.1:

| Variant | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Same code without the fragment | works |
| Fragment, status, one `with` block | works |
| Fragment, status, one `with` block plus a later `update()` | works |
| Fragment, status, **two separate `with` blocks** | **crash** |
| Outside container is `st.container`, `st.popover`, or `st.expander` | crash in all three |
| Inner block is `outside.container()` instead of `outside.status()` | works |

`st.status` is the element that matters, because it is the one that re-emits its own block from a stored path. The type of the outside container does not matter.

The one-`with` case still emits the misdirected delta and still replaces the wrapper, but nothing is written inside the block afterwards, so no delta is left without a parent and no crash is visible. The element tree is already wrong in that case, which means this defect can also corrupt a page silently.

#### Related work

The 1.59.0 change that introduces the redirection is the outside-container-writes work: #15541, #15545, #15598, #15620, and #15623.

This looks close to #12514 (fragments inside a shared container), but it is a different defect. #16171 is the fix for #12514 and it is present in the nightly listed above, which still reproduces this crash.

#### Possible fix

Capture `_delta_path` after the block is created, from the path `_block()` actually wrote to, rather than predicting it from the parent cursor beforehand. It may be worth auditing any other element that stores a delta path and later enqueues a message with it directly.

#### Workarounds

Both verified on 1.59.1:

- Write everything to the status inside a single `with` block.
- Create the status on a container declared inside the fragment, or use `st.expander` or `st.container` instead of `st.status`.
