issues.title: Add a command menu / command palette widget (CMD+K)
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a native command menu / command palette widget that opens with a keyboard shortcut (e.g. `Cmd/Ctrl+K`) and lets users quickly search and trigger app-defined commands. Similar to the [`cmdk`](https://uiw.tf/cmdk) React component and the command palettes found in VS Code, Linear, Raycast, etc.

### Why?

Command palettes are a fast, keyboard-first way to navigate and act in an app — jumping between pages, running actions, changing settings, or searching. For data apps and internal tools with many pages/actions, this is a big UX and power-user win, and it's currently only achievable with custom components.

### How?

A widget that registers a searchable list of commands and opens as an overlay on `Cmd/Ctrl+K` (and/or programmatically). Rough sketch:

```python
choice = st.command_menu(
    [
        {"label": "Go to Dashboard", "icon": ":material/dashboard:", "group": "Navigation"},
        {"label": "Export data", "icon": ":material/download:", "group": "Actions"},
    ],
    placeholder="Type a command or search...",
)
if choice == "Export data":
    ...
```

Possible features:
- Fuzzy search, grouping/sections, icons, keyboard navigation.
- Customizable trigger shortcut and a programmatic open.
- Returns the selected command (rerun-based), similar to other widgets.
- Optionally integrate with multipage navigation (pages appear as commands automatically).

### Additional Context

- Prior art: [`cmdk`](https://uiw.tf/cmdk) (fast, composable command menu for React).

issues.title: Add a native 3D model viewer element
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a native element to display interactive 3D models (with orbit controls), similar to the existing [`three_viewer` in streamlit-extras](https://arnaudmiribel.github.io/streamlit-extras/extras/three_viewer/). It would render common 3D formats (GLTF/GLB, OBJ, STL, PLY, FBX) using Three.js, with drag-to-rotate, scroll-to-zoom, and pan.

### Why?

Displaying 3D models is a common need for CAD, scientific/medical visualization, product/asset previews, ML/3D reconstruction outputs, and gaming. Today users rely on the streamlit-extras component or custom components, which is extra setup and not officially maintained. A first-class element would make 3D viewing a one-liner and keep it maintained in-sync with Streamlit.

### How?

A new command, e.g. `st.model_viewer` / `st.three_viewer`, roughly mirroring the streamlit-extras API:

```python
st.model_viewer("model.glb")
st.model_viewer("https://example.com/model.gltf", height=600)
st.model_viewer(stl_bytes, file_format=".stl")
```

Parameters (to be refined):
- `source`: URL, local path, `bytes`, or file-like object.
- `file_format`: optional explicit format override (inferred otherwise).
- `height`: viewer height in pixels.
- `key`: widget key.

Supported formats: GLTF/GLB (recommended), OBJ, STL, PLY, FBX. Could later add options for background, camera, lighting, and auto-rotate.

### Additional Context

- Prior art: [streamlit-extras `three_viewer`](https://arnaudmiribel.github.io/streamlit-extras/extras/three_viewer/).

issues.title: Allow prepending/appending text (prefix/suffix addons) to `st.text_input`
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Allow prepending and appending static text to `st.text_input` (input-group-style "addons"), e.g. a `https://` prefix, an `@gmail.com` suffix, or a unit like `kg`. This is already partly covered by the `icon` parameter, but that only supports an icon, not arbitrary text.

### Why?

Prefix/suffix addons are a very common form pattern (URLs, usernames, currencies, units, domains). Today users either build custom components or hack it together with adjacent columns/markdown, which doesn't look integrated and misaligns with the input. Native support would make forms cleaner and more professional with minimal effort.

### How?

Add optional parameters to prepend/append text to the input, rendered as attached addons inside/adjacent to the input field. For example:

```python
st.text_input("Website", prefix="https://")
st.text_input("Email", suffix="@gmail.com")
st.text_input("Weight", suffix="kg")
```

Naming TBD (e.g. `prefix`/`suffix` vs `prepend`/`append`). The added text is display-only and not part of the widget's returned value. Could build on the existing `icon` addon slot.

### Additional Context

- Partly covered today by the `icon` parameter of `st.text_input`.
- Related: #6704 (specialized input types for `st.text_input`).

issues.title: Add dedicated development and production modes to optimize app execution
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Introduce an explicit **development mode** vs. **production mode** distinction for Streamlit apps, with each mode optimizing execution and UI for its use case. By default, use development mode when we detect local development, with a configuration option to set it explicitly.

### Why?

Streamlit currently treats local development and deployed apps the same. Local development benefits from richer debugging and warnings, while deployed apps benefit from performance optimizations and a cleaner, end-user-facing UI. A clear mode distinction lets us tune both without compromise.

### How?

**Detection / opt-in:** config option, CLI flag, environment variable, or request origin (e.g. requests from `127.0.0.1` are likely the developer — with a caveat for Docker-based dev). Possibly a dedicated `streamlit debug app.py` command to promote the feature.

**Production mode — optimize execution & clean up UI:**
- Skip code-hashing in `st.cache_data` / `st.cache_resource` (small speedup when the code isn't changing).
- Disable the file watcher to save resources — but keep it enabled on Streamlit Community Cloud.
- Route deprecation/dev warnings and parameter-hash warnings to stderr instead of printing them in the app UI.
- Optionally hide/simplify the hamburger menu,

**Development mode — a "Debug Toolbar"-style panel** (e.g. a button in the bottom corner, similar to "Manage app"), with focused sub-panels:
- Cache inspector (view & clear cache).
- Metrics panel.
- SQLAlchemy / SQL query inspector.
- Variable, state, and cache inspection/visualization.
- Show deprecation & dev-specific warnings in the browser.
- Theme editing, preheating, and other WYSIWYG dev conveniences.

**Open question:** naming — "Development / Production" vs. "Debug / Release" mode.

### Additional Context

- Related: [Ability to hide the hamburger menu (#395)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/395)
- Prior art: [Django Debug Toolbar](https://django-debug-toolbar.readthedocs.io/) and [streamlit-forum](https://github.com/snehankekre/streamlit-forum).

issues.title: Add a `streamlit dockerize` CLI command to package an app into a Docker image
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `streamlit dockerize` CLI command that automatically turns a given Streamlit app into a Docker image (generating a sensible `Dockerfile` and building the image), so users can containerize and deploy their app with a single command.

### Why?

We should make it super easy to deploy Streamlit apps anywhere, and the obvious place to start is making it easier to dockerize an app. Today users have to hand-write a `Dockerfile`, figure out dependencies, ports, and entrypoints themselves. A one-command flow lowers the barrier to deploying Streamlit apps on any container platform.

### How?

Introduce a command such as:

```bash
streamlit dockerize app.py
```

It could:
- Generate a sensible `Dockerfile` for the project (base image, dependency install from `requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml`, exposed port, correct `streamlit run` entrypoint).
- Optionally build the image directly (e.g. `--build`, `--tag`).
- Detect and include project dependencies and config automatically.

### Additional Context

Part of a broader "make it easy to deploy Streamlit apps anywhere" effort.

issues.body:

### Summary

Streamlit renders Altair plots perfectly as long as they are visualized within a browser.

However, if i want to download the graph as a .png, the downloaded file is very low quality (blurry). 

This can be validated by going here and downloading an image from any of the charts:
https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/charts/st.altair_chart

This makes it impossible to use these downloaded PNG:s in a report (powerpoint).

This seems to because altair defaults to using a PPI of 72 when rendering. Altair does support using a 'ppi' parameter when calling chart.save:
https://altair-viz.github.io/user_guide/saving_charts.html#png-figure-size-resolution

In order to create and download a higher-resolution image i can run the following code:

```python
    b = st.altair_chart(chart, use_container_width=False)

    chart.save("test.png", ppi=200)
    with open("test.png", "rb") as file:
        btn = st.download_button(label="Download image", data=file, file_name="test.png", mime="image/png")
```

**The problem with this approach is that the Streamlit theme is not used in the resulting graph.**


Is there any way to support:
* Setting PPI to be used for "Save as PNG" calls?
* Using the Streamlit theme in chart.save ?

### Reproducible Code Example
In order to create a higher-resolution image i can run the following code:
```Python
    b = st.altair_chart(chart, use_container_width=False)

    chart.save("test.png", ppi=200)
    with open("test.png", "rb") as file:
        btn = st.download_button(label="Download image", data=file, file_name="test.png", mime="image/png")

```
The problem with this approach is that the Streamlit theme is not used in the resulting graph.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Go to https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/charts/st.altair_chart
2. Click "Download as PNG" from any of the charts
3. Open the blurry image from your downloads folder

### Expected Behavior

issues.title: Button or API for users to switch between themes
issues.body:
### Problem

As of now (version 1.15.2), for users to switch the theme, they have to go to the hamburger menu to access the setting. This is not very intuitive for the end users if they are not familiar with Streamlit. In addition, if I hide the hamburger menu in my app, the users won't be able to change the theme by themselves at all.

### Solution

It would be nice to have a button outside the hamburger menu for users to quickly switch between light mode and dark mode (or other themes if available). 

Another solution would be to provide an API for switching between the themes, so the developers can implement the theme switcher by themselves if needed.

issues.title: `st.download_button` rejects documented `io.StringIO` data
issues.body:
## Summary

`st.download_button` documents `io.StringIO` as a supported file-like value, and the public typing tests accept it, but the runtime raises `StreamlitAPIException`. This affects both eager values and deferred callables because they share the same data conversion helper.

## Reproducible Code Example

```python
import io

import streamlit as st

st.download_button("Download", data=io.StringIO("hello"))
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Save the example as `app.py`.
2. Run `streamlit run app.py`.
3. Observe the exception while the download button is created.

## Expected Behavior

The download button is rendered and downloads `hello` as `text/plain`, matching the documented `io.StringIO` support.

## Current Behavior

Streamlit raises:

```text
streamlit.errors.StreamlitAPIException:
Invalid binary data format: <class '_io.StringIO'>
```

`convert_data_to_bytes_and_infer_mime` handles `str` and the concrete `io.TextIOWrapper`, but not `io.StringIO`. The public `DownloadButtonDataType` and typing test already accept `io.StringIO`.

## Debug info

- Streamlit version: current `develop` (`1.60.0`)
- Python version: 3.11.15
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: not applicable; the exception occurs during script execution

## Additional Information

A focused fix and regression test are available in [ShiroKSH/streamlit@e4e7da440](https://github.com/ShiroKSH/streamlit/commit/e4e7da4400646822221cbdeb9423467d0ce4264b). It reads `io.StringIO` with `getvalue()`, matching the existing `io.BytesIO` behavior without changing the stream cursor.

Validated with:

- `make check`
- `uv run pytest lib/tests/streamlit/runtime/download_data_util_test.py -q`
- `uv run pytest lib/tests/streamlit/elements/download_button_test.py -q`
- `uv run pytest lib/tests/streamlit/runtime/media_file_manager_test.py -k execute_deferred -q`

issues.title: Reconnect to existing sessions instead of creating new upon unclean websocket close.
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Similar to the issues linked, if the network connection is intermittent/flaky the existing session is lost and a new one created, causing unpleasant/unexpected user experience.

See:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1386
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1628
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6442

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time

if "counter" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.counter = 0

st.write(f"Run count = {st.session_state.counter}")

st.session_state.counter += 1

time.sleep(3)

st.rerun()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the reproducible code example provided in streamlit on one server host.
2. Observe the "Run count = X" increase steadily in a client host different from the server host.
3. Disable the client network connection and wait for some arbitrary time duration.
4. Re-enable the client network connection.
5. Observer the "Run count = X" start from zero again.

### Expected Behavior

The user session should be restored so they may continue where they left off in the face of their network/internet connection being flaky (packet drops, high latency etc) causing unclean websocket close behind the scenes.

### Current Behavior

Observe streamlit warning log "Session with id %s is already connected! Connecting to a new session." and user loses their streamlit session and starts afresh.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.35
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: Chrome/Firefox


### Additional Information

I have been able to make a potentially naive code change (will link a PR as a proposal to this issue) which I am unable to run against full test suite because I have been unable to build the streamlit project. I have been able to test partially by modifying the python code in my installed streamlit venv.

issues.title: [Request for feedback] Starlette/ASGI Support in Streamlit
issues.body:
Starting with **Streamlit 1.53**, we're introducing experimental support for running Streamlit with [Starlette](https://www.starlette.io/) as the underlying web framework. This is the first step toward our long-term goal of **fully migrating from Tornado to Starlette/ASGI**, and we need your help to identify any issues or gaps before the full transition. ## What's New > **Note:** To use the experimental Starlette features, you need to install the optional dependencies: > > ```bash > pip install streamlit[starlette] > ``` ### 1. Starlette Server Mode (Experimental) You can now run Streamlit using Starlette instead of Tornado by setting a config option: ```toml # .streamlit/config.toml [server] useStarlette = true ``` Or via command line: ```bash streamlit run app.py --server.useStarlette=true ``` ### 2. ASGI App Entry Point (Experimental) For advanced use cases, you can now create an ASGI-compatible Streamlit application using the new `App` class: ```python from streamlit.starlette import App app = App("main.py") ``` Run it with `streamlit run` (preferred): ```bash streamlit run myapp.py ``` Streamlit will automatically detect the `App` instance and run it in Starlette mode. Alternatively, you can use any ASGI server directly: ```bash uvicorn myapp:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8501 ``` The `App` class supports advanced configuration including: - **Custom HTTP routes** — Add REST API endpoints alongside your Streamlit app - **Middleware** — Add security headers, authentication, logging, etc. - **Lifespan hooks** — Run code on startup/shutdown (e.g., pre-warm caches, initialize resources) - **Framework integration** — Mount Streamlit inside FastAPI, Django, or other ASGI frameworks > 📖 For more details on the `App` interface and its full capabilities, see the [specification in PR #13449](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/13449).
Example: Adding custom routes ```python from streamlit.starlette import App from starlette.routing import Route from starlette.responses import JSONResponse async def health_check(request): return JSONResponse({"status": "healthy", "service": "streamlit-app"}) async def get_data(request): return JSONResponse({"items": ["apple", "banana", "cherry"], "count": 3}) app = App( "main.py", routes=[ Route("/api/health", health_check), Route("/api/data", get_data), ], ) ```
Example: Adding custom middleware ```python from streamlit.starlette import App from starlette.middleware import Middleware from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware class SecurityHeadersMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware): async def dispatch(self, request, call_next): response = await call_next(request) response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff" response.headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "SAMEORIGIN" return response app = App( "main.py", middleware=[Middleware(SecurityHeadersMiddleware)], ) ```
Example: Mounting FastAPI in Streamlit ```python from fastapi import FastAPI from starlette.routing import Mount from streamlit.starlette import App # Create FastAPI sub-application api = FastAPI() @api.get("/health") async def health(): return {"status": "healthy"} @api.post("/predict") async def predict(data: dict): return {"prediction": data.get("value", 0) * 2} # Mount FastAPI into Streamlit app # - Streamlit UI at / # - FastAPI endpoints at /api/* # - FastAPI docs at /api/docs app = App( "dashboard.py", routes=[Mount("/api", app=api)], ) ```
Example: Mounting Streamlit in FastAPI ```python from fastapi import FastAPI from streamlit.starlette import App # Create the Streamlit sub-application streamlit_app = App("dashboard.py") # Create FastAPI with Streamlit's lifespan to manage the runtime lifecycle api = FastAPI(lifespan=streamlit_app.lifespan()) @api.get("/api/data") async def get_data(): return {"data": [1, 2, 3]} # Mount Streamlit under /dashboard api.mount("/dashboard", streamlit_app) # Run with: uvicorn myapp:api ```
Example: Lifespan hooks for startup/shutdown ```python from contextlib import asynccontextmanager from streamlit.starlette import App @asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(app): # Startup: runs before accepting connections print("🚀 Starting up...") model = load_ml_model() # Pre-warm caches db = init_db_connection() # Yield state accessible via app.state yield {"model": model, "db": db} # Shutdown: cleanup resources print("👋 Shutting down...") db.close() app = App("main.py", lifespan=lifespan) ```
## Why We're Migrating to Starlette/ASGI The migration to Starlette/ASGI will unlock numerous frequently-requested features: ### Custom HTTP Endpoints - #439 - #9673 - #6195 - #9090 - #11333 - #8713 ### Security Headers & Middleware - #6417 - #9160 - #861 - #8823 ### Framework Integration & ASGI Support - #4311 - #4567 - #927 - #7546 ### Server Configuration & Lifecycle - #7688 - #8991 - #6108 - #9916 - #8545 - #7667 - #11050 - #10543 - #3426 - #8661 ### SEO & Metadata - #5673 - #8999 ### Advanced App Execution - #4162 - #9450 - #12972 - #662 ## We Need Your Feedback Since we plan to eventually make Starlette the default (and only) server backend, we want to catch any compatibility issues early. Please help us by: ### 1. Try it out Enable Starlette mode in your existing apps: ```bash streamlit run your_app.py --server.useStarlette=true ``` ### 2. Report any issues If you encounter problems, please comment below with: - **What happened** — Error messages, unexpected behavior - **Your environment** — OS, Python version, Streamlit version - **How to reproduce** — Minimal code example if possible - **Comparison** — Does the issue occur with the default Tornado server? ### 3. Share your use cases We're especially interested in: - ⚡ Performance comparisons (response times, memory usage, concurrent users) - 🔌 Integration scenarios (FastAPI, Django, other ASGI frameworks) - 🛡️ Security/middleware requirements - 🚀 Deployment configurations (uvicorn, gunicorn, hypercorn, cloud platforms) ## Known Limitations - This is **experimental** — APIs may change before the final release - TBD --- **Thank you for helping us build a better Streamlit!** Your early feedback is invaluable in ensuring a smooth transition for the entire community. 🙏 Please comment below with your experiences, questions, or concerns. ![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-13600)

issues.title: Unify PNG export scale (DPR-aware) across Altair, Mermaid, and Plotly
issues.body:
### Problem

PNG export behavior is inconsistent across chart types:

- **Altair / Vega-Lite** (fixed in #16170): DPR-aware, floor of 2× via `Math.max(2, window.devicePixelRatio || 1)`.
- **Mermaid** (`frontend/lib/src/components/shared/StreamlitMarkdown/MermaidChart.tsx:592`): hard-coded `const scale = 2` on a raw canvas draw, DPR-unaware.
- **Plotly** (`frontend/lib/src/components/elements/PlotlyChart/…`): never sets `config.toImageButtonOptions.scale`, so downloads export at 1×.

Users get different export fidelity depending on which chart they downloaded, which is surprising.

### Proposal

Converge on a DPR-aware helper (e.g., `getMinExportScale()` that returns `Math.max(2, window.devicePixelRatio || 1)`) shared by:

1. `useVegaEmbed.exportToPng` — already using this expression inline (should be swapped to the helper).
2. `MermaidChart` — replace the hard-coded `2` in the canvas draw.
3. `PlotlyChart` — pipe the value into `toImageButtonOptions.scale`.

Test coverage per chart to lock the behavior in.

### Context

Called out by @sfc-gh-nbellante in review of #16170.

### Non-goals

- Not an upper bound on `scaleFactor` — separate consideration.

issues.title: Vertical st.segmented_control
Disable chat_input submit button if uploaded files exceed size limit or uploads fail or file format mismatch
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

When st.chat_input (and st.file_uploader) accept files, a file that exceeds max_upload_size or otherwise fails to upload is flagged with an error chip in the UI, but the submit button stays enabled — so the user can still send the message with a failed or missing attachment. Please provide a way to automatically disable the submit button while any attached file is over the limit, errored, or still uploading, so an incomplete/invalid set of files can't be submitted. Ideally also expose the per-file upload status so developers can gate submission themselves.

### Why?

There's currently no way to stop a chat submission when an upload fails. max_upload_size (from #12692) rejects oversized files before upload, which is great, but the rejected file is then silently dropped — it never appears in the returned ChatInputValue.files / st.file_uploader value, and st.chat_input returns None until submit, so no upload status is available to Python before the user hits send. As a result the app can't detect the failure or set disabled= off it.

The practical impact:
- The user attaches 3 files, 1 is over the limit → only 2 upload, the failed one is invisible to the app, and the user can still submits mistakenly believing all 3 went. The app then runs on a partial/incorrect set — wrong results, wasted compute/tokens (very common in LLM apps), and confusion.
- Submitting while a file is still uploading can send an incomplete set.
- submit_mode only governs behavior after submit (disable/stop during the run), so it doesn't help gate submission on upload state.

### How?

Two complementary options:

1. A built-in guard — a parameter that auto-disables the submit button until every attached file has uploaded successfully. For example:

st.chat_input(
       "Type a message…",
       accept_file="multiple",
       max_upload_size=1,
       block_submit_on_upload_error=True,  # submit stays disabled while any file errors/uploads
   )

2. Expose the upload status so developers can implement their own logic — e.g. a list of {name, size, status} (uploading / success / error) available on rerun before submit, so we can do disabled=any(f.status != "success" for f in files).

Desired behavior (matching the natural mental model): submit is enabled only when all attached files have status success. If the user deletes an errored file, it drops out of the status list, and since the remaining files are already success, submit re-enables. In short: track upload status per file before submit, and let it drive the submit button.

### Additional Context

issues.title: Enhance menu button with download payload capability
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

The new `st.menu_button` is a welcome addition. It would be more useful if it could be combined with download behavior: the user picks an export format from a menu (for example Markdown, plain text, or PDF), and Streamlit serves the matching file without requiring a separate `st.download_button` or fragile conditional wiring for each format.
The idea is a single control—similar to an **Export** menu in desktop apps—where each menu option is tied to download metadata (`data`, `file_name`, `mime`) so “choose format → file downloads” is a first-class pattern.


### Why?

Today, `st.menu_button` only communicates **which option was selected** on the rerun where the user picks something; **sending bytes to the browser still requires `st.download_button`** (or other workarounds). In practice that causes:
- **Awkward UX**: pick a format from the menu, then click again to download—or rely on `st.session_state` because the menu’s return value resets on later reruns.
- **Repeated boilerplate**: every app reimplements mapping from “format label” → `data` / `file_name` / `mime`.
- **Cost vs. laziness**: precomputing every variant (e.g. large PDFs or zips) wastes CPU and memory; deferring generation until after a choice fights Streamlit’s rerun model unless authors invent their own patterns.
A combined primitive would match common product UI, reduce custom session-state hacks, and make multi-format export easier to build and maintain.

### How?

Ship either a **new widget** (for example `st.download_menu_button`) or an **extension** of `st.menu_button` / `st.download_button` so one control can:
1. Show a dropdown of export labels.
2. On selection, trigger a download using the **payload mapped to that label**.
**Options API (sketch for discussion)**
Accept a structured mapping instead of plain string labels only, for example:
- A **list of tuples or small dicts**, e.g. `(label, file_name, mime, data)`; or  
- A **dict** keyed by label with values like `{ "data": ..., "file_name": ..., "mime": ... }`.
**Lazy payloads**
Allow `data` (or the equivalent field) to be a **callable** that Streamlit invokes **only when that option is chosen**, so expensive exports are not built on every rerun. Document when the callable runs, error handling, and any constraints (e.g. serialization, size limits).

issues.title: Native support for multi-level nested keys in widget `st.session_state` assignments
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

### Problem
When building complex, dynamic forms in Streamlit (e.g., configuration builders, dynamic rows with reordering, or nested JSON editors), `st.session_state` forces developers into a flat key-value architecture. 





### Why?

Currently, if a user wants to update a nested dictionary or list, they have to use flat keys like `key=f"rep_sales_{row_id}_email"` and then write boilerplate code (either `on_change` callbacks or post-run loop reconstruction) to reassemble those flat keys back into a nested Python dictionary or data class. This leads to bloated code, higher risk of state desync (especially when reordering UI elements), and poor developer ergonomics.

### How?

### Proposed Solution
Allow the `key` parameter in input widgets to accept multi-level paths, automatically updating the deeply nested structure inside `st.session_state` when the widget value changes. Here are three potential API designs:

**Option A: State Reference Proxy (Best for IDE Type Hints & Autocomplete)**
Introduce a `st.path` proxy object or a `st.bind` method. This allows developers to use standard dictionary/attribute access—enabling IDE type hints and auto-completion—without Python prematurely evaluating the value before Streamlit sees it.
```python
# Approach 1: Path Proxy
st.text_input(
    "Sales Rep Email", 
    key=st.path.representatives["sales"][2]["email"]
)

# Approach 2: Object Binding (excellent for typed dataclasses)
rep = st.session_state.representatives["sales"][2]
st.text_input(
    "Sales Rep Email", 
    key=st.bind(rep, "email")
)
```

**Option B: String-based Pathing**
Allow a string that represents the path. While this lacks strict type-hinting, it is highly readable and easy to implement using standard dictionary traversal.
```python
# Automatically updates st.session_state.representatives["sales"][2]["email"]
st.text_input(
    "Sales Rep Email", 
    key='representatives["sales"][2]["email"]', 
    multi_level_key=True
)
```

**Option C: Tuple/List Pathing (Pythonic Backend Approach)**
This avoids string parsing entirely, providing a clean programmatic way to define the traversal path.
```python
# Automatically updates st.session_state.representatives["sales"][2]["email"]
st.text_input(
    "Sales Rep Email", 
    key=("representatives", "sales", 2, "email")
)
```

### Expected Behavior
1. If the base key (`representatives`) does not exist in `st.session_state`, Streamlit should throw a `KeyError` (or initialize it, depending on preferred design).
2. If the path exists, when the user types in the widget, Streamlit natively traverses the nested dictionary/list and updates the final leaf node with the new widget value.
3. The widget reads its initial `value` directly from that nested path, eliminating the need to manually pass `value=st.session_state["representatives"]["sales"][2]["email"]`.

### Alternatives Considered
* **`on_change` callbacks with `kwargs`:** Developers currently do this by passing the path arguments to a callback function that mutates the dictionary. This requires declaring a separate function for every type of input, which gets incredibly tedious.
* **Third-party state wrappers:** Using external libraries or custom Python `@property` wrappers to handle the sync between flat widget keys and nested object structures. While functional, nested structures are common enough that native support would vastly improve the developer experience.

### Additional Context

As Streamlit apps grow from simple scripts into full-fledged CRUD applications and internal tools, dynamic layouts (like adding/removing rows of structured data) become the norm. Tying widget state directly to a durable, deeply nested structure rather than a flat string would solve an entire class of state-sync bugs related to dynamic UIs and list reordering.

issues.body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary I have an issue with `st.fragment`s within a container disappearing on rerender. The initial render works as expected, but after the first user interaction within the fragment, the container seems to act somewhat like an `st.empty()`. It only happens under very particular conditions. I isolated the issue by simplifying my example as much as possible. Of course, that example now looks silly, but in my app, these "particular conditions" have reasons to be. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import streamlit as st @st.fragment # Has to be a fragment. def a(): st.button("Rerender `a()`") container = st.container() with container: b(1) with container: # Has to be a separate `with`. b(2) @st.fragment # Has to be a fragment. def b(i: int): st.markdown(i) a() ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Try the above code example. 2. On the initial render, you should see "1" and "2". 3. Click the "Rerender `a()`" button. 4. Notice the "1" is now gone. 5. Variations: - If you add anything after `with container: b(2)`, say `container.markdown(3)`, the "2" will also disappear, leaving only the "3". - If you replace `st.container()` with `st.columns(1)[0]`, `st.expander("")`, `st.popover("")`, or `st.tabs(("Tab",))[0]`, the same issue happens. 7. If you remove any one of the three lines with a comment, it avoids the issue. These three conditions are necessary to reproduce the issue. ### Expected Behavior Always seeing "1" and "2", even after a rerender. ### Current Behavior Initial render: After clicking the "Rerender `a()`" button: ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.49.1 - Python version: 3.11.9 - Operating System: MacOS - Browser: Chrome ### Additional Information See `Steps To Reproduce` #7 for workarounds. Personally, I am not blocked; I am fine with the second workaround. I just thought I'd share my findings since it took me a whiiile to identify the issue, and it's clearly unexpected.

issues.title: st.data_editor NumberColumn commits after first keystroke when a CJK IME (Japanese/Korean) is active — regression in 1.59.0+ (works in 1.58.0)
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When editing a `NumberColumn` cell in `st.data_editor` while a CJK IME (Japanese / Korean input method) is active, the cell editor commits after the **first keystroke**, making it impossible to type multi-digit numbers (e.g. typing `15` commits `1`).

This is a **regression introduced between 1.58.0 and 1.59.0**: the same app and the same input method work correctly on 1.58.0. The bug persists in 1.60.0.

Typing the same digits with the IME switched to direct alphanumeric input works fine on all versions, which points to IME composition events (`compositionstart` / `isComposing`) not being handled by the cell overlay editor.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"Mon": [8], "Tue": [9]}, index=["item"])
df.index.name = "name"

edited = st.data_editor(
    df,
    num_rows="fixed",
    column_config={
        c: st.column_config.NumberColumn(c, min_value=0, step=1, format="%d")
        for c in df.columns
    },
)
st.write(edited)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. On macOS, enable a CJK input method (reproduced with Japanese and Korean IME).
2. Run the app above on Streamlit 1.59.0 or 1.60.0.
3. Double-click a number cell to open the cell editor.
4. With the IME **on**, type `15`.

### Expected Behavior

The cell accepts both keystrokes and commits `15` (this is the behavior on 1.58.0, and on 1.59.0+ when the IME is off / direct alphanumeric input is used).

### Current Behavior

The cell editor commits immediately after the first keystroke; the cell ends up with `1` and the editor closes. Multi-digit input is impossible while the IME is active.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. Works in **1.58.0**, broken in **1.59.0** and **1.60.0**.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.59.0 and 1.60.0 (broken), 1.58.0 (works)
- Python version: 3.11 (Linux container / Railway) — also observed from macOS clients
- Operating System (client): macOS (multiple machines)
- Browser: not browser-specific in our testing (the determining factor is whether the IME is composing; direct alphanumeric input works on the same machines/browsers)

### Additional Information

- In production this hit users editing production-planning quantities: users typing numbers with a Japanese/Korean IME still enabled could only enter single-digit values.
- Workaround we use: switch the IME to direct alphanumeric mode before typing digits.
- This looks like the classic IME pitfall where key handling ignores `KeyboardEvent.isComposing` / composition events, so the first keystroke during composition is treated as a complete edit. Streamlit had a similar IME issue in another component in the past (#6988, `st.chat_input`).

issues.title: Look for Configuration Files in Platform-Recommended Directories
issues.body:
# Problem

Streamlit uses the home directory for its configuration, but that adds _another_ config file to pollute a home directory. We should be good platform citizens and provide thoughtful locations for configuration files.

# Solution

We as a team agreed on the following order:

1. `$PROJECT_FOLDER/.streamlit`
2. (great if possible, but not required) `$PROJECT_FOLDER/{../}+.streamlit` (i.e. any subfolder containing .streamlit)
3. `~/.config/streamlit` if Unix/macOS (or in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, if defined), `%CSIDL_COMMON_APPDATA%/streamlit` if Windows (that's [`ProgramData`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/usmt/usmt-recognized-environment-variables), meaning we follow Git and Conda)
4. `~/.streamlit`

### Additional context

See Closed Pull Request #1907

issues.title: Server-side validation of client-side widget constraints
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Widget constraints like `options` allow-lists, `disabled`, `num_rows`, `max_chars`, and DataFrame column `validate` are enforced only in the browser, so a forged `WidgetState`/`BackMsg` can submit out-of-constraint values that flow into `st.session_state`, callbacks, and return values. We could add a way to have Streamlit re-check these constraints server-side.


### Why?

Many developers reasonably assume `st.selectbox(options=[...])` can only return one of its options, or that `disabled=True` blocks a value/callback — but that only holds client-side. Relying on it today means hand-rolling server-side validation for every widget, which is easy to forget.

### How?

Enforce declared widget constraints server-side by default in the widget deserialize path — validating the incoming value against `options` allow-lists, `min_value`/`max_value`, `max_chars`, `disabled=True`, and `st.data_editor` `disabled`/`num_rows`/column `validate`. On a violation, coerce to a valid value (reset to default / clamp), consistent with how Streamlit already handles stale `options` today, so normal frontend/backend sync races don't break.

### Additional Context

_No response_

issues.title: ProgressColumn: allow per-row max_value (bar scaled to each row's own total)
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

`st.column_config.ProgressColumn` only accepts a single scalar `max_value` that applies to the **entire column**. There is no way to set a **per-row** maximum, so you cannot render a progress bar whose fill reflects each row's own denominator.

This matters whenever each row has its own "total" and you want the bar to show `value / that_row's_total` (a within-row proportion) while still displaying the raw `value` in the cell.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

# Each row has its own denominator ("total"). We'd like every progress bar to be
# filled relative to that row's own total:
#   - "small task": 8 / 10   = 80% done
#   - "big task"  : 20 / 1000 = 2%  done
df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "task": ["small task", "big task"],
        "done": [8, 20],       # raw value shown in the cell
        "total": [10, 1000],   # per-row denominator we'd want the bar scaled to
    }
)

st.dataframe(
    df,
    column_config={
        "done": st.column_config.ProgressColumn(
            "done", min_value=0, max_value=1000  # one fixed max for ALL rows
        ),
    },
    hide_index=True,
)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above.
2. Observe the `done` column: "small task" (actually 80% complete) shows a bar filled to `8/1000 ≈ 1%`, while "big task" (2% complete) shows `20/1000 = 2%`.
3. The bar lengths do not reflect each row's own progress. Setting `max_value=10` instead makes "big task" overflow the bar.

### Expected Behavior

A way to scale each row's progress bar to that row's own maximum — e.g. one of:

- `max_value` (and/or `min_value`) accepting the name of another column to read the per-row bound from, e.g. `max_value="total"`, or
- `max_value` accepting a callable / per-row value, or
- documented guidance for the intended pattern.

So that `done=8, total=10` renders an 80% bar and `done=20, total=1000` renders a 2% bar, while the cell still displays the raw `done` value.

### Current Workaround

Precompute the percentage into a separate column and use a fixed `max_value=100`, but then the cell shows the percentage instead of the raw count — you can't show the raw value and a per-row-scaled bar at the same time.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.60.0
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: N/A (server-side column_config)

### Additional Information

`inspect.signature(st.column_config.ProgressColumn)` shows `max_value: int | float | None` — a scalar only, with no per-row/callable variant.

issues.title: `st.expander` content permanently clipped — interrupted open/close animation leaves inline height/overflow lock on `<details>`
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

After certain sequences of expanding and collapsing multiple `st.expander`s
on a long page, one expander can end up **permanently clipped**: it shows
part of its content and cuts off the rest, and the page cannot scroll to
the hidden remainder. The state persists until a rerun/reload replaces the
element.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
A deterministic minimal repro is hard because the bug is a race in the
animation cleanup (analysis below). The sequence that reproduces it on our
production app (a long page with ~7 expanders, several containing multiple
`st.plotly_chart`s):


import streamlit as st
import numpy as np

for i in range(7):
    with st.expander(f"Section {i}", expanded=(i < 3)):
        for j in range(3):
            st.line_chart(np.random.randn(200, 3))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Expand the collapsed sections at the bottom of the page.
2. Collapse the expanded sections at the top.
3. Collapse the bottom sections again, then re-expand them, without waiting
   for animations to settle.
4. (May take a few attempts — it's a race between interrupted animations
   and content resize, so chart-heavy expanders make it likelier.)

### Expected Behavior

The re-expanded section shows all of its content.

### Current Behavior

The section renders at a stale fixed height with the tail of its content
clipped and unreachable. In dev tools, the `<details>` element inside
`div[data-testid="stExpander"]` carries a leftover inline
`overflow: hidden` (and, depending on which path failed, an inline
`height: <px>` and/or a still-live Web-Animations effect holding the
height — the latter is invisible in the Styles panel).

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.59.2
- Python version: 3.11 (conda)
- Operating System: Windows 11 Enterprise
- Browser: Edge (Chromium)


### Additional Information

## Analysis (root cause in the frontend animation cleanup)

In `frontend/lib/src/components/elements/Expander/useDetailsAnimation.ts`
(1.59.2; identical on `develop` as of 2026-07-15), both `animateTo` and
`animateResize` lock the element before animating:

```ts
cancelAnimation()
details.style.height = `${currentHeight}px`
details.style.overflow = "hidden"
```

and rely on `animateHeight`'s WAAPI **finish** listener to clear the lock:

```ts
animation.addEventListener("finish", () => {
  element.style.height = ""
  element.style.overflow = ""
  ...
})
animation.addEventListener("cancel", () => {
  resolve()   // <-- inline styles NOT cleared on cancel
})
```

So every **cancelled** animation leaves `height: <px>; overflow: hidden`
inline on the `<details>`, on the assumption that a follow-up animation
will always take over and eventually finish. Paths where that assumption
breaks:

1. **Cancel with no successor.** Rapid toggle sequences across several
   expanders (each toggle calls `cancelAnimation()` first) can end a chain
   on a cancel — e.g. when the debounced ResizeObserver callback bails on
   its early-return guards (`!details.open` / `!isOpenRef.current`) or the
   height delta is under `RESIZE_THRESHOLD_PX`, so no new animation is ever
   scheduled to clean up.
2. **The deliberate `contentHeight === 0` lock** in `animateTo` (open path)
   keeps the inline lock and waits for the ResizeObserver to heal it; if
   the (10 ms-debounced) callback hits an early return, the lock stays.
3. **Unmount cleanup** calls `cancelAnimation()` without clearing styles
   (harmless when the DOM node is discarded, but part of the same pattern).

`StyledDetails` in `styled-components.ts` sets no `height`/`overflow` of
its own, so any inline `overflow: hidden` observed on the `<details>` at
rest is always residue from this cleanup gap.

## Suggested fix

Clear the inline styles in the `cancel` listener (or in
`cancelAnimation()`) and have the follow-up animation re-lock immediately
— callers already re-lock synchronously right after cancelling, so
clearing on cancel is safe and makes "locked with nothing running" an
unreachable state. Alternatively, use `animation.finished`/`.oncancel`
with a `finally`-style cleanup.

## Additional Information

Workaround we're shipping: a small watchdog script that clears leftover
inline `height`/`overflow` from `stExpander` `<details>` elements whenever
no height animation is currently running (and cancels one still running

issues.title: Joining user threads
issues.body:
### Problem

This request is related to #1792. There is no mechanism currently to join user issued threads from the script runner thread.

### Solution

**MVP:** 

After some digging, I think the simplest way to address this is to kill all active threads stored in the session state during `AppSession.shutdown`. (I don't know where the cached variables are stored, but something similar for those as well.)

Below is my minimal working example, monkey patching `AppSession.shutdown`:

```python
import streamlit as st
import time
import asyncio
import threading

# monkey patch to kill all active threads stored in the session state
from streamlit.runtime.app_session import AppSession

_shutdown = None

def app_session_shutdown(appsession):
    # kill all threads in the session state
    states = appsession._session_state
    for key in states:
        val = states[key]
        if isinstance(val, threading.Thread) and val.is_alive() and not val.isDaemon():
            val.join()

    # run the normal AppSession.shutdown
    _shutdown(appsession)

if AppSession.shutdown != app_session_shutdown:
    _shutdown = AppSession.shutdown
    AppSession.shutdown = app_session_shutdown

# END MONKEY PATCHING

class AsyncThread(threading.Thread):
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.started = threading.Event()
        self.join_req = None

    def get_time(self, delay=1):
        """user function interface"""
        future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(self._get_time(delay), self.loop)
        return future.result()  # Wait for the result:

    async def _get_time(self, delay):
        """user function implementation"""
        await asyncio.sleep(delay)
        return time.strftime("%X")

    def start(self) -> None:
        """waits until thread is running"""
        super().start()
        self.started.wait()

    def join(self):
        """release main()"""
        if self.join_req:
            self.loop.call_soon_threadsafe(self.join_req.set)
        super().join()

    def run(self):
        """Thread function. Run until join_req is set"""

        async def main():
            self.loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
            self.started.set()
            self.join_req = asyncio.Event()
            await self.join_req.wait()

        asyncio.run(main())

if "async_thread" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["async_thread"] = th = AsyncThread()
    th.start()

st.text(st.session_state["async_thread"].get_time())
st.button("Click bottom to update the time")
```


When applied on the source, the relevant lines in `app_session_shutdown()` should be placed in [L203 of `runtime/app_session.py`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/7ec02a14bddbf866e36b1fe24a25afe72a5975b1/lib/streamlit/runtime/app_session.py#L203)

**Preferred solution:** 

Introduce the `blinker.signal` mechanism (which is already being used for the `ScriptRunner` class) in `AppSession` to allow users to assign arbitrary shutdown event handlers.

issues.title: Using multiprocessing module
issues.body:
### Problem

I have some CPU-bound tasks and want to use `multiprocessing` module.

But, `multiprocessing` module can only used in `if __name__ == "__main__"` or with in a function.

For example, a flask app:

```python
from multiprocessing import Pool
import time
from flask import Flask

app = Flask(__name__)

def expensive_function(x):
    time.sleep(4)
    return x*x


@app.route('/')
def expcalc():
    t = time.time()
    with Pool() as p:
        f = p.map(expensive_function, range(4))
    return f'time: {time.time() -t }, Result is'+str(f)

if __name__=='__main__':
    app.run()

```
Either `python app.py` or `gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:5000 app:app` is okey.

BUT, if I do it in streamlit:

```python
from time import sleep, time
import streamlit as st
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed, ProcessPoolExecutor
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

st.title("parallel")

def slow_process(width:int):
    sleep(3)
    return pd.DataFrame(np.random.rand(3,width))


input_args = [3,5,7,9]

t1 = time()
flist = []

if __name__ == "__main__":

    with ProcessPoolExecutor() as executor:
        for arg in input_args:
            flist.append(executor.submit(slow_process, arg))

    for f in flist:
        rdf = f.result()
        st.dataframe(rdf)

    st.write(f"total time usage: {time() - t1}s")
```
I only got  several warnings:

```

  run it with the following command:

    streamlit run [FILE_NAME] [ARGUMENTS]
```

What's the right way to use `multiprocessing` module?

issues.title: Timer.run() receives an extra positional argument with Sentry ThreadingIntegration and st.fragment(run_every)
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When Streamlit is used together with Sentry's default ThreadingIntegration, a periodically running fragment can fail with:

TypeError: Timer.run() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given

The error appears to be caused by an interaction between Streamlit's thread-state wrapper and Sentry's threading wrapper.

Streamlit stores the already-bound thread.run method and later forwards *args and **kwargs to it. Sentry's threading integration may invoke the replacement wrapper with the thread instance as a positional argument. That argument is then forwarded to the already-bound Timer.run method, resulting in the TypeError.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import sentry_sdk
import streamlit as st

sentry_sdk.init(
    dsn="YOUR_TEST_SENTRY_DSN",
)

@st.fragment(run_every="1s")
def timer_fragment() -> None:
    st.write("Fragment executed")

timer_fragment()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Install the dependencies:

pip install streamlit==1.60.0 sentry-sdk

Create app.py:

import sentry_sdk
import streamlit as st

sentry_sdk.init(
    dsn="YOUR_TEST_SENTRY_DSN",
)

@st.fragment(run_every="1s")
def periodically_updated_fragment() -> None:
    st.write("Fragment is running")

periodically_updated_fragment()

Run the application:

streamlit run app.py

Leave the application open while the fragment timer runs.

### Expected Behavior

st.fragment(run_every=...) should run normally when Sentry's default integrations are enabled.

Third-party wrappers around thread.run should not cause Streamlit to forward an extra thread instance to an already-bound run method.

### Current Behavior

The background timer can fail with:

TypeError: Timer.run() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given
  File "streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner_utils/script_run_context.py", line ..., in _run_with_thread_state
    original_run(*args, **kwargs)

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.60.0
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Linux in the deployed environment
- Browser: Google Chrome


### Additional Information

The issue does not occur after adding ThreadingIntegration() to disabled_integrations.

A related earlier Streamlit change allowed the thread-state wrapper to accept *args and **kwargs, but forwarding those arguments to an already-bound Timer.run appears to introduce this follow-up incompatibility.

issues.title: st.selectbox fuzzy search only matches contiguous substrings since 1.59.0 (BaseWeb → react-aria migration)
issues.body:
### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Since 1.59.0 (the `BaseWeb` → react-aria `ComboBox` migration, #15438), typing in
`st.selectbox` only matches options where the query is a **contiguous substring**
of the label. In 1.58.0 the search was truly fuzzy (non-contiguous subsequence),
so e.g. typing `ape` matched both `Grape` and `Apple`. Now it only matches
`Grape`, and queries like `aple` / `rp` that used to match return "No results".

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

FRUITS = ["Apple", "Apricot", "Banana", "Cherry", "Grape", "Mango", "Peach", "Pear"]
v = st.selectbox("Fruit", FRUITS, index=2)  # Banana pre-selected
st.write("value:", v)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above.
2. Click the selectbox and type `ape`.
3. Observe the dropdown.
4. Repeat with `aple` and `rp`.

### Expected Behavior

Fuzzy (non-contiguous, case-insensitive, label-only, score-ordered) matching, as
in 1.58.0:

| Type | Dropdown |
|------|----------|
| `ape`  | `Grape`, `Apple` |
| `aple` | `Apple` |
| `rp`   | `Grape` |

### Current Behavior

Only contiguous-substring matches survive (1.59.0 through current):

| Type | Dropdown |
|------|----------|
| `ape`  | `Grape` only |
| `aple` | *No results* |
| `rp`   | *No results* |

Root cause appears to be that the react-aria `ComboBox` applies its own built-in
`contains` text filter on top of Streamlit's already-fuzzy-filtered options, so
the visible list is the intersection (substring-only). Streamlit's own
`fuzzyFilterSelectOptions` util is still correct in isolation
(`ape → [Grape, Apple]`), so the fuzzy result is being re-filtered away by the
component. Consider disabling the component's built-in filter (e.g. a pass-through
`defaultFilter`) so Streamlit's fuzzy filter is authoritative.

(Screenshots attached: `EVIDENCE_v1_58_0_gap1_type_ape.png` shows `Grape, Apple`
on 1.58.0; `EVIDENCE_branch_gap1_type_ape.png` shows `Grape` only on 1.59.0+.)

### Is this a regression?
- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Confirmed via bisect against official PyPI wheels: `ape` → `[Grape, Apple]` on
**1.58.0** (BaseWeb `Select`), `[Grape]` on **1.59.0** (react-aria `ComboBox`).
Identical in Chromium and WebKit. Introduced by #15438.

### Debug info
- Streamlit version: 1.59.0 (introduced); still present in current 1.59.x / dev builds
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Linux (browser-independent)
- Browser: Chromium and WebKit (both affected)

### Additional Information

- Related migration PR: #15438 (Remove `BaseWeb` for `selectbox`).
- Discovered during QA of #15996 (which fixes the separate type-to-search
  append bug #15985). This filtering regression is independent of that fix.
- `filter_mode="fuzzy"` is the default and the mode affected; `prefix` / `contains`
  behave as documented.

issues.title: Add exclusive=True parameter to st.audio()
issues.body:
## Summary

### Problem
Currently, when multiple st.audio() components are displayed on the same page, users can start playback on multiple audio elements simultaneously. This often results in overlapping audio, which can be confusing and degrade the user experience.

### Proposed API
```python
audio1 = st.audio(audio_data_1, exclusive=True)
audio2 = st.audio(audio_data_2, exclusive=True)
```

### Expected Behavior
When exclusive=True:
- Starting playback on an audio component automatically pauses any other currently playing audio that also have exclusive=True.
- Audio components with exclusive=False (default) retains the current behavior.

### Example Use Cases
- Audio playlists
- Podcast applications
- Language learning platforms
- Text to speech applications
- Music preview interfaces
- Educational content with multiple audio examples, and so on.


#### Hope your community add this feature as soon as possible!

issues.title: Allow console_scripts as streamlit run scripts
issues.body:
### Problem

Right now streamlit requires a raw Python script (e.g. `your_script.py`) that is invoked, e.g.
```
streamlit run your_script.py [-- script args]
```

This is really frustrating if you want to package your streamlit application in a wheel file and distribute it to your friends & colleagues.  Streamlit's requirement of a raw Python script makes this impossible.

Assume I have created a proper Python package/distribution `my-streamlit-dashboard` and uploaded it to PyPI or some company-internal artefact store. If my colleagues now runs `pip install my-streamlit-dashboard`, my package will be installed but how would my colleague now run my dashboard? There is no `script.py` entry point for him or her to run. 


### Solution

For use-cases like this, Python packaging allows the definition of `console_scripts` which allow you to define command-line scripts that are installed e.g. within your virtual environment, and behave like normal shell scripts (but are actual Python scripts). All details can be found [here](https://python-packaging.readthedocs.io/en/latest/command-line-scripts.html#the-console-scripts-entry-point). Quite many Python tools & frameworks use this capability like for instance [PyScaffold's `putup` command](https://github.com/pyscaffold/pyscaffold), [Django's `django-admin` command](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/3.2/ref/django-admin/), [poetry's `poetry` command](https://python-poetry.org/docs/) and streamlit's own `streamlit` command.

Continuing the example from above, I could define a console-script `my-cool-dashboard` within the package `my-streamlit-dashboard` that would act as the initial script to run for streamlit, i.e.
```
streamlit run my-streamlit-dashboard
```
For this to work, streamlit would need to allow console scripts defined by `console_scripts` as start points for dashboard. Technically this should be possible as they are just Python scripts. Doing this right now leads to the error:
```
Error: Streamlit requires raw Python (.py) files, but the provided file has no extension.
For more information, please see https://docs.streamlit.io
```
if the console script doesn't end with `.py`, which is common. Adding `.py` leads to:
```
Error: Invalid value: File does not exist: my-cool-dashboard.py
```
A crude and unsatisfying workaround is:
```
streamlit run `which my-cool-dashboard.py`
```
This seems to mostly work but also emits nasty errors during execution:
```
File "/Users/fwilhelm/.mambaforge/envs/streamlit-demo/lib/python3.9/site-packages/streamlit/script_runner.py", line 354, in _run_script
    exec(code, module.__dict__)
File "/Users/fwilhelm/.mambaforge/envs/streamlit-demo/bin/my-streamlit-dashboard.py", line 33, in <module>
    sys.exit(load_entry_point('my-streamlit-dashboard', 'console_scripts', 'my-cool-dashboard.py')())
```


### Additional context

What are the benefits of making packaging for streamlit apps possible? I'm glad you asked! 
* Another way of distribution. For production, a streamlit app would right now be deployed as docker container most likely. Allowing proper packaging would also make it possible for users to just install and run it locally via pip. Thus more **flexibility**.
* Proper **versioning**. Since Python packages/distributions are versioned, one could apply proper versioning to these packages and enforce certain processes within an organisation, like semantic versioning etc. which is hard if everyone is just cloning a git repo. 
* Enabling [**ML-Ops** principles](https://ml-ops.org/content/mlops-principles). Most organisation provide templates for Python projects that support developers in applying techniques like testing (CI/CD), reproducibility, documentation, deployment, etc. With the suggested solution it would be much easier to incorporate streamlit in such templates as e.g. provided by [PyScaffold](https://pyscaffold.org/).

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

**If you'd like the Streamlit team to prioritize this feature request, please use the 👍 (thumbs up emoji) reaction in response to the initial post.**

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-4162)

Here is a snippet of the relevant part of my `Dockerfile` (last version after many tries):

COPY . .

### Summary

In ChatGPT and many other apps, the submit button in the chat input turns into a stop button after submitting. Clicking it interrupts the current LLM generation/streaming. We should have the same thing!

Today, there's no way to interrupt an LLM generation in a Streamlit app. That can be annoying for long LLM messages.

After submitting a message, the submit button should turn into a stop button. Clicking it should interrupt the current run, maybe simply by calling `st.stop` under the hood? If the run is interrupted or finished, the stop button should turn back into a submit button.

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a user enters a prompt in st.chat_input, it is not possible to disable the input while an LLM is generating the response to that input. 

This leads to the possibility of the user 'interrupting' the model output and messing up the conversation structure.

I've tried binding the `disable` argument to a variable inside the `st.session_state`, but it does not work.

This happens in the official ['chat-GPT like' implementation on streamlit forums](https://docs.streamlit.io/knowledge-base/tutorials/build-conversational-apps#write-the-app).


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time

st.title("ChatGPT-like clone")

def stream_example_response():
    response = "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua."

    # yield 5 characters every 0.1 seconds
    for i in range(0, len(response), 5):
        time.sleep(0.1)
        yield response[i:i+5]

if "messages" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.messages = []

if "disable_chat_input" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.disable_chat_input = False

for message in st.session_state.messages:
    with st.chat_message(message["role"]):
        st.markdown(message["content"])

if prompt := st.chat_input("What is up?", disabled=st.session_state.disable_chat_input):
    
    st.session_state['disable_chat_input'] = True

    st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt})
    with st.chat_message("user"):
        st.markdown(prompt)

    with st.chat_message("assistant"):
        response = st.write_stream(stream_example_response())
    st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response})

    st.session_state['disable_chat_input'] = False
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the minimal example provided (`streamlit run minimal.py`)
2. Send a prompt
3. While the response is streaming, send another prompt
4. The response gets interrupted, doesn't get registered on the history and the messages become messed up.

### Expected Behavior

With the `disabled=st.session_state.disable_chat_input` I was expecting that the user input would be disabled until the response stops streaming. 
Perhaps would be useful to have an argument in `st.chat_input` or something so that it automatically disables until all the code inside the `if prompt:= ...` statement ends, whatever works best.

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.31.1
- Python version: 3.10.13
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Firefox


### Additional Information

issues.title: Persist widget state if `key` is set, even if the widget is not rendered
issues.body:
👋 I work on developer experience for Streamlit and wanted to get some feedback on this recurring issue.

**TL;DR: Take a look at the [example app](https://keyed-widget-state-issue.streamlit.app/) and let us know how it impacts you, and what you think about how to fix this issue!**

**Discussion on the forums [here](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/keyed-widget-state-persistence-discussion-possible-fixes/37359)**

One of the current Streamlit behaviors that causes confusion for many of us is how widgets with `key='foo'` lose their session_state value when they are not rendered in a given run. It seems to come up most often with multipage apps that have some state dependency between pages, but also possible in a single page app with conditional rendering. A minimal example:

```
view = st.radio("View", ["view1", "view2"])

if view == "view1":
    st.text_input("Text1", key="text1")
    "☝️ Enter some text, then click on view2 above"
elif view == "view2":
    "☝️ Now go back to view1 and see if your text is still there"
```

I'm working with @tconkling on whether / how to update this behavior so it's more intuitive, or at least possible to get the intuitive behavior easily.

I put together a simple example app showing the behavior and linking some of the prior issues about it:
[https://keyed-widget-state-issue.streamlit.app/](https://keyed-widget-state-issue.streamlit.app/)

### Questions

- Do you have a full working public app where you had to hack around this (such as duplicating or using "shadow keys")? Please share with us!
- Do you have an app or use case where you rely on the current behavior (widget has `key` set but needs value to reset after not rendering), that will break if we change this? We **really** want to hear about these! Please share!

### Possible fixes

It seems like most developers we hear from find the current behavior very unintuitive, and we see a lot more use cases that have to work around this rather than benefit from it.
- Given that, should we just do a breaking change to the default behavior to persist, like most of us seem to expect?
- If so: We should still provide a path to clear keyed widget state when needed. Need to figure out how to best do this.

If not a breaking change: most proposals seem to prefer something like a `persist=` key. For example, both @whitphx and @mathcatsand propose something like this in [#4458](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4458). Thoughts on this approach, or other ideas?

issues.title: Caching improvements
issues.body:
### Problem

I'm using Streamlit to build a complicated report which takes about an hour to generate an output. It processes a hundred megabytes of Pandas dataframes. The performance of this report is important to keep UX better. Data processing has also it's own cost. 

To show report results during a reasonable amount of time and minimize processing costs I utilize caching approach. Using Streamlit's caching mechanism I've faced multiple difficulties:
1. I would like to use persistence on the disk instead of keeping the cache inside in RAM. It helps to avoid wasting RAM when you have multiple nodes where the report is hosted. I understand that it needs time to load the cache into memory but it is excepted. When there are multiple cache values which take 100MB it is reasonable to keep this on disk instead of in RAM to avoid OOM. Unfortunately, Streamlit keeps a copy of cache value in memory when `persist=True`.
2. There are only two strategies of caching: memory and disk. In my particular case, it is reasonable to have the possibility to keep cache directly in S3/Minio.
3. Streamlit has only one strategy of data serialization: Pickle. In the case of large Pandas data frames, it is reasonable to have other formats support like Arrow (it more efficient in term of memory usage and loading time). In general, it would be great to have different strategies which depend on the data type.
4. I'm not able to configure caching folder. Currently, Streamlit keep all cache in `~/.streamlit`

I'm still exploring Streamlit features and code, so probably it is not a complete list of missing cache features.

### Solution

**MVP:**
1. Add `skip_memory_cache=True`
2. As a workaround we can mount S3 into `~/.streamlit` folder using the FUSE driver ([s3 FUSE driver](https://github.com/s3fs-fuse/s3fs-fuse), [Minio FUSE driver](https://github.com/minio/minfs))
3. Pickle is good enough but it does not support unserialization streaming which leads to RAM usage spike.
4. Add cache folder into config (see #3269)
5. Do not remove `cache` directory, because it might be mounted using `s3fs`

**Preferred solution:**
1-2. Add different caching strategies and possibility to chain different strategies (like `cache_strategies=['memory', 'disk', 's3']`). Initially, we can fetch from the fast cache and if it is miss then from the slower cache.
3. Implement data serialization for Pandas. Parquet is a preferable format (see formats [comparison](https://towardsdatascience.com/the-best-format-to-save-pandas-data-414dca023e0d))
4. Cache folder should be a part of `disk` strategy configuration.
5. Decouple cache component as a separate library to avoid coupling on the whole streamlit project. I found this useful when I want to use the same caching approach in my libraries.

### Additional context

Probably integration of an already existing cache library that already supports all these features might be a faster and more robust solution.

Here is a library that can be easily replace FS Python operations with S3:
https://s3fs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/

issues.title: Automatically reformat in CI on lint failure
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, the CI fails a check if `ruff format --check` fails, thus preventing poorly-formatted code from making it into the codebase, which is good. However, the CI should simply make the reformatting commit for the user. This is almost always desireable. And, in rare cases when it's not desireable, the user can always rollback the automatic commit and manually add the noqa comments they will need, or whatever, so no harm no foul.

### Why?

Dev QoL

### How?

I think mypy achieves this with a "pre-commit" github action, but there are probably a couple ways.

### Additional Context

Here's an example from mypy, for reference https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19494/commits/7f102209eaab90297b6bbac4066419accc281050

I run afoul of lint rules all the time, because I don't care about code line length at all and just keep typing; so I love it when the reformatter just takes care of it without complaint, according to the preferences of the repo owner. The popular python reformatters I know about (ruff, black) are also 100% safe in the sense of never changing code meaning by reformatting (except for the occasional formatter bug). There may be security implications for hooking up this action, altho' probably not more than hooking up other actions.

issues.title: Contribution documentation suggestions
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

I cannot edit the Contribution documentation directly to propose changes, because it is a "wiki" page https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/wiki/Contributing I don't have edit access to instead of living directly in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md

Here are my suggestions based on my struggles building Streamlit on Ubuntu WSL:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/wiki/Contributing#ubuntu should have the additions:

* If you are on Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS or earlier, then you will only have access to libprotoc 3.12.4, which is lower than the minimum required version 3.20. Therefore, you will have to `do-release-upgrade`. *(This one could be edited to have the weasel word "might" instead of "will" if you don't believe very strongly in the validity of the detective work I did months ago.)*

* Make sure you have sudo installed. This comes with Ubuntu by default; but if you somehow lack it, you can become root using `su -` and then install sudo with `apt-get install -y sudo`. *(This one is of questionable usefulness, but for some reason I did need to do this at some point.)*

* If you get an error like `error: failed to remove file [blah blah blah]/streamlit/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/streamlit-1.43.2.dist-info/INSTALLER: Permission denied (os error 13)`, try running `sudo chmod -R 777 .venv` first, and/or prefix your `make` command with `sudo`, eg `sudo make all`. *(This one could be moved to the section that talks about WSL, I suppose, since I don't know if this issue ever arises on native linux (I've only run everything through WSL so I don't know what happens on not-WSL).)*

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/wiki/Contributing#windows should have the addition:

* WSL2 is more likely than WSL1 to work, as there is (or, at least, has been) a [binary compatibility problem](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/8151) between nodejs and WSL1.

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/wiki/Contributing#2-grab-the-code should have the addition:

* For implementation reasons, the absolute filepath of the Streamlit directory must not contain any characters that are specially interpreted by the shell. (The shell in question is almost certainly [Bash](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html).) *(~~If #11741 and #11742 get fixed then this advice will become obsolete.~~ Edit: unfortunately, this one will not be obsolete until https://github.com/protobufjs/protobuf.js/issues/2081 (a thing with a similar problem, that we depend upon internally) is also fixed, and there is little momentum there. Edit 2026-04-29: that was fixed two days ago, so whenever you get on the current version of that dep special characters are back on the menu...!)*
* **(new)** Independent of the previous warning, there should be a warning: Due to [internal implementation reasons](https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#resolution-algorithm-specification), the absolute filepath of the Streamlit directory must not contain any backslashes.

### Why?

WSL is not officially supported, but neither is it officially anathema, so I'm happy to share these hard-won tips I discovered. Some of the other info relates to platforms that are officially supported.

### How?

You may copy these all verbatim or change them in any way you like. I release all of that text I wrote into the public domain and also the license of this project. Feel free to close this issue when you've determined you've taken all that you want.

### Additional Context

**Trivia**

These tips mostly come from stuff I discovered while working on https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/10829, which was in turn something I started while trying to start working on a pull request for some other feature that I actually wanted.
