issues.title: Enable `request_rerun`-ing session through external sources and using a session_id
issues.body:
_(Note, you don't have to fill out every section here. They're just here for guidance. That said, nicely detailed feature requests are more likely to get eng attention sooner)_

### Problem

Dear StreamLit Team, first of all, thank you deeply for this awesome framework. I have learned quite a lot diving through the codebase and resolved some long lasting issues of mine thanks to your ScriptRunner magic :)

I have been playing with StreamLit recently and I have the need to refresh a user tab from an external source, ideally from external requests.

I couldn't find the recommended way to do it, so I hacked StreamLit internals. 

I found an almost unused Handler (DebugHandler) on the tornado routes and patched it to enable receiving a refresh from outside using its get method.

```py
...
if _STREAMLIT_AVAILABLE:
    import urllib.parse as _parse

    import streamlit as st
    import streamlit.bootstrap as bootstrap
    import tornado
    from streamlit import config
    from streamlit.bootstrap import (
        _fix_matplotlib_crash,
        _fix_pydeck_mapbox_api_warning,
        _fix_sys_argv,
        _fix_sys_path,
        _fix_tornado_crash,
        _install_config_watchers,
        _on_server_start,
        _set_up_signal_handler,
    )
    from streamlit.cli import _get_command_line_as_string, check_credentials
    from streamlit.report_thread import get_report_ctx
    from streamlit.server.server import Server
    from tornado.web import RequestHandler

    class RefreshSessionHandler(RequestHandler):
        def initialize(self, server):
            self._server = server

        async def get(self):
            query_arguments = self.request.query_arguments
            session_info = ast.literal_eval([v for v in query_arguments.keys()][0])
            session_id = session_info["session_id"]
            session_info = Server.get_current()._get_session_info(session_id)
            if session_info is None:
                return
            session = session_info.session

            session.request_rerun(session._client_state)

    st.server.server.DebugHandler = RefreshSessionHandler


def _render_ui(script_path, args=None, **flag_options):
    # This code has been taken from StreamLit, so we can patch the DebugHandler
    # with our RefreshSessionHandler
    bootstrap.load_config_options(flag_options=flag_options)

    if args is None:
        args = []

    if flag_options is None:
        flag_options = {}

    command_line = _get_command_line_as_string()

    st._is_running_with_streamlit = True
    check_credentials()
    _fix_sys_path(script_path)
    _fix_matplotlib_crash()
    _fix_tornado_crash()
    _fix_sys_argv(script_path, args)
    _fix_pydeck_mapbox_api_warning()
    _install_config_watchers(flag_options)
    _set_up_signal_handler()
    ioloop = tornado.ioloop.IOLoop.current()
    with mock.patch("streamlit.server.server.DebugHandler", RefreshSessionHandler):
        server = Server(ioloop, script_path, command_line)
    server.start(_on_server_start)
    server.add_preheated_report_session()
    ioloop.start()
```

This worked perfectly for StreamLit 1.3.9, but the API has changed quite a lot since then and this hack doesn't work.

However, I believe there would be a growing community need to have a more reliable way for external sources to refresh a StreamLit UI. I believe this would be worth prioritizing.

As a side note, I have been investigating how to unittest StreamLit UI behaviour and looked into this test [test_calls_widget_callbacks](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/tests/streamlit/scriptrunner/script_runner_test.py#L142) in particular.

I have used the `TestScriptRunner` to test my StreamLit apps, but its API changed between versions. I would like to ask the StreamLit Team to invest in making the testing tool stable and part of the main package. This would become critical for users to reliability productionize StreamLit apps.
And I am afraid this would create friction to buy into the StreamLit ecosystem if this isn't made available by the Core Team.

Thanks for you deeply for your time and effort !

### Summary

If you use an unevaluated Snowpark/PySpark dataframe in `st.bar_chart` etc, we do the following:

1. Restrict the dataframe to the first 1000 rows if it's larger. 
2. Evaluate and download the resulting dataframe by calling `to_pandas`. 
3. Drop all columns except the ones we need, e.g. if `x`, `y`, or `color` are set. 
4. Send that dataframe to the frontend and show it. 

To improve performance, it would be better to switch steps 2 and 3, so that we first drop unnecessary columns and then evaluate the dataframe. Especially for dataframes with lots of columns this could result in a speedup.

issues.title: Streamlit log handler
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

A streamlit log handler to allow using Streamlit to show logs.

### Why?

Python's built-in logging framework is extremely versatile. Hooking into that would make debugging easier.

In my own app, I have observations I both want to save to a log system and show to the user. Having a streamlit log handler allows me to do that without duplicating code.

### How?

I have written something that I use in my own project that can be used as a starting place:

```
import logging

import streamlit as st


class StreamlitLogHandler(logging.Handler):
    """
    Log handler to display logs in Streamlit app.

    This handler formats log messages and sends them to the Streamlit app for display.
    If the log record contains an "object" attribute, its value will be displayed in an expander.
    If the log record contains a "link" attribute, the log text will be a link with the content as the target address.

    If streamlit session state contains a "log_container", logs will be displayed there.
    Otherwise, logs will be displayed on the page as they are emitted.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def get_icon(levelno: int) -> str:
        if levelno <= logging.INFO:
            return "ℹ️"
        elif levelno <= logging.WARNING:
            return "⚠️"
        elif levelno <= logging.ERROR:
            return "❌"
        else:
            return "🛑"

    def emit(self, record: logging.LogRecord):
        if "log_container" in st.session_state and isinstance(
            st.session_state["log_container"], st.delta_generator.DeltaGenerator
        ):
            log_container = st.session_state["log_container"]
        else:
            log_container = st
        msg = self.format(record)
        if "link" in record.__dict__:
            msg = f"[{msg}]({record.__dict__['link']})"
        if "object" in record.__dict__:
            with log_container.expander(
                msg, expanded=False, icon=self.get_icon(record.levelno)
            ):
                log_container.write(record.__dict__["object"])
        else:
            if record.levelno <= logging.INFO:
                log_container.info(msg)
            elif record.levelno <= logging.WARNING:
                log_container.warning(msg)
            else:
                log_container.error(msg)

```

The "log_containter" in st.session_state allows you to specify where the logs should be shown. The obvious use case is a collapsed expander that can be opened to see what logs there are. It is not the most transparent way of doing it, and it risks them not being shown (if it is set on on page, and the page is then changed).

You can set the object to show by e.g. `logger.error("Example error log message", extra={"object": object_to_log})`

You can set where you want the text to link to by e.g `logger.error("Example error log message.",extra={"link": "#" + self.name})`. This allows you to link in the same page (used as shown) or another page. You could also make the log message into a markdown text with the link, but you typically don't want that in other log systems, so doing that would make the logging less versatile.

This is just a suggestion, it works for my app, but I am sure many improvements can be done. 

### Additional Context

_No response_

issues.title: st.table() / st.dataframe() / st.data_editor() causes fatal SIGSEGV (exit code 139) in PyArrow convert_column - process killed silently, no Python exception raised
issues.body:
### Summary

Calling st.table(), st.dataframe(), or st.data_editor() with a pandas DataFrame causes a fatal segmentation fault (SIGSEGV, exit code 139) that kills the entire Streamlit process. The crash originates inside PyArrow's convert_column C extension, called during Streamlit's internal DataFrame-to-Arrow serialization. No Python exception is raised. The process dies silently with no user-visible error. In containerized environments (Kubernetes/OpenShift) this triggers a pod restart.


### Steps To Reproduce

We were unable to produce a minimal example that reliably crashes in all environments. The crash is non-deterministic and appears to depend on the process memory state at the time of rendering. It reproduces consistently in our containerized Linux environment (OpenShift, Python 3.11) but not on a local Windows developer machine.

The code that triggers it in the enviroments:

```
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# This DataFrame is rendered on every page rerun
df = pd.DataFrame({"Group": st.session_state.get("usergroup", [])})
st.table(df)  
```

or

```
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# DataFrame built from backend JSON response
rows = [{"col_a": "value", "col_b": None}, {"col_a": "other", "col_b": 3}]
df = pd.DataFrame(rows)  # object-dtype columns with None values
st.dataframe(df)  #
```


Steps To Reproduce

1. Deploy a Streamlit 1.55.0 app to a Linux container (e.g. OpenShift/Kubernetes)
2. Navigate to a page that renders st.table() or st.dataframe() with a DataFrame that has object-dtype columns (e.g. built from pd.DataFrame(list_of_dicts) where some cells are None)
3. Trigger a Streamlit script rerun via a button click that loads new data into session state before the render
4. Observed: process dies with exit code 139, container restarts
5. Repeat the exact same steps - it works on the second attempt

### Expected Behavior

The DataFrame renders normally. If an internal serialization error occurs, Streamlit catches it and displays an error in the UI without killing the process.

### Current Behavior

The Python process is killed with SIGSEGV (exit code 139). Nothing appears in logs unless faulthandler is explicitly enabled at startup. With import faulthandler; faulthandler.enable() added, the crash trace is:

```
Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault

Current thread (most recent call first):
  File ".../pyarrow/pandas_compat.py", line 638 in convert_column
  File ".../pyarrow/pandas_compat.py", line 656 in dataframe_to_arrays
  File ".../streamlit/dataframe_util.py", line 839 in convert_pandas_df_to_arrow_bytes
  File ".../streamlit/dataframe_util.py", line 919 in convert_anything_to_arrow_bytes
  File ".../streamlit/elements/table.py", line 78 in marshall_table
  File ".../streamlit/elements/table.py", line 234 in table
```

The crash is non-deterministic: it only occurs on some reruns, always the first one after the pod/process starts, and does not occur on subsequent reruns with identical data and code. We have no confirmed explanation for the non-determinism beyond it appearing to depend on process memory state.

**Workaround**: converting object-dtype columns to pd.StringDtype() before rendering prevents the crash:

- For st.table(): replace with st.write() / st.markdown() to avoid PyArrow entirely

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- **Streamlit version:** 1.55.0
- **Python version:** 3.11
- **OS:** Linux (OpenShift container, py311ora base image)
- **PyArrow version:** (bundled with Streamlit 1.55.0)
- **pandas version:** (default installed with Streamlit 1.55.0)
- **Browser**: Microsoft Edge

### Additional Information

- The crash is in PyArrow's C extension code, not in Streamlit's Python layer - Streamlit could potentially guard against it by catching signals or pre-validating column types before passing to PyArrow
- After the SIGSEGV the container restarts automatically (Kubernetes/OpenShift restart policy). On the very next attempt, with the process freshly started and identical code, data, and user actions, the crash does not occur and the app works normally. This "works after restart" behavior is what made the bug difficult to diagnose initially, as it appeared to be a transient infrastructure issue rather than a code defect.

issues.title: Schedule clear cache
issues.body:
### Problem

I learned that the cache from "st.cache_data()" will only be cleared when the option "Clear cache" from developer options is manually activated by the owner of the app or if the cache expires. 

The problem with that is when you have multiple sets of data in your app that are scheduled to be updated in specific dates of the month, at specific times, you either go and manually clear cache yourself in each of this updates or you'll have outdated data in your app until the cache expires.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/73763541/236198590-0ef4604e-1c36-4379-89d4-2663704f5ddc.png)

Of course you can leave a small time for the argument "ttl" in "st.cache_data()" to try to get around this issue but you will be querying your database multiple times, and also increasing user loading time, when you know the data hasn't changed (in my case, the data is only updated once a month). This also creates the issue that the user of the app won't have the most recent data as soon as it is released.

### Solution

It would be great to be able to leave a really long time as an argument to "st.cache_data()" and be able to schedule a "Clear cache" on the app settings (https://share.streamlit.io/) for when you know the data is gonna be released along the following months. 

The format for this scheduling would be great if it was something close to what the Windows Task Scheduler offers as triggers, with multiple dates that don't exactly follow a standard such as crontab from linux, Databricks and other tools. Why? Because the data I work with has some randomness on the date it is released. Sometimes the 5th, sometimes the 8th, some time 1st day of the month, and so on.

issues.title: Is it possible to make Streamlit interactive plot as fast as Plotly?
issues.body:
### Problem

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-6978)

I am trying to create a responsive plot in Streamlit that responds to a slider bar, but it is extremely slow.
```
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import streamlit as st


if st.session_state.get('fig') is None:
    st.session_state['freq'] = np.arange(0.0, 5.1, 0.1).round(2)    
    f = st.session_state['freq'][2]
    st.session_state['fig'] = go.Figure()
    st.session_state['fig'].add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            name=str(f),
            x=np.arange(0, 10.01, 0.01),
            y=np.sin(f* np.arange(0, 10.01, 0.01))))
    
def sldier_callback():
    f = st.session_state['slider_freq']
    x = st.session_state['fig'].data[0].x
    st.session_state['fig'].data[0].y = np.sin(f*x)
    st.session_state['fig'].data[0].name = str(f)


f = st.select_slider(
    label='Frequency', 
    options=st.session_state['freq'],
    value=2,
    on_change=sldier_callback,
    key='slider_freq'
)

st.plotly_chart(st.session_state['fig'])
```
![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/15989924/de4641d3-ee8b-44f3-9893-81f58d371e17)

### Solution

The [Plotly chart](https://plotly.com/python/sliders/), on the other hand, is much more responsive to the slider bar. It creates and hides the figures at the beginning and then unhides the correct figure when you move the slider bar.
```
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import numpy as np


fig = go.Figure()
for step in np.arange(0, 5, 0.1):
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            visible=False,
            name="f = " + str(step),
            x=np.arange(0, 10, 0.01),
            y=np.sin(step * np.arange(0, 10, 0.01))))

fig.data[10].visible = True

# Create and add slider
steps = []
for i in range(len(fig.data)):
    step = dict(
        method="update",
        args=[              
            {"visible": [False] * len(fig.data)},
            {"title": "Slider switched to step: " + str(i)}],  
    )
    step["args"][0]["visible"][i] = True
    steps.append(step)

sliders = [dict(
    active=10,
    currentvalue={"prefix": "Frequency: "},
    pad={"t": 50},
    steps=steps
)]

fig.update_layout(
    sliders=sliders
)

fig.show()
```

![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/15989924/b1c3b597-9a86-403f-8e6b-8ce9bfe3e0dc)


### Additional context

I tried to do the same in Streamlit with the following code, but it is still very slow. Does anyone know how to speed it up in Streamlit? Thanks!

```
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go


if st.session_state.get('fig') is None:
    st.session_state['freq'] = np.arange(0.0, 5.01, 0.1).round(2)
    st.session_state['fig'] = go.Figure()
    for f in st.session_state['freq']:
        st.session_state['fig'].add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                visible=False,
                name=str(f),
                x=np.arange(0, 10.01, 0.01),
                y=np.sin(f*np.arange(0, 10.01, 0.01))))
    
    st.session_state['selected'] = 0
    st.session_state['fig'].data[0].visible = True


def sldier_callback():
    i = st.session_state['selected']
    st.session_state['fig'].data[i].visible = False
    freq = st.session_state['slider_freq']
    i = np.where(st.session_state['freq']==freq)[0][0]
    st.session_state['fig'].data[i].visible = True
    st.session_state['selected'] = i


f = st.select_slider(
    label='freq', 
    options=st.session_state['freq'],
    value=2,
    on_change=sldier_callback,
    key='slider_freq'
)

st.plotly_chart(st.session_state['fig'])
```

issues.title: Add `allowed_dates` parameter to st.date_input to restrict selectable dates to a specific list
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, st.date_input only supports continuous date ranges via min_value and max_value. 
There is no way to restrict selectable dates to a specific list of valid dates, such as 
dates available in a dataframe. Adding an allowed_dates parameter would fill this gap.

### Why?

I'm always frustrated when I need to show a date picker that only allows the user to select 
dates that exist in a dataset. For example, when a dataframe contains sales data only for 
specific dates, the current widget allows the user to select any date in the range, even 
dates with no data. This forces developers to use workarounds like st.selectbox, which 
lacks the calendar UI and date-picking experience that st.date_input provides.

### How?

Introduce a new parameter called `allowed_dates` in `st.date_input` with the following behavior:

- Accepts a list of datetime.date objects
- Disables all dates not present in the list in the calendar UI
- Example usage:

import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"date": ["2025-01-01", "2025-01-15", "2025-02-10"]})
df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"]).dt.date

selected = st.date_input(
    "Select a date",
    allowed_dates=df["date"].tolist()
)

### Additional Context

This feature request was inspired by a common use case discussed while using st.date_input  with dataframes. The current workaround is to use st.selectbox with the list of available dates, but this sacrifices the calendar UI   experience.

Related issue: st.date_input currently supports min_value and max_value for continuous 
ranges, but has no support for non-continuous date lists.

issues.title: More consistent handling of relative paths
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

We have two main ways relative paths are parsed:
- For Page and navigation commands, paths are relative to the entrypoint file
- For most other command (like media), paths are relative to the current working directory

Although this may be the same for many people, Community Cloud in particular used the root of the repository as the current working directory which can necessitate some rearranging of files/path handling for complex apps. When it comes to Community Cloud's handling of Python dependencies, both the entrypoint-file directory and the root of the repository are searched, in that order. (This is not the case for packages.txt, nor for Streamlit's config.toml. The former must be handled in Cloud, but the latter may be handled in open source.)

It would be nice if all of Streamlit's paths prioritized "relative to the entrypoint file" then fell back to "relative to the current working directory." This could be implemented for `.streamlit/config.toml` (or anything in the `.streamlit` folder before falling back to the user's global settings). This could also be used for all local file paths (`st.image`, `st.video`, etc).

Related to #7731, #7578 (though more restrictive than those requests).

cc @tvst @sfc-gh-tteixeira

Consistency.

# Summary
When Streamlit interrupts (and terminates) a script that has spawned children processes, the children processes don't appear to be properly handled causing the session to hang and ultimately become unusable. The user must refresh the browser page to continue using the app; the administrator must send SIGKILL signals the streamlit process (and its children) when trying to stop the streamlit server.

# Steps to reproduce
Create a script using `with muiltiprocessing.pool.Pool() as pool:` and submit some tasks to the pool that require some time to finish.
Before the pool has been closed and joined, click Stop or Rerun for the script.
Notice the session is now hung and the children processes that persist.

## Expected behavior:
Streamlit should probably send some king of a signal to the script so it can attempt to terminate itself before Streamlit kills it.

## Actual behavior:
Session is seemingly corrupted and children processes are orphaned.

## Is this a regression?
No

# Debug info
- Streamlit version: 0.53.0
- Python version: 3.8.1
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? Just a normal virtual environment from python -m venv
- OS version: CentOS Linux 7
- Browser version: Firefox 72.0.1

# Additional information
[More here discuss.streamlit.io](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/spawning-process-es-within-a-streamlit-script-can-lead-to-a-corrupted-user-session-if-a-script-run-is-interrupted-rerun/1703/2)

issues.title: For deferred download with `st.download_button`, pipe errors to the script thread
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

If you use deferred download with `st.download_button`, there should be a way to catch errors that may be raised by the deferred generation function. Currently, if the funciton encounters an error, a warning message is displayed on the frontend and isn't accessible on the backend.

### Why?

When you use deferred download with `st.download_button`, the function which returns the download runs on its own thread so it won't block the script thread. This has two consequences:
1. There is no script context, so you can't use any Streamlit command, like `st.session_state`. (See #13337).
2. You can't handle errors raised by the deferred download function.

You can put try-catch blocks in your download function to avoid an unhandled error, but you can't really _do_ anything about it because you can't display a custom message or log something in Session State. (Maybe you could hack a solution by writing something to a temporary file on the server, but that doesn't seem ideal.)

### How?

A couple different solutions:
* Have the download button return an error if encountered so it can be caught in the main script.
* Give the download thread some (possibly restricted) script context (like #13337).
* Improve multithreading support more generally, and have some hook at the end of a script run to catch a session's child threads, like the download thread.

### Additional Context

_No response_

issues.title: torch.tensor should play well with st.write
issues.body: ### Checklist - [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests. - [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue. ### Summary Streamlit has arguable the most beautiful visualization of array data (like Numpy arrays) and tabular data (like Pandas dataframes) of any Python visualization library. All of these visualizations can be effortlessly accessed through the magic of `st.write`. Amazing! However, as data compute moves to GPU-accelerate and distributed environments, new primitives, such as PyTorch tensors are rapidly replacing these older primtives, while have similar visual properties, but are instantly and properly displayed by `st.write` which risks making Streamlit feel dated relative to trends modern AI programming. This GitHub issue covers a minor but obvious first step: rendering `torch.tensor` similarly to how we render `numpy.ndarray`. ### Why? I'd love if `st.write(pytorch_tensor)` felt amazing. ### How? Ideally, the following code which creates a **pytorch** array: ```python torch_array = torch.tensor([1, 2, 3]) st.write(torch_array) ``` Would display identically to this code which creates a **numpy** array: ```python numpy_array = torch.tensor([1, 2, 3]).numpy() st.write(numpy_array) ``` Visually: ### Additional Context This GitHub issue *only* covers the case of `torch.tensor` because 1. Streamlit already beautiful visualization of such objects 2. It is such a basic primitive for writing, understanding, debugging, and presenting GPU-accelerate machine learning code. However, a more ambitious project, would be to wrap all the "natural" PyTorch primitives, potentially covering: - **Tensors** (`torch.tensor`): Multi-dimensional arrays holding data, easily printable in text or graphical form. - **Modules** (`torch.nn.Module`): Defines neural networks, with structures that can be printed or visualized. **Note:** We could potentially use PyTorch's own `torchviz` for this. Or do something extra beautiful in Streamlit. - **Parameters** (`torch.nn.Parameter`): Tensors that are part of the model’s learnable parameters, also printable. - **Datasets** (`torch.utils.data.Dataset`): Contains structured data that can be accessed and printed. - **Data Loaders** (`torch.utils.data.DataLoader`): Provides batches of data for training, easily printable batch-by-batch. - **Gradients** (`torch.Tensor.backward()`): Computes and stores gradients in tensors, which can be printed out. This is obviously a giant project, but it would also ground Streamlit firmly as an AI-centered library for building and exploring large models in the future. :heart:

issues.title: st.selectbox user experience is confusing.
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The selectbox UI could be clearer to users.  In our use case editing the selectbox makes no sense.   The arrow key interactions were difficult because the selected row would go off-screen rather than autoscrolling to keep the selected item in view.  When arrowing around, the UI was expected to update rather than require the enter key.

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-7187)

```Python
import streamlit as st


selection = st.selectbox("My List Box", [ f'Option {i}' for i in range(1,100) ] )
```


### Steps To Reproduce

Run the program, edit the text in select box, and then arrow around in the selectbox until the highlighted line disappears off the top or bottom of the listbox.


### Expected Behavior

I expect select boxes to at least optionally be read-only (my 90% default is read-only)
I expect select boxes to have more than one item visible. Optionally, depending on screen space, I'm fine specifying the height in pixels or items.
I expect select boxes to keep the selected item visible under all conditions while using arrow keys.
I would like to optionally be able to control whether arrowing in the list box triggers a change in the UI

### Current Behavior

I watched users interact with the selectbox UI I made for them and was shocked by their confusion.

1) Several users immediately started EDITING the text, which confused me as I watched!  This is the very last thing I expected a selectbox to allow. It never occurred to me to type.  My use case is selecting options, not free-form text entry.  This became a pseudo-feature for longer lists, acting as a filter only showing items that matched the typed text (this could be very useful as some UI toolkits have this type of widget). A `read_only=True`  or `filter_mode=True` could be useful.
2) Part of the reason for these issues was that selectboxes show one item until you interact with them, so they look like a text boxes.  It would be nice to have a `visible_items` parameter to allow control of vertical space.  Having only one item visible obscures the fact that there could be more than one, though admittedly, the height of 1 is optimal for vertical space.
3) The arrow keys act oddly.  Users are used to arrowing up/down and having the selected item change, and when the selected item gets to the top or bottom, the UI should scroll to keep giving feedback on what is selected. In Steamlit, the highlighted item goes off-screen, breaking the UI feedback.
4) It would be nice if arrowing "triggered" a UI update to give immediate feedback.  I see the need for arrowing + enter key to trigger the change for use cases that are expensive in time.  An `auto_update=True` might be nice.

### Is this a regression?

NO

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.25
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Windows 10
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

I ❤️ streamlit.

issues.title: Improve support custom class hashing
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit implements custom hashing for some popular classes, such as `numpy.ndarray`. In some cases, we want to reuse them in the implementation of a hash function for a custom class, but there is no public API for this.

### Why?

The documentation lacks a comprehensive list of supported types for hashing (for example, `dataclass`). 

Consider the following synthetic example:
```python
class CustomArray:
    def __init__(self, description: str, array: np.ndarray):
        self.description = description
        self.values = array
```
For specific reasons we don't use `dataclasses`. Thus, we need to implement hash function, the documentation provides three approaches:
1) Using uniquely identifies.
2) Using Python's built in `hash()`.
3) Implementing a custom mechanism.

`CustomArray` doesn't have uniquely identifies (1). 
The `np.darray` doesn't have `hash()` (2). Furthermore, the docstring of `hashing._to_bytes()` appears to contradict the documentation: 
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/c7d29c1ade36a347fd740e4adb66e06708957159/lib/streamlit/runtime/caching/hashing.py#L341-L342

Thus, a custom mechanism is required (3), and the ideal solution would involve using Streamlit's hashing mechanism for `np.ndarray`. Unfortunately, this mechanism is currently a private part of Streamlit.

### How?

- [ ] Include a list of supported types for hashing in the documentation.
- [ ] Check the contradiction between [the example with `hash()`](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/caching#example-1-hashing-a-custom-class) and [the docsting](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/c7d29c1ade36a347fd740e4adb66e06708957159/lib/streamlit/runtime/caching/hashing.py#L341-L342). 
- [ ] Introducing a public API for Streamlit's hashing mechanism.

It may be related to: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7353


### Additional Context

_No response_

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

It would be great if the new `on_select` feature had better support for subplots and hovermodes. Overall, better control of grouping of elements would help make the feature more usable. I've sketched up some dummy code. Please run it and try these various actions:

1. Clicking on an element in stacked barplots selects a single slice of the stack. It would be nice to have the option to be able to select one entire stack. 

2. Clicking on elements in the stacked barplot when hovermode is "x-unified" makes the selection bug out. Makes selection very erratic and strange. Just try clicking around on different elements. Sometimes it selects the wrong slice of the stack. Sometimes it doesn't select. Visuals go weird too. 

3. If you remove the hovermode argument, then click on an element on the top bar chart, and then another element on the bottom bar chart, the selection of the top element is still VISUALLY there but the selection dictionary corresponds to the bottom bar chart only. I really wish selection dictionary had awareness of which subplot it was accessing. 

4. In an absolutely ideal world, I would like an option for the user to be able to click on a data element so that all traces with the same x value become selected, along with hovermode to behave as expected when in "x" or "x unified". 

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-8766)
```Python
import pandas as pd
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
import plotly.graph_objects as go

import streamlit as st

df = pd.DataFrame({
        "id": ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"],
        "data1": [124, 12, 473, 219, 122],
        "stack1": [234, 346, 124, 743, 586],
        "stack2": [586, 24, 346, 235, 584],
        "stack3": [456, 34, 243, 745, 423]
    })

    st.dataframe(df)

    fig = make_subplots(rows = 3, cols = 1, shared_xaxes = True)

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Bar(
            x = df.id,
            y = df.data1
        ),
        row = 1,
        col = 1
    )


    bars = []
    for _, row in df.iterrows():
        for i in [1, 2, 3]:
            bars.append(
                go.Bar(
                    x = [row.id],
                    y = [row[f"stack{i}"]]
                )
            )

    fig.add_traces(bars, rows = 2, cols = 1)
    fig.update_layout(hovermode = "x unified",
                      barmode = 'stack')

    s = st.plotly_chart(fig, on_select = "rerun")

    st.json(s)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

issues.title: st.image, st.video, and st.audio should build image, video, and audio headers (respectively) for raw numpy array data
issues.body:
### Problem

Many users want to use Streamlit to programmatically generate images and videos.

Right now we accept numpy arrays as valid data with `st.video` and `st.image`, but we require that the user do the work in their own script of creating the proper headers for those images.  (See streamlit discussion question [Is it possible to embed a tiff/array video with Streamlit?](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/is-it-possible-to-embed-a-tiff-array-video-with-streamlit/1393).

To the extent that is reasonable, we should support automatically creating the appropriate headers for a handful of common formats: JPG, PNG (already expliciltly named), TIFF (as an addition), etc.

Some user research would be useful to see which formats people might benefit from.

### Solution

**MVP:**  (First thought) -- implement another argument in `st.image` and `st.video` like "add_headers" (boolean).

**Possible additions:**  Autodetect the file type based on its contents and add headers appropriately?  This seems like an improbable stretch since filetype detection generally revolves around reading the headers.

**Preferred solution:**  Explicitly support adding headers to specific image and video formats.  TIFF, JPG, PNG, etc.  So the streamlit api would become something like this:

    st.image(image=some_array, format="JPG", add_headers=True)

    st.video(data=some_array, format="TIFF", add_headers=True)

### Additional context

The same should be done for `st.audio` (and there are #todo statements in the code to that effect); this will be opened as a separate issue since the headers for audio wouldn't overlap with image and video headers.

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

**If you'd like the Streamlit team to prioritize this feature request, please use the 👍 (thumbs up emoji) reaction in response to the initial post.**

issues.title: Allow multiple value paste to st.multiselect
Feature: st.scatterplot_matrix_chart — scatterplot matrix (SPLOM) navigation with excentric labeling and lasso query layers
issues.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

## Summary

Add `st.scatterplot_matrix_chart`, a native chart command for exploring multivariate/high-dimensional tabular data through a scatterplot matrix (SPLOM). It adds animated "rolling" navigation between attribute pairs, excentric labeling for dense regions, and persistent lasso-based query layers that let you track a subset of rows across different attribute views.

## Why?

Data scientists frequently need to explore relationships across many numeric columns at once. A standard SPLOM grid gives a good overview, but it's hard to inspect any one pair in detail, label individual points in dense clusters, or keep track of the same subset of rows as you move between attribute pairs. This is a longstanding, well-studied interaction pattern in the information-visualization literature, and I think it's a good fit for Streamlit's data-science audience:

- I first built a version of this technique in a data visualization course project over a decade ago (~2012), based on:
  - Pierre Dragicevic (@dragice) et al., "Rolling the Dice: Multidimensional Visual Exploration using Scatterplot Matrix Navigation"
  - Jean-Daniel Fekete (@jdfekete) and Catherine Plaisant, "Excentric Labeling: Dynamic Neighborhood Labeling for Data Visualization"
  - My original project instructions/write-up from that time (personal notes, kept private)
- A few years ago, a tech company I was working with asked me to use Streamlit, and separately took an interest in this old scatterplot project of mine. Looking back, I read that as an implicit nudge toward combining the two — bringing this navigation technique into Streamlit itself, rather than leaving it as a standalone tool.

Revisiting both experiences, I think this technique deserves a first-class home in Streamlit rather than living on as scattered internal/academic tools.

## How?

I generalized the navigation technique above into a self-contained, WebGL-rendered element and exposed it as a new command, `st.scatterplot_matrix_chart`:

- A small scatterplot cell for every pair of chosen numeric columns, plus one large "detail" plot.
- Left-click a cell to jump to it; right-click (or arrow keys) to "roll" to it through an animated transition across intermediate cells.
- Hover the large plot for an excentric label lens (labels fan out around the cursor in dense regions).
- Up to 8 independent, colored query layers: lasso-select points in the large plot to build a persistent subset, then navigate to other attribute pairs to see how that same subset behaves elsewhere.
- Selections are returned to Python via `on_select="rerun"` as row indices, so they can drive the rest of the app.

A full implementation (backend + frontend + tests) is up for review at #16059.

## Additional Context

- Original ~2012 project instructions (background/inspiration, written by me as a student at the time — personal notes, kept private)
- Academic references: Dragicevic et al., "Rolling the Dice: Multidimensional Visual Exploration using Scatterplot Matrix Navigation"; Fekete & Plaisant, "Excentric Labeling: Dynamic Neighborhood Labeling for Data Visualization"
- Implementation PR: #16059

issues.title: st.selectbox Escape no longer clears the typed search query since 1.59.0 (stale query left in the input)
issues.body:
### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Since 1.59.0 (the `BaseWeb` → react-aria `ComboBox` migration, #15438), pressing
`Escape` while searching in a value-selected `st.selectbox` no longer discards the
typed query. The dropdown closes and the committed value is (correctly) preserved,
but the half-typed query stays visible in the input, so the box shows a query that
does not match the actual value. In 1.58.0, `Escape` cleared the query and
restored the committed value.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

FRUITS = ["Apple", "Apricot", "Banana", "Cherry", "Grape", "Mango", "Peach", "Pear"]
v = st.selectbox("Fruit", FRUITS, index=2)  # Banana pre-selected
st.write("value:", v)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above (value is `Banana`).
2. Click the selectbox and type `gr`.
3. Press `Escape`.
4. Look at what the input shows vs. the committed value.
5. (Control) Repeat steps 2–3 but click elsewhere instead of pressing Escape.

### Expected Behavior

`Escape` discards the query and restores the committed value in the input (as in
1.58.0): after Escape the box shows `Banana` again and `value` is still `Banana`.

### Current Behavior

- The dropdown closes and the committed value stays `Banana` (good — no accidental
  commit), **but the input still shows the stale query** (`gr`; on raw 1.59.0 the
  original append bug makes it `Bananagr`).
- Typing again without blurring appends to the stale query (e.g. `gr` + `ap` → `grap`).
- The control case (click away / blur) **does** correctly restore `Banana`, so only
  the Escape path is affected.

(Screenshots attached: `EVIDENCE_branch_gap2_after_escape.png` shows the stale
`gr` after Escape on 1.59.0+; `EVIDENCE_v1_58_0_gap2_after_escape.png` shows the
input restored on 1.58.0.)

### Is this a regression?
- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Confirmed via bisect against official PyPI wheels: after typing `gr` and pressing
Escape, the input is cleared/restored on **1.58.0** (BaseWeb `Select`) but retains
`gr` / `Bananagr` on **1.59.0** (react-aria `ComboBox`). Identical in Chromium and
WebKit. Introduced by #15438.

### Debug info
- Streamlit version: 1.59.0 (introduced); still present in current 1.59.x / dev builds
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Linux (browser-independent)
- Browser: Chromium and WebKit (both affected)

### Additional Information

- Related migration PR: #15438 (Remove `BaseWeb` for `selectbox`).
- Discovered during QA of #15996 (which fixes the separate type-to-search append
  bug #15985). This Escape regression is independent of that fix.
- Likely fix: on `Escape` for a non-clearable selectbox, reset `inputValue` to the
  committed label and clear the active-filter state (mirroring the existing
  blur-restore path). Clearable (`index=None`) selectboxes already clear to `None`
  on Escape via a separate code path and are not affected.

Hi,
I really enjoy using streamlit to deploy all sorts of applications, but I consistently run into an issue that I have started to be able to reproduce, but is very difficult to understand. I have seen people discuss this issue before, but I haven't been able to find a version of streamlit that fixes the issue. Essentially, the application seems to refresh on me after a certain period of time. Here is one example.

https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/i-get-kicked-out-of-my-app-at-random-times/28316

### Reproducible Code Example

N/A

### Steps To Reproduce

Deploy a long running application to a non streamlit cloud environment using docker.

### Expected Behavior

I expect the _stcore/health to not throw an exception, seemingly causing my application to refresh.

### Current Behavior

Essentially, the gist of the issue is that when I deploy this using Docker to a cloud environment (AWS/Azure), I find the call made to the /_stcore/health endpoint **fails to parse on the frontend**. The endpoint produces a response with the text "ok", but further into the code, it seems the axios library tries to parse this response as json using JSON.parse(). However, this results in an error, which seems to refresh the page. I don't know how often the health endpoint is called, but it seems like it happens approximately every 5 minutes, so for long running processes, these don't end up finishing.

I tried to trace the bug through the streamlit codebase and found that perhaps you are returning the text "ok" on line 519 in the function labeled "is_ready_for_browser_connection". This seems to get returned to the UI, likely through in the "HealthHandler" class on line 148 in the get function. I suspect self.write() will converts dictionaries to json and text is just returned as text through the API. However, perhaps returning the dictionary {"status": "ok"} might fix the issue. 

From the code and stacktrace, it seems there is a websocket that attempts to close, and before closing, it pings the server (the health check), however, the health check indicates it is "ok" and should keep the websocket open. However, an exception occurs during the parsing of the health check, so the connection is closed and perhaps that is when the page refreshes.

Importantly, this does not seem to happen for me in the Streamlit Cloud nor locally, likely because neither seem to call the health check endpoint. The streamlit cloud seems to call the app/status endpoint and locally, no health checks are performed.

issues.body:
### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When an `st.popover` is used inside an `st.dialog`, the popover opens but its body
is rendered underneath the dialog's interaction layer. Widgets inside the popover
(e.g. a `selectbox`) cannot be interacted with, and clicking them lands on the
dialog's dismissable overlay — which can close the dialog. This is a regression
from the migration of `st.dialog` to React Aria (#15327); it worked in 1.58.0.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st


@st.dialog("My dialog")
def show_dialog():
    st.write("dialog content")
    with st.popover("Open popover"):
        fruit = st.selectbox("Fruit", ["Apple", "Banana", "Cherry"])
        st.write(f"picked: {fruit}")


if st.button("Open dialog"):
    show_dialog()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and click **Open dialog**.
2. Inside the dialog, click **Open popover** (the popover body appears).
3. Try to open the popover's `selectbox` dropdown and pick an option.
4. The dropdown does not open; clicking in the popover body instead hits the
   dialog overlay (and can dismiss the dialog).

### Expected Behavior

The popover body renders above the dialog and its widgets are fully interactive:
opening the `selectbox`, picking an option, and having the value commit —
dismissing neither the popover nor the dialog. (This is how it behaved in 1.58.0.)

### Current Behavior

The popover body is occluded by the dialog. The in-popover widget is not
interactable, and interacting with it can close the dialog.

Objective evidence (Playwright, both Chromium and WebKit): hit-testing the
in-popover selectbox at its own center with `document.elementFromPoint` returns
the dialog rather than the widget, and the dropdown cannot be opened even with a
forced click:

```
selectbox_hit = { topTestId: "stDialog", inBody: false, inDialog: true }
dropdown_opened = false
```

Root cause: the popover body is portalled to `document.body` (outside the dialog's
DOM subtree), while `st.dialog` is now a React Aria (`data-rac`) overlay that
establishes its own stacking/overlay layer that paints and hit-tests above the
portalled popover body. Control: a BaseWeb overlay opened from a widget placed
**directly** in the dialog (e.g. a `multiselect` in the dialog) renders correctly
above the dialog, so the dialog does not occlude all portalled overlays — only the
popover body at the `popup` z-tier.

### Is this a regression?
- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Confirmed via `git bisect` (probe: is the in-popover selectbox usable above the
dialog?):

| Commit | Description | Result |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| tag `1.58.0` (`209ad55c`) | 1.58.0 release (does not contain #15327) | PASS |
| `590deca9` | parent of #15327 | PASS |
| **`a7200715` (#15327)** | **Remove `BaseWeb` for `Dialog` (React Aria migration)** | **FAIL (first bad commit)** |
| `d65a3aae` (#15339) | Remove BaseWeb for Popover (floating-ui) | FAIL (not the cause) |
| current `develop` | — | FAIL |

#15327 shipped in 1.59.0 and is not in 1.58.0, which is why 1.58.0 works and
1.59.0+ is broken. This is independent of the `st.popover` floating-ui migration
(#15339). There is a prior related fix, #15876 "Fix React Aria dialog overlay
stacking", which does not cover this popover-in-dialog case.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: `develop` (reproduces on 1.59.0 and later; first broken in #15327)
- Python version: 3.12.3
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chromium and WebKit (both affected)

### Additional Information

- Scope: only the combination **popover inside a dialog** is affected. Standalone
  popovers, and widgets placed directly in a dialog, work correctly.
- Suggested direction for a fix: render/portal the popover body into the dialog's
  overlay/stacking context when it is opened inside a dialog, or raise the popover
  body to a tier that clears the React Aria dialog overlay (mirroring how direct
  BaseWeb overlays clear it via the `basewebOverlay` tier).
- Found during QA of PR #15961 (which fixes the separate #15959 popover-overlay
  stacking/dismissal issues). This popover-in-dialog gap is not caused by, and is
  out of scope for, that PR.

issues.title: Parent-page scroll resets after closing `st.dialog` opened from a custom component (regression since 1.41.0, worsened at 1.53.0)
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

### Summary

When a `@st.dialog` is opened from a Streamlit custom component (e.g. via
`Streamlit.setComponentValue(...)` on user interaction) and then closed, the main content
area's scroll position — `section[data-testid="stMain"]` in the parent DOM — is reset. This
is a regression that was introduced in Streamlit 1.41.0 and was made strictly worse in
1.53.0.

### Bisect (using streamlit-pdf-viewer as the test vehicle)

| streamlit-pdf-viewer | Streamlit | Browser  | scrollTop 200 → | Verdict              |
|----------------------|-----------|----------|-----------------|----------------------|
| 0.0.25               | 1.40.2    | both     | 200             | ok                   |
| 0.0.25               | 1.47.0    | both     | 200             | ok *(reporter's env)*|
| 0.0.25               | **1.52.0**| firefox  | 200             | **ok**               |
| 0.0.25               | **1.53.0**| firefox  | 0               | **regression**       |
| 0.0.25               | 1.53.0    | chromium | 0               | regression           |
| 0.0.25               | 1.56.0    | both     | 0               | broken               |
| 0.0.26+              | 1.40.2    | both     | 200             | ok                   |
| **0.0.26+**          | **1.41.0**| firefox  | 0               | **regression**       |
| 0.0.26+              | 1.41.0    | chromium | ~174            | minor shift          |
| 0.0.26+              | 1.56.0    | firefox  | 0               | broken               |

Two distinct regressions are visible:

1. **1.40.2 → 1.41.0** — Firefox-only reset. Only triggers when the custom component's DOM
   has a `.scrolling-container` wrapper plus an absolutely-positioned sibling (a common shape
   for components with overlay controls). A minimal-DOM component escapes it.
2. **1.52.0 → 1.53.0** — reset on **both** browsers, regardless of DOM shape. Any custom
   component that triggers a rerun via `st.dialog` close hits this.

After 1.53.0, there is no version of the downstream component that avoids the bug.




### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
from streamlit_pdf_viewer import pdf_viewer  # pip install streamlit-pdf-viewer==0.0.26


@st.dialog("popup")
def show_popup():
    st.text("Close me and observe the page scroll reset.")


with open("resources/test.pdf", "rb") as f:
    content = f.read()

annotations = [
    {"page": 1, "x": 100, "y": 100, "height": 22, "width": 30, "color": "blue"},
    {"page": 1, "x": 150, "y": 120, "height": 22, "width": 30, "color": "green"},
    {"page": 2, "x": 180, "y": 130, "height": 22, "width": 30, "color": "purple"},
    {"page": 2, "x": 220, "y": 155, "height": 22, "width": 30, "color": "red"},
]

clicked = pdf_viewer(content, width=800, annotations=annotations)
if clicked:
    show_popup()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Steps:

1. Run the app on Streamlit 1.53.0+.
2. Scroll the main page down to bring page 2 annotations into view.
3. Click any annotation. A `st.dialog` opens.
4. Close the dialog (X button or Escape).
5. Observe the main content scrolls back to the top.

Same steps on Streamlit 1.40.2 preserve the scroll position.

### Expected Behavior

After the dialog closes, the main content area (`section[data-testid="stMain"]`) should
retain the scroll position it had when the dialog was opened. In our Playwright harness:
scroll before click = scroll after dialog close (delta ≈ 0). This is exactly what happens
on Streamlit ≤ 1.40.2 on both Chromium and Firefox.

### Current Behavior

On Streamlit ≥ 1.41.0 the scroll position is disturbed after the dialog closes:

- **1.41.0 – 1.52.x, Firefox, with a custom component whose DOM has a `.scrolling-container`
  wrapper + overlay controls** — `stMain.scrollTop` is reset to `0` (full jump to top).
- **1.41.0 – 1.52.x, Chromium** — `stMain.scrollTop` shifts by ~20–30 px (minor but
  consistently wrong direction).
- **1.41.0 – 1.52.x, Firefox, with a minimal-DOM custom component (e.g. streamlit-pdf-viewer
  v0.0.25)** — scroll is preserved; the bug does not manifest.
- **≥ 1.53.0, both browsers, any custom-component DOM shape** — `stMain.scrollTop` is reset
  to `0`. No version of the downstream component escapes it.

Numeric evidence (same harness, `scrollTop=200` before the click):

| Streamlit | Component DOM shape | Browser  | `stMain.scrollTop` after close |
|-----------|---------------------|----------|--------------------------------|
| 1.40.2    | any                 | both     | 200 (expected)                 |
| 1.41.1    | v0.0.26 (wrapper)   | firefox  | **0**                          |
| 1.41.1    | v0.0.26 (wrapper)   | chromium | 174                            |
| 1.41.1    | v0.0.25 (minimal)   | both     | 200 (expected)                 |
| 1.53.0    | v0.0.25 (minimal)   | firefox  | **0**                          |
| 1.53.0    | v0.0.25 (minimal)   | chromium | **0**                          |
| 1.56.0    | any                 | both     | **0**                          |

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

### Evidence this is not a component-side problem

We instrumented the component's Vue hooks (`onMounted`, `onUnmounted`) and its resize /
render entry point (`handleResize`) with `console.log`. Through the entire dialog lifecycle
(click → dialog open → dialog close → scroll reset), **no component code runs**. The scroll
reset is observed with zero in-iframe JavaScript activity. We also experimentally removed
the ResizeObserver, all Vue watchers, and even the `.scrolling-container` wrapper — the
reset still happens on Firefox with Streamlit 1.41+ and on all browsers with 1.53+.

This places the root cause in Streamlit's host-page logic during script rerun, outside the
reach of any custom component.

### Suspected origin (1.41.0)

This commit was flagged by @t29mato on the downstream thread as the probable source of the
1.41.0 regression:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/commit/96241e135e0a5597ff975c232fa2c44b45e71358

It changed iframe handling for custom components. The 1.52 → 1.53 all-browser regression
would require a separate bisect by Streamlit maintainers.

### Environment

- Host: macOS 25.4 (darwin-arm64), Python 3.12
- Firefox 146.0.1, Chrome-for-Testing 145.0.7632.6 (both via Playwright 1.58 headless)
- streamlit-pdf-viewer 0.0.25 and 0.0.26 (both reproduce with Streamlit 1.53.0+)



### Additional Information

### Related issues 

I searched existing `streamlit/streamlit` issues with multiple term combinations
(`scroll reset dialog custom component`, `iframe scroll position rerun`,
`page scroll reset rerun`, `custom component iframe rerun`,
`main page scroll top st.dialog component`, `scroll position lost after rerun`) and did
not find a duplicate. The closest adjacent issues are:

- #10756 (closed): *Custom components unmount and reload on switch_page* — same theme of
  iframe lifecycle surprises on rerun/navigation, different trigger (switch_page rather
  than dialog close).
- #14505 (open PR): *fix: reset dialog scroll position to top when reopened* — fixes the
  **dialog's internal** scroll, not the parent page scroll. Different scroll surface.
- #10701 (open): *Preserve Selection, Sorting and Scrolling Position in st.dataframe* —
  widget-internal scroll preservation, unrelated mechanism.

If this turns out to be a duplicate of an issue I missed, happy to consolidate.

### Links

- Downstream issue (full history, repro videos, user-reported workaround): https://github.com/lfoppiano/streamlit-pdf-viewer/issues/107

issues.title: Consider adding a changelog to track version history
issues.body:
## Feature Request

### Summary
A `CHANGELOG.md` file would help users understand what changed between versions and make upgrade decisions easier.

### Motivation
When upgrading dependencies, developers need to know:
- What bugs were fixed
- What new features were added
- Whether there are any breaking changes

### Suggested Format
Follow the [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com) convention:

```markdown
# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

## [1.2.0] - 2024-01-15
### Added
- New feature X
### Fixed  
- Bug with Y under Z conditions
### Changed
- Behaviour of Z is now more consistent
```

### Additional Context
This is purely a documentation change with no code impact.

issues.title: Input Widgets defined inside Forms Experiencing Significant Lag (Text/Number Inputs)
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When interacting with text and number input widgets inside forms, there is a noticeable delay between clicking into the field and the appearance of the cursor. Additionally, when typing, the text takes a few seconds to appear, creating significant lag. This becomes especially problematic when correcting mistakes, as deleting and rewriting text further exacerbates the delay. The responsiveness of these widgets should be improved.




### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-9512)

```Python
import os
import streamlit as st
import time
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from copy import deepcopy
import random

data_points = {}
references = {}
existing_entries = {}

CATEGORIES = ['cat1', 'cat2', 'cat3']
METRICS = ['metric1', 'metric2', 'metric3', 'metric4', 'metric5', 'metric6', 'metric7', 'metric8', 'metric9', 'metric10', 'metric11', 'metric12', 'metric13']
IMPACTS = ['impact1', 'impact2', 'impact3', 'impact4', 'impact5', 'impact6', 'impact7', 'impact8', 'impact9', 'impact10', 'impact11', 'impact12', 'impact13']
METRIC_ALIASES = {'metric1': 'm1', 'metric2': 'm2', 'metric3': 'm3', 'metric4': 'm4', 'metric5': 'm5', 'metric6': 'm6', 'metric7': 'm7', 'metric8': 'm8', 'metric9': 'm9', 'metric10': 'm10', 'metric11': 'm11', 'metric12': 'm12', 'metric13': 'm13'}
shift_types = ['percent', 'percent point']
shift_evolutions = ['constant', 'fade', 'rise']

for impact_name in IMPACTS:
    data_points[impact_name] = {
        metric: {
            category: {
                'shift_value': round(random.uniform(-1.0, 1.0), 3),
                'shift_type': random.choice(shift_types),
                'shift_evolution': random.choice(shift_evolutions),
                'shift_start': random.randint(0, 1000),
                'shift_end': random.randint(0, 1000),
                'version_start_conversion_week': '2023-W01',
                'version_end_conversion_week': '2023-W52',
                'version_start_delivery_week': '2023-W01',
                'version_end_delivery_week': '2023-W52'
            } for category in CATEGORIES
        } for metric in METRICS
    }

print(data_points)

def apply_references(entry_details, reference, metric):
    if reference != 'Define individually':
        for category in CATEGORIES:
            entry_details[metric][category] = deepcopy(entry_details[metric][reference])
    return entry_details

st.sidebar.button("test_widgets")

# Text input for creating a new entry
tab_side_test = st.sidebar
tab_side_test.text_input(
    label='Create New Entry',
    value='',
    placeholder='New Entry',
    key='new_entry'
)

# Create a form for assumptions
assumptions_form = tab_side_test.form('assumptions_form')

# Tabs for existing data points if available
if len(data_points.keys()):
    tabs_for_entries = assumptions_form.tabs(list(data_points.keys()))
else:
    tabs_for_entries = []

# Iterate over each tab (data point) to process details
for tab_idx, tab in enumerate(tabs_for_entries):
    entry_name = list(data_points.keys())[tab_idx]
    entry_details = data_points[entry_name]
    references[entry_name] = {}

    # entry_details['comment'] = tab.text_input(
    #     label=f'Comment:',
    #     value=entry_details['comment'],
    #     key=f'{entry_name}_comment'
    # )

    # Tabs for metrics inside each data point
    metric_tabs = tab.tabs(list(METRIC_ALIASES.values()))
    for metric_idx, metric_tab in enumerate(metric_tabs):
        metric = METRICS[metric_idx]
        metric_alias = list(METRIC_ALIASES.values())[metric_idx]

        # Drop-down for category definition
        references[entry_name][metric] = metric_tab.selectbox(
            'Category Definition',
            options=['Define individually'] + [f"Apply {category} to all" for category in CATEGORIES],
            index=0,
            key=f'category_{entry_name}_{metric_alias}'
        ).replace('Apply ', '').replace(' to all', '')

        # Iterate over categories
        category_tabs = metric_tab.tabs(CATEGORIES)
        for category_idx, category_tab in enumerate(category_tabs):
            category = CATEGORIES[category_idx]
            current_assumptions = deepcopy(entry_details[metric][category])

            # Numeric input for percentage value
            entry_details[metric][category]['shift_value'] = category_tab.number_input(
                label=f'Value % (e.g., 1.5%)',
                min_value=-1.000, max_value=1.000,
                step=1e-3,
                value=min(float(current_assumptions['shift_value']), 1.000),
                format="%.3f",
                key=f'{entry_name}_{metric}_{category}_shift_value'
            )

            # Drop-down for shift type
            entry_details[metric][category]['shift_type'] = category_tab.selectbox(
                'Shift Type',
                index=shift_types.index(current_assumptions['shift_type']),
                options=shift_types,
                format_func=lambda x: f'{x.capitalize()} of baseline' if x == 'percent' else x.capitalize(),
                key=f'{entry_name}_{metric}_{category}_shift_type'
            )

            # Drop-down for shift evolution
            entry_details[metric][category]['shift_evolution'] = category_tab.selectbox(
                'Shift Evolution',
                index=shift_evolutions.index(current_assumptions['shift_evolution']),
                options=shift_evolutions,
                format_func=lambda x: x.capitalize(),
                key=f'{entry_name}_{metric}_{category}_shift_evolution'
            )

            # Inputs for start and end values
            col1, col2 = category_tab.columns([1, 1])
            entry_details[metric][category]['shift_start'] = col1.number_input(
                label=f'Start Value:',
                min_value=0, max_value=1000,
                value=min(current_assumptions['shift_start'], 1000),
                step=1,
                key=f'{entry_name}_{metric}_{category}_shift_start'
            )
            entry_details[metric][category]['shift_end'] = col2.number_input(
                label=f'End Value:',
                min_value=0, max_value=1000,
                value=min(current_assumptions['shift_end'], 1000),
                step=1,
                key=f'{entry_name}_{metric}_{category}_shift_end'
            )

            # Additional fields for versioning
            col1.text_input(
                label=f'From Week:',
                value=current_assumptions['version_start_conversion_week'],
                key=f'{entry_name}_{metric}_{category}_version_start'
            )
            col2.text_input(
                label=f'To Week:',
                value=current_assumptions['version_end_conversion_week'],
                key=f'{entry_name}_{metric}_{category}_version_end'
            )

        # Apply category references
        entry_details = apply_references(entry_details, references[entry_name][metric], metric)

# Form submission button
assumptions_form.form_submit_button("Submit")

```

issues.title: st.data_editor column order not respected when column name type is not str
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I want to make an editable dataframe using `st.data_editor`. My dataframe has int column names, in descending order. For my application, it is important that this order is respected.

However, when I define the `column_config` argument, the order gets flipped into ascending order.

I have also tried specifying `column_order`, but this results in an error `TypeError: bad argument type for built-in operation` (this is because the column names are not str type but they are expected as such)
```python
df = st.data_editor(
    df,
    column_order=df.columns,
    column_config={
            col: st.column_config.TextColumn(
                col,
            )
            for col in df.columns
        },
)
```



### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-8473)

```Python

issues.title: Integrate VegaFusion to move Altair and Vega-Lite transforms out of the browser
issues.body:
### Problem
The charts generated by Altair and the Streamlit `st.line_chart`, `st.area_chart`, and `st.bar_chart` functions are built on Vega-Lite. One of the awesome things about Vega-Lite is that it incorporates data transformations (like histogram binning and aggregation) into the chart specifications.  This is really powerful when quickly iterating on statistical charts, but there's a downside. By default, the entire dataset must be sent to the browser.  For example, if you build a 10-bin histogram from a dataset with 1 million rows and 10 columns, all of the rows and columns are transferred to the browser even though only two columns (bin edges and bin counts) and 10 rows (one per bar) are needed to actually render the bars of the histogram.

As I understand it, this situation is somewhat less detrimental to Streamlit as the inline datasets are extracted and shipped to the browser in Arrow format, but it still becomes a poor experience as datasets get larger.

### Solution
I'm the maintainer of [VegaFusion](https://vegafusion.io/), which is an [open source](https://github.com/hex-inc/vegafusion) library designed to solve this problem by analyzing the Vega specifications generated by Vega-Lite and automatically moving data transformations to the Python kernel. 

VegaFusion already provides a few forms of integration with Altair for use in Jupyter contexts, and with a relatively modest amount of effort I expect we could work out a way for Streamlit to offer VegaFusion support as well.

#### MVP
As an MVP, I'd propose adding an optional `vegafusion=False` kwarg to `st.altair_chart`. When `True`, VegaFusion would be imported and used to pre-apply data aggregations in Python before the resulting Vega spec is transferred to the browser for rendering by the Vega JavaScript library.

In the case of a 10-bin histogram on a dataset with 1 millions rows and 10 columns, this would result in sending a 2-column 10-row dataset to the browser, alongside the transformed Vega specification.

**Possible additions:** Support `st.line_chart`, `st.area_chart`, and `st.bar_chart` as well.

### Additional context
If the Streamlit team is interested in pursuing this integration, I'd be happy to take a closer look at the Streamlit code base and make some suggestions for how the integration could work.

My initial expectation is that it would work similarly to the VegaFusion Mime Renderer ([docs](https://vegafusion.io/mime_renderer.html), [YouTube overview](https://youtu.be/kEFD5syneq0))

issues.title: Make Streamlit easy to deploy as a standalone executable (e.g. PyInstaller, Electron)
issues.body:
Is there a future for electron deployment of streamlit?
___

```
streamlit electron app.py
```

Streamlits target demographic (seemingly the Data Science / ML / AI community) often has apps which consume *a lot* of resources. RAM for loading data used by the app can be quite a bit- pair this with `st.cache` and in a few hours/days time your streamlit app needs to be killed / controlled / scaled. That is fine (and good for AWS' profit), but why not be able to distribute the app across its users so they can run it on their machine (and use their resources).  This is easy enough if your streamlit users are capable of running `streamlit run ..` in their terminal. However, *who are the users of these apps*? Oftentimes they will be other engineers / programmers sure - but I think a substantial chunk of the user-base of streamlit apps is a non-technical audience. We send links to streamlit apps to management / non-technical members of the organization *constantly* I would much rather send them an `S3` link to download an electron app and not worry about scaling up the AWS instance(s) hosting it. Sure, they have to have python and some dependencies - but those are relatively easy to control by IT and can often involve little user work. Furthermore, we could maybe have a future where the `streamlit build electon` command could bundle dependencies? I am not sure - but it seems possible.


Streamlit seems well-positioned for this to be possible. It is trivial to "fake it". Just do something like this to get an *MVP*. 

```python
import streamlit as lit  # you guys really dropped the ball on this not being the suggested import
# idk - maybe it is too z00mer.

def main():
    lit.sidebar.title("Electron")
    lit.sidebar.info("The Electron Slide...")
    lit.sidebar.slider('How "nativive"?', 0, 100, 50)
    lit.title("Streamlit in `Electron`")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Run it,

```
streamlit run app.py
```

Take the starter electron app from [here](https://github.com/electron/electron-quick-start). and change literally 1 line (:16)

```
mainWindow.loadURL('http://localhost:8501/')  // or wherever you served
```

And...

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8339189/79810221-8cb46680-8340-11ea-80a4-8d112f3b4611.png)

___
I am just opening this issue to see if you guys (and the community) think this has any legs. I am not sure of the specifics. For example,

```
streamlit (electron|run_electron) app.py  # for local testing and development
streamlit build -t electron app.py <name>  # for building and bundling dependencies
# to a downloadable launcher? 
...
```

Could there be electron-specific component implementations (so sidebar could be a native window), or tab support, keyboard shortcuts, etc? Could session state be saved to disk and loaded on app start to preserve state? Or maybe this is all a terrible idea... (also if there is another discussion of this already somewhere else (I couldn't find one) lmk and this can just be closed)

---
